source: Tamil text, transliteration, G. U. Pope's verse translation (1886) and the Drew/Lazarus prose translation (1840/1885), all public domain; compiled from github.com/tk120404/thirukkural

kurals.translit: Akara Mudhala Ezhuththellaam Aadhi / Pakavan Mudhatre Ulaku
kurals.pope: A, as its first of letters, every speech maintains; The "Primal Deity" is first through all the world's domains
kurals.drew: As the letter A is the first of all letters, so the eternal God is first in the world

kurals.translit: Katradhanaal Aaya Payanenkol Vaalarivan / Natraal Thozhaaar Enin
kurals.pope: No fruit have men of all their studied lore, Save they the 'Purely Wise One's' feet adore
kurals.drew: What Profit have those derived from learning, who worship not the good feet of Him who is possessed of pure knowledge ?

kurals.translit: Malarmisai Ekinaan Maanati Serndhaar / Nilamisai Neetuvaazh Vaar
kurals.pope: His feet, 'Who o'er the full-blown flower hath past,' who gainIn bliss long time shall dwell above this earthly plain
kurals.drew: They who are united to the glorious feet of Him who passes swiftly over the flower of the mind, shall flourish long above all worlds

kurals.translit: Ventudhal Ventaamai Ilaanati Serndhaarkku / Yaantum Itumpai Ila
kurals.pope: His foot, 'Whom want affects not, irks not grief,' who gainShall not, through every time, of any woes complain
kurals.drew: To those who meditate the feet of Him who is void of desire or aversion, evil shall never come

kurals.translit: Irulser Iruvinaiyum Seraa Iraivan / Porulser Pukazhpurindhaar Maattu
kurals.pope: The men, who on the 'King's' true praised delight to dwell, Affects not them the fruit of deeds done ill or well
kurals.drew: The two-fold deeds that spring from darkness shall not adhere to those who delight in the true praise of God

kurals.translit: Porivaayil Aindhaviththaan Poidheer Ozhukka / Nerinindraar Neetuvaazh Vaar
kurals.pope: Long live they blest, who 've stood in path from falsehood freed; His, 'Who quenched lusts that from the sense-gates five proceed'
kurals.drew: Those shall long proposer who abide in the faultless way of Him who has destroyed the five desires of the senses

kurals.translit: Thanakkuvamai Illaadhaan Thaalserndhaark Kallaal / Manakkavalai Maatral Aridhu
kurals.pope: Unless His foot, 'to Whom none can compare,' men gain,'Tis hard for mind to find relief from anxious pain
kurals.drew: Anxiety of mind cannot be removed, except from those who are united to the feet of Him who is incomparable

kurals.translit: Aravaazhi Andhanan Thaalserndhaark Kallaal / Piravaazhi Neendhal Aridhu
kurals.pope: Unless His feet 'the Sea of Good, the Fair and Bountiful,' men gain,'Tis hard the further bank of being's changeful sea to attain
kurals.drew: None can swim the sea of vice, but those who are united to the feet of that gracious Being who is a sea of virtue

kurals.translit: Kolil Poriyin Kunamilave Enkunaththaan / Thaalai Vanangaath Thalai
kurals.pope: Before His foot, 'the Eight-fold Excellence,' with unbent head, Who stands, like palsied sense, is to all living functions dead
kurals.drew: The head that worships not the feet of Him who is possessed of eight attributes, is as useless as a sense without the power of sensation

kurals.translit: Piravip Perungatal Neendhuvar Neendhaar / Iraivan Atiseraa Thaar
kurals.pope: They swim the sea of births, the 'Monarch's' foot who gain; None others reach the shore of being's mighty main
kurals.drew: None can swim the great sea of births but those who are united to the feet of God

kurals.translit: Vaannindru Ulakam Vazhangi Varudhalaal / Thaanamizhdham Endrunarar Paatru
kurals.pope: The world its course maintains through life that rain unfailing gives; Thus rain is known the true ambrosial food of all that lives
kurals.drew: By the continuance of rain the world is preserved in existence; it is therefore worthy to be called ambrosia

kurals.translit: Thuppaarkkuth Thuppaaya Thuppaakkith Thuppaarkkuth / Thuppaaya Thooum Mazhai
kurals.pope: The rain makes pleasant food for eaters rise; As food itself, thirst-quenching draught supplies
kurals.drew: Rain produces good food, and is itself food

kurals.translit: Vinindru Poippin Virineer Viyanulakaththu / Ulnindru Utatrum Pasi
kurals.pope: If clouds, that promised rain, deceive, and in the sky remain, Famine, sore torment, stalks o'er earth's vast ocean-girdled plain
kurals.drew: If the cloud, withholding rain, deceive (our hopes) hunger will long distress the sea-girt spacious world

kurals.translit: Erin Uzhaaar Uzhavar Puyalennum / Vaari Valangundrik Kaal
kurals.pope: If clouds their wealth of waters fail on earth to pour, The ploughers plough with oxen's sturdy team no more
kurals.drew: If the abundance of wealth imparting rain diminish, the labour of the plough must cease

kurals.translit: Ketuppadhooum Kettaarkkuch Chaarvaaimar Raange / Etuppadhooum Ellaam Mazhai
kurals.pope: 'Tis rain works all: it ruin spreads, then timely aid supplies; As, in the happy days before, it bids the ruined rise
kurals.drew: Rain by its absence ruins men; and by its existence restores them to fortune

kurals.translit: Visumpin Thuliveezhin Allaalmar Raange / Pasumpul Thalaikaanpu Aridhu
kurals.pope: If from the clouds no drops of rain are shed'Tis rare to see green herb lift up its head
kurals.drew: If no drop falls from the clouds, not even the green blade of grass will be seen

kurals.translit: Netungatalum Thanneermai Kundrum Thatindhezhili / Thaannalkaa Thaaki Vitin
kurals.pope: If clouds restrain their gifts and grant no rain, The treasures fail in ocean's wide domain
kurals.drew: Even the wealth of the wide sea will be diminished, if the cloud that has drawn (its waters) up gives them not back again (in rain)

kurals.translit: Sirappotu Poosanai Sellaadhu Vaanam / Varakkumel Vaanorkkum Eentu
kurals.pope: If heaven grow dry, with feast and offering never more, Will men on earth the heavenly ones adore
kurals.drew: If the heaven dry up, neither yearly festivals, nor daily worship will be offered in this world, to the celestials

kurals.translit: Thaanam Thavamirantum Thangaa Viyanulakam / Vaanam Vazhangaa Thenin
kurals.pope: If heaven its watery treasures ceases to dispense, Through the wide world cease gifts, and deeds of 'penitence'
kurals.drew: If rain fall not, penance and alms-deeds will not dwell within this spacious world

kurals.translit: Neerindru Amaiyaadhu Ulakenin Yaaryaarkkum / Vaanindru Amaiyaadhu Ozhukku
kurals.pope: When water fails, functions of nature cease, you say; Thus when rain fails, no men can walk in 'duty's ordered way'
kurals.drew: If it be said that the duties of life cannot be discharged by any person without water, so without rain there cannot be the flowing of water

kurals.translit: Ozhukkaththu Neeththaar Perumai Vizhuppaththu / Ventum Panuval Thunivu
kurals.pope: The settled rule of every code requires, as highest good, Their greatness who, renouncing all, true to their rule have stood
kurals.drew: The end and aim of all treatise is to extol beyond all other excellence, the greatness of those who, while abiding in the rule of conduct peculiar to their state, have abandoned all desire

kurals.translit: Thurandhaar Perumai Thunaikkoorin Vaiyaththu / Irandhaarai Ennikkon Tatru
kurals.pope: As counting those that from the earth have passed away,'Tis vain attempt the might of holy men to say
kurals.drew: To describe the measure of the greatness of those who have forsaken the two-fold desires, is like counting the dead

kurals.translit: Irumai Vakaidherindhu Eentuaram Poontaar / Perumai Pirangitru Ulaku
kurals.pope: Their greatness earth transcends, who, way of both worlds weighed, In this world take their stand, in virtue's robe arrayed
kurals.drew: The greatness of those who have discovered the properties of both states of being, and renounced the world, shines forth on earth (beyond all others)

kurals.translit: Uranennum Thottiyaan Oraindhum Kaappaan / Varanennum Vaippirkor Viththu
kurals.pope: He, who with firmness, curb the five restrains, Is seed for soil of yonder happy plains
kurals.drew: He who guides his five senses by the hook of wisdom will be a seed in the world of heaven

kurals.translit: Aindhaviththaan Aatral Akalvisumpu Laarkomaan / Indhirane Saalung Kari
kurals.pope: Their might who have destroyed 'the five', shall soothly tellIndra, the lord of those in heaven's wide realms that dwell
kurals.drew: Indra, the king of the inhabitants of the spacious heaven, is himself, a sufficient proof of the strength of him who has subdued his five senses

kurals.translit: Seyarkariya Seyvaar Periyar Siriyar / Seyarkariya Seykalaa Thaar
kurals.pope: Things hard in the doing will great men do; Things hard in the doing the mean eschew
kurals.drew: The great will do those things which is difficult to be done; but the mean cannot do them

kurals.translit: Suvaioli Ooruosai Naatramendru Aindhin / Vakaidherivaan Katte Ulaku
kurals.pope: Taste, light, touch, sound, and smell: who knows the wayOf all the five,- the world submissive owns his sway
kurals.drew: The world is within the knowledge of him who knows the properties of taste, sight, touch, hearing and smell

kurals.translit: Niraimozhi Maandhar Perumai Nilaththu / Maraimozhi Kaatti Vitum
kurals.pope: The might of men whose word is never vain, The 'secret word' shall to the earth proclaim
kurals.drew: The hidden words of the men whose words are full of effect, will shew their greatness to the world

kurals.translit: Kunamennum Kundreri Nindraar Vekuli / Kanameyum Kaaththal Aridhu
kurals.pope: The wrath 'tis hard e'en for an instant to endure, Of those who virtue's hill have scaled, and stand secure
kurals.drew: The anger of those who have ascended the mountain of goodness, though it continue but for a moment, cannot be resisted

kurals.translit: Andhanar Enpor Aravormar Revvuyir / Kkum Sendhanmai Poontozhuka Laan
kurals.pope: Towards all that breathe, with seemly graciousness adorned they live; And thus to virtue's sons the name of 'Anthanar' men give
kurals.drew: The virtuous are truly called Anthanar; because in their conduct towards all creatures they are clothed in kindness

kurals.chapter_en: Assertion of the Strength of Virtue
kurals.translit: Sirappu Eenum Selvamum Eenum / Araththinooungu Aakkam Evano Uyirkku
kurals.pope: It yields distinction, yields prosperity; what gainGreater than virtue can a living man obtain
kurals.drew: Virtue will confer heaven and wealth; what greater source of happiness can man possess ?

kurals.chapter_en: Assertion of the Strength of Virtue
kurals.translit: Araththinooungu Aakkamum Illai Adhanai / Maraththalin Oongillai Ketu
kurals.pope: No greater gain than virtue aught can cause; No greater loss than life oblivious of her laws
kurals.drew: There can be no greater source of good than (the practice of) virtue; there can be no greater source of evil than the forgetfulness of it

kurals.chapter_en: Assertion of the Strength of Virtue
kurals.translit: Ollum Vakaiyaan Aravinai Ovaadhe / Sellumvaai Ellaanj Cheyal
kurals.pope: To finish virtue's work with ceaseless effort strive, What way thou may'st, where'er thou see'st the work may thrive
kurals.drew: As much as possible, in every way, incessantly practise virtue

kurals.chapter_en: Assertion of the Strength of Virtue
kurals.translit: Manaththukkan Maasilan Aadhal Anaiththu / Aran Aakula Neera Pira
kurals.pope: Spotless be thou in mind! This only merits virtue's name; All else, mere pomp of idle sound, no real worth can claim
kurals.drew: Let him who does virtuous deeds be of spotless mind; to that extent is virtue; all else is vain show

kurals.chapter_en: Assertion of the Strength of Virtue
kurals.translit: Azhukkaaru Avaavekuli Innaachchol Naankum / Izhukkaa Iyandradhu Aram
kurals.pope: 'Tis virtue when, his footsteps sliding not through envy, wrath, Lust, evil speech-these four, man onwards moves in ordered path
kurals.drew: That conduct is virtue which is free from these four things, viz, malice, desire, anger and bitter speech

kurals.chapter_en: Assertion of the Strength of Virtue
kurals.translit: Andrarivaam Ennaadhu Aranjeyka Matradhu / Pondrungaal Pondraath Thunai
kurals.pope: Do deeds of virtue now Say not, 'To-morrow we'll be wise'; Thus, when thou diest, shalt thou find a help that never dies
kurals.drew: Defer not virtue to another day; receive her now; and at the dying hour she will be your undying friend

kurals.chapter_en: Assertion of the Strength of Virtue
kurals.translit: Araththaaru Ithuvena Ventaa Sivikai / Poruththaanotu Oorndhaan Itai
kurals.pope: Needs not in words to dwell on virtue's fruits: compareThe man in litter borne with them that toiling bear
kurals.drew: The fruit of virtue need not be described in books; it may be inferred from seeing the bearer of a palanquin and the rider therein

kurals.chapter_en: Assertion of the Strength of Virtue
kurals.translit: Veezhnaal Pataaamai Nandraatrin Aqdhoruvan / Vaazhnaal Vazhiyataikkum Kal
kurals.pope: If no day passing idly, good to do each day you toil, A stone it will be to block the way of future days of moil
kurals.drew: If one allows no day to pass without some good being done, his conduct will be a stone to block up the passage to other births

kurals.chapter_en: Assertion of the Strength of Virtue
kurals.translit: Araththaan Varuvadhe Inpam Mar / Rellaam Puraththa Pukazhum Ila
kurals.pope: What from virtue floweth, yieldeth dear delight; All else extern, is void of glory's light
kurals.drew: Only that pleasure which flows from domestic virtue is pleasure; all else is not pleasure, and it is without praise

kurals.chapter_en: Assertion of the Strength of Virtue
kurals.translit: Seyarpaala Thorum Arane Oruvarku / Uyarpaala Thorum Pazhi
kurals.pope: 'Virtue' sums the things that should be done;'Vice' sums the things that man should shun
kurals.drew: That is virtue which each ought to do, and that is vice which each should shun

kurals.translit: Ilvaazhvaan Enpaan Iyalputaiya Moovarkkum / Nallaatrin Nindra Thunai
kurals.pope: The men of household virtue, firm in way of good, sustainThe other orders three that rule professed maintain
kurals.drew: He will be called a (true) householder, who is a firm support to the virtuous of the three orders in

kurals.translit: Thurandhaarkkum Thuvvaa Dhavarkkum Irandhaarkkum / Ilvaazhvaan Enpaan Thunai
kurals.pope: To anchorites, to indigent, to those who've passed away, The man for household virtue famed is needful held and stay
kurals.drew: He will be said to flourish in domestic virtue who aids the forsaken, the poor, and the dead

kurals.translit: Thenpulaththaar Theyvam Virundhokkal Thaanendraangu / Aimpulaththaaru Ompal Thalai
kurals.pope: The manes, God, guests kindred, self, in due degree, These five to cherish well is chiefest charity
kurals.drew: The chief (duty of the householder) is to preserve the five-fold rule (of conduct) towards the manes, the Gods, his guests, his relations and himself

kurals.translit: Pazhiyanjip Paaththoon Utaiththaayin Vaazhkkai / Vazhiyenjal Egngnaandrum Il
kurals.pope: Who shares his meal with other, while all guilt he shuns, His virtuous line unbroken though the ages runs
kurals.drew: His descendants shall never fail who, living in the domestic state, fears vice (in the acquisition of property) and shares his food (with others)

kurals.translit: Anpum Aranum Utaiththaayin Ilvaazhkkai / Panpum Payanum Adhu
kurals.pope: If love and virtue in the household reign, This is of life the perfect grace and gain
kurals.drew: If the married life possess love and virtue, these will be both its duty and reward

kurals.translit: Araththaatrin Ilvaazhkkai Aatrin Puraththaatril / Pooip Peruva Thevan?
kurals.pope: If man in active household life a virtuous soul retain, What fruit from other modes of virtue can he gain
kurals.drew: What will he who lives virtuously in the domestic state gain by going into the other, (ascetic) state ?

kurals.translit: Iyalpinaan Ilvaazhkkai Vaazhpavan Enpaan / Muyalvaarul Ellaam Thalai
kurals.pope: In nature's way who spends his calm domestic days,'Mid all that strive for virtue's crown hath foremost place
kurals.drew: Among all those who labour (for future happiness) he is greatest who lives well in the household state

kurals.translit: Aatrin Ozhukki Aranizhukkaa Ilvaazhkkai / Norpaarin Nonmai Utaiththu
kurals.pope: Others it sets upon their way, itself from virtue ne'er declines; Than stern ascetics' pains such life domestic brighter shines
kurals.drew: The householder who, not swerving from virtue, helps the ascetic in his way, endures more than those who endure penance

kurals.translit: Aran Enap Pattadhe Ilvaazhkkai / Aqdhum Piranpazhippa Thillaayin Nandru
kurals.pope: The life domestic rightly bears true virtue's name; That other too, if blameless found, due praise may claim
kurals.drew: The marriage state is truly called virtue The other state is also good, if others do not reproach it

kurals.translit: Vaiyaththul Vaazhvaangu Vaazhpavan Vaanu�ryum / Theyvaththul Vaikkap Patum
kurals.pope: Who shares domestic life, by household virtues graced, Shall, mid the Gods, in heaven who dwell, be placed
kurals.drew: He who on earth has lived in the conjugal state as he should live, will be placed among the Gods who dwell in heaven

kurals.translit: Manaikdhakka Maanputaiyal Aakiththar Kontaan / Valaththakkaal Vaazhkkaith Thunai
kurals.pope: As doth the house beseem, she shows her wifely dignity; As doth her husband's wealth befit, she spends: help - meet is she
kurals.drew: She who has the excellence of home virtues, and can expend within the means of her husband, is a help in the domestic state

kurals.translit: Manaimaatchi Illaalkan Illaayin Vaazhkkai / Enaimaatchith Thaayinum Il
kurals.pope: If household excellence be wanting in the wife, Howe'er with splendour lived, all worthless is the life
kurals.drew: If the wife be devoid of domestic excellence, whatever (other) greatness be possessed, the conjugal state, is nothing

kurals.translit: Illadhen Illaval Maanpaanaal Ulladhen / Illaval Maanaak Katai?
kurals.pope: There is no lack within the house, where wife in worth excels, There is no luck within the house, where wife dishonoured dwells
kurals.drew: If his wife be eminent (in virtue), what does (that man) not possess ? If she be without excellence, what does (he) possess ?

kurals.translit: Pennin Perundhakka Yaavula Karpennum / Thinmaiun Taakap Perin
kurals.pope: If woman might of chastity retain, What choicer treasure doth the world contain
kurals.drew: What is more excellent than a wife, if she possess the stability of chastity ?

kurals.translit: Theyvam Thozhaaal Kozhunan Thozhudhezhuvaal / Peyyenap Peyyum Mazhai
kurals.pope: No God adoring, low she bends before her lord; Then rising, serves: the rain falls instant at her word
kurals.drew: If she, who does not worship God, but who rising worships her husband, say, "let it rain," it will rain

kurals.translit: Tharkaaththuth Tharkontaar Penith Thakaisaandra / Sorkaaththuch Chorvilaal Pen
kurals.pope: Who guards herself, for husband's comfort cares, her household's fame, In perfect wise with sleepless soul preserves, -give her a woman's name
kurals.drew: She is a wife who unweariedly guards herself, takes care of her husband, and preserves an unsullied fame

kurals.translit: Siraikaakkum Kaappevan Seyyum Makalir / Niraikaakkum Kaappe Thalai
kurals.pope: Of what avail is watch and ward?Honour's woman's safest guard
kurals.drew: What avails the guard of a prison ? The chief guard of a woman is her chastity

kurals.translit: Petraar Perinperuvar Pentir Perunjirappup / Puththelir Vaazhum Ulaku
kurals.pope: If wife be wholly true to him who gained her as his bride, Great glory gains she in the world where gods bliss abide
kurals.drew: If women shew reverence to their husbands, they will obtain great excellence in the world where the gods flourish

kurals.translit: Pukazhpurindha Illilorkku Illai Ikazhvaarmun / Erupol Peetu Natai
kurals.pope: Who have not spouses that in virtue's praise delight, They lion-like can never walk in scorner's sight
kurals.drew: The man whose wife seeks not the praise (of chastity) cannot walk with lion-like stately step, before those who revile them

kurals.translit: Mangalam Enpa Manaimaatchi Matru / Adhan Nankalam Nanmakkat Peru
kurals.pope: The house's 'blessing', men pronounce the house-wife excellent; The gain of blessed children is its goodly ornament
kurals.drew: The excellence of a wife is the good of her husband; and good children are the jewels of that goodness

kurals.translit: Perumavatrul Yaamarivadhu Illai Arivarindha / Makkatperu Alla Pira
kurals.pope: Of all that men acquire, we know not any greater gain, Than that which by the birth of learned children men obtain
kurals.drew: Among all the benefits that may be acquired, we know no greater benefit than the acquisition of intelligent children

kurals.translit: Ezhupirappum Theeyavai Theentaa Pazhipirangaap / Panputai Makkat Perin
kurals.pope: Who children gain, that none reproach, of virtuous worth, No evils touch them, through the sev'n-fold maze of birth
kurals.drew: The evils of the seven births shall not touch those who abtain children of a good disposition, free from vice

kurals.translit: Thamporul Enpadham Makkal Avarporul / Thamdham Vinaiyaan Varum
kurals.pope: 'Man's children are his fortune,' say the wise; From each one's deeds his varied fortunes rise
kurals.drew: Men will call their sons their wealth, because it flows to them through the deeds which they (sons) perform on their behalf

kurals.translit: Amizhdhinum Aatra Inidhedham Makkal / Sirukai Alaaviya Koozh
kurals.pope: Than God's ambrosia sweeter far the food before men laid, In which the little hands of children of their own have play'd
kurals.drew: The rice in which the little hand of their children has dabbled will be far sweeter (to the parent) than ambrosia

kurals.translit: Makkalmey Theental Utarkinpam Matru / Avar Sorkettal Inpam Sevikku
kurals.pope: To patent sweet the touch of children dear; Their voice is sweetest music to his ear
kurals.drew: The touch of children gives pleasure to the body, and the hearing of their words, pleasure to the ear

kurals.translit: Kuzhal Inidhu Yaazhinidhu Enpadham / Makkal Mazhalaichchol Kelaa Thavar
kurals.pope: 'The pipe is sweet,' 'the lute is sweet,' by them't will be averred, Who music of their infants' lisping lips have never heard
kurals.drew: "The pipe is sweet, the lute is sweet," say those who have not heard the prattle of their own children

kurals.translit: Thandhai Makarkaatrum Nandri Avaiyaththu / Mundhi Iruppach Cheyal
kurals.pope: Sire greatest boon on son confers, who makes him meet, In councils of the wise to fill the highest seat
kurals.drew: The benefit which a father should confer on his son is to give him precedence in the assembly of the learned

kurals.translit: Thammindham Makkal Arivutaimai Maanilaththu / Mannuyirk Kellaam Inidhu
kurals.pope: Their children's wisdom greater than their own confessed, Through the wide world is sweet to every human breast
kurals.drew: That their children should possess knowledge is more pleasing to all men of this great earth than to themselves

kurals.translit: Eendra Pozhudhin Peridhuvakkum Thanmakanaich / Chaandron Enakketta Thaai
kurals.pope: When mother hears him named 'fulfill'd of wisdom's lore,'Far greater joy she feels, than when her son she bore
kurals.drew: The mother who hears her son called "a wise man" will rejoice more than she did at his birth

kurals.translit: Makandhandhaikku Aatrum Udhavi Ivandhandhai / Ennotraan Kol Enum Sol
kurals.pope: To sire, what best requital can by grateful child be done?To make men say, 'What merit gained the father such a son?'
kurals.drew: (So to act) that it may be said "by what great penance did his father beget him," is the benefit which a son should render to his father

kurals.translit: Anpirkum Unto Ataikkundhaazh Aarvalar / Punkaneer Poosal Tharum
kurals.pope: And is there bar that can even love restrain?The tiny tear shall make the lover's secret plain
kurals.drew: Is there any fastening that can shut in love ? Tears of the affectionate will publish the love that is within

kurals.translit: Anpilaar Ellaam Thamakkuriyar Anputaiyaar / Enpum Uriyar Pirarkku
kurals.pope: The loveless to themselves belong alone; The loving men are others' to the very bone
kurals.drew: Those who are destitute of love appropriate all they have to themselves; but those who possess love consider even their bones to belong to others

kurals.translit: Anpotu Iyaindha Vazhakkenpa Aaruyirkku / Enpotu Iyaindha Thotarpu
kurals.pope: Of precious soul with body's flesh and bone, The union yields one fruit, the life of love alone
kurals.drew: They say that the union of soul and body in man is the fruit of the union of love and virtue (in a former birth)

kurals.translit: Anpu Eenum Aarvam Utaimai / Adhueenum Nanpu Ennum Naataach
kurals.pope: From love fond yearning springs for union sweet of minds; And that the bond of rare excelling friendship binds
kurals.drew: Love begets desire: and that (desire) begets the immeasureable excellence of friendship

kurals.translit: Anputru Amarndha Vazhakkenpa Vaiyakaththu / Inputraar Eydhum Sirappu
kurals.pope: Sweetness on earth and rarest bliss above, These are the fruits of tranquil life of love
kurals.drew: These are the fruits of tranquil life of love

kurals.translit: Araththirke Anpusaar Penpa Ariyaar / Maraththirkum Aqdhe Thunai
kurals.pope: The unwise deem love virtue only can sustain, It also helps the man who evil would restrain
kurals.drew: The ignorant say that love is an ally to virtue only, but it is also a help to get out of vice

kurals.translit: Enpi Ladhanai Veyilpolak Kaayume / Anpi Ladhanai Aram
kurals.pope: As sun's fierce ray dries up the boneless things, So loveless beings virtue's power to nothing brings
kurals.drew: Virtue will burn up the soul which is without love, even as the sun burns up the creature which is without bone, ie worms

kurals.translit: Anpakath Thillaa Uyirvaazhkkai Vanpaarkan / Vatral Marandhalirth Thatru
kurals.pope: The loveless soul, the very joys of life may know, When flowers, in barren soil, on sapless trees, shall blow
kurals.drew: The domestic state of that man whose mind is without love is like the flourishing of a withered tree upon the parched desert

kurals.translit: Puraththurup Pellaam Evanseyyum Yaakkai / Akaththuruppu Anpi Lavarkku
kurals.pope: Though every outward part complete, the body's fitly framed; What good, when soul within, of love devoid, lies halt and maimed
kurals.drew: Of what avail are all the external members (of the body) to those who are destitute of love, the internal member

kurals.translit: Anpin Vazhiyadhu Uyirnilai Aqdhilaarkku / Enpudhol Porththa Utampu
kurals.pope: Bodies of loveless men are bony framework clad with skin; Then is the body seat of life, when love resides within
kurals.drew: That body alone which is inspired with love contains a living soul: if void of it, (the body) is bone overlaid with skin

kurals.translit: Irundhompi Ilvaazhva Thellaam Virundhompi / Velaanmai Seydhar Poruttu
kurals.pope: All household cares and course of daily life have this in viewGuests to receive with courtesy, and kindly acts to do
kurals.drew: The whole design of living in the domestic state and laying up (property) is (to be able) to exercise the benevolence of hospitality

kurals.translit: Virundhu Puraththadhaath Thaanuntal Saavaa / Marundheninum Ventarpaar Randru
kurals.pope: Though food of immortality should crown the board, Feasting alone, the guests without unfed, is thing abhorred
kurals.drew: It is not fit that one should wish his guests to be outside (his house) even though he were eating the food of immortality

kurals.translit: Varuvirundhu Vaikalum Ompuvaan Vaazhkkai / Paruvandhu Paazhpatudhal Indru
kurals.pope: Each day he tends the coming guest with kindly care; Painless, unfailing plenty shall his household share
kurals.drew: The domestic life of the man that daily entertains the guests who come to him shall not be laid waste by poverty

kurals.translit: Akanamarndhu Seyyaal Uraiyum Mukanamarndhu / Nalvirundhu Ompuvaan Il
kurals.pope: With smiling face he entertains each virtuous guest,'Fortune' with gladsome mind shall in his dwelling rest
kurals.drew: Lakshmi with joyous mind shall dwell in the house of that man who, with cheerful countenance, entertains the good as guests

kurals.translit: Viththum Italventum Kollo Virundhompi / Michchil Misaivaan Pulam
kurals.pope: Who first regales his guest, and then himself supplies, O'er all his fields, unsown, shall plenteous harvests rise
kurals.drew: Is it necessary to sow the field of the man who, having feasted his guests, eats what may remain ?

kurals.translit: Selvirundhu Ompi Varuvirundhu Paarththiruppaan / Nalvarundhu Vaanath Thavarkku
kurals.pope: The guest arrived he tends, the coming guest expects to see; To those in heavenly homes that dwell a welcome guest is he
kurals.drew: He who, having entertained the guests that have come, looks out for others who may yet come, will be a welcome guest to the inhabitants of heaven

kurals.translit: Inaiththunaith Thenpadhon Rillai Virundhin / Thunaiththunai Velvip Payan
kurals.pope: To reckon up the fruit of kindly deeds were all in vain; Their worth is as the worth of guests you entertain
kurals.drew: The advantages of benevolence cannot be measured; the measure (of the virtue) of the guests (entertained) is the only measure

kurals.translit: Parindhompip Patratrem Enpar Virundhompi / Velvi Thalaippataa Thaar
kurals.pope: With pain they guard their stores, yet 'All forlorn are we,' they'll cry, Who cherish not their guests, nor kindly help supply
kurals.drew: Those who have taken no part in the benevolence of hospitality shall (at length lament) saying, "we have laboured and laid up wealth and are now without support."

kurals.translit: Utaimaiyul Inmai Virundhompal Ompaa / Matamai Matavaarkan Untu
kurals.pope: To turn from guests is penury, though worldly goods abound;'Tis senseless folly, only with the senseless found
kurals.drew: That stupidity which excercises no hospitality is poverty in the midst of wealth It is the property of the stupid

kurals.translit: Moppak Kuzhaiyum Anichcham Mukandhirindhu / Nokkak Kuzhaiyum Virundhu
kurals.pope: The flower of 'Anicha' withers away, If you do but its fragrance inhale; If the face of the host cold welcome convey, The guest's heart within him will fail
kurals.drew: As the Anicham flower fades in smelling, so fades the guest when the face is turned away

kurals.translit: Insolaal Eeram Alaiip Patiruilavaam / Semporul Kantaarvaaich Chol
kurals.pope: Pleasant words are words with all pervading love that burn; Words from his guileless mouth who can the very truth discern
kurals.drew: Sweet words are those which imbued with love and free from deceit flow from the mouth of the virtuous

kurals.translit: Akanamarndhu Eedhalin Nandre Mukanamarndhu / Insolan Aakap Perin
kurals.pope: A pleasant word with beaming smile's preferred, Even to gifts with liberal heart conferred
kurals.drew: Sweet speech, with a cheerful countenance is better than a gift made with a joyous mind

kurals.translit: Mukaththaan Amarndhuinidhu Nokki Akaththaanaam / Inso Linadhe Aram
kurals.pope: With brightly beaming smile, and kindly light of loving eye, And heart sincere, to utter pleasant words is charity
kurals.drew: Sweet speech, flowing from the heart (uttered) with a cheerful countenance and a sweet look, is true virtue

kurals.translit: Thunpurooum Thuvvaamai Illaakum Yaarmaattum / Inpurooum Inso Lavarkku
kurals.pope: The men of pleasant speech that gladness breathe around, Through indigence shall never sorrow's prey be found
kurals.drew: Sorrow-increasing poverty shall not come upon those who use towards all, pleasure-increasing sweetness of speech

kurals.translit: Panivutaiyan Insolan Aadhal Oruvarku / Aniyalla Matrup Pira
kurals.pope: Humility with pleasant speech to man on earth, Is choice adornment; all besides is nothing worth
kurals.drew: Humility and sweetness of speech are the ornaments of man; all others are not (ornaments)

kurals.translit: Allavai Theya Aramperukum Nallavai / Naati Iniya Solin
kurals.pope: Who seeks out good, words from his lips of sweetness flow; In him the power of vice declines, and virtues grow
kurals.drew: If a man, while seeking to speak usefully, speaks also sweetly, his sins will diminish and his virtue increase

kurals.translit: Nayan Eendru Nandri Payakkum / Payaneendru Panpin Thalaippiriyaach Chol
kurals.pope: The words of sterling sense, to rule of right that strict adhere, To virtuous action prompting, blessings yield in every sphere
kurals.drew: That speech which, while imparting benefits ceases not to please, will yield righteousness (for this world) and merit (for the next world)

kurals.translit: Sirumaiyul Neengiya Insol Marumaiyum / Immaiyum Inpam Tharum
kurals.pope: Sweet kindly words, from meanness free, delight of heart, In world to come and in this world impart
kurals.drew: Sweet speech, free from harm to others, will give pleasure both in this world and in the next

kurals.translit: Insol Inidheendral Kaanpaan Evankolo / Vansol Vazhangu Vadhu?
kurals.pope: Who sees the pleasure kindly speech affords, Why makes he use of harsh, repellant words
kurals.drew: Why does he use harsh words, who sees the pleasure which sweet speech yields ?

kurals.translit: Iniya Ulavaaka Innaadha Kooral / Kaniiruppak Kaaikavarn Thatru
kurals.pope: When pleasant words are easy, bitter words to use, Is, leaving sweet ripe fruit, the sour unripe to choose
kurals.drew: To say disagreeable things when agreeable are at hand is like eating unripe fruit when there is ripe

kurals.translit: Seyyaamal Seydha Udhavikku Vaiyakamum / Vaanakamum Aatral Aridhu
kurals.pope: Assistance given by those who ne'er received our aid, Is debt by gift of heaven and earth but poorly paid
kurals.drew: (The gift of) heaven and earth is not an equivalent for a benefit which is conferred where none had been received

kurals.translit: Kaalaththi Naarseydha Nandri Siridheninum / Gnaalaththin Maanap Peridhu
kurals.pope: A timely benefit, -though thing of little worth, The gift itself, -in excellence transcends the earth
kurals.drew: A favour conferred in the time of need, though it be small (in itself), is (in value) much larger than the world

kurals.translit: Payandhookkaar Seydha Udhavi Nayandhookkin / Nanmai Katalin Peridhu
kurals.pope: Kindness shown by those who weigh not what the return may be:When you ponder right its merit, 'Tis vaster than the sea
kurals.drew: If we weigh the excellence of a benefit which is conferred without weighing the return, it is larger than the sea

kurals.translit: Thinaiththunai Nandri Seyinum Panaiththunaiyaak / Kolvar Payandheri Vaar
kurals.pope: Each benefit to those of actions' fruit who rightly deem, Though small as millet-seed, as palm-tree vast will seem
kurals.drew: Though the benefit conferred be as small as a millet seed, those who know its advantage will consider it as large as a palmyra fruit

kurals.translit: Udhavi Varaiththandru Udhavi Udhavi / Seyappattaar Saalpin Varaiththu
kurals.pope: The kindly aid's extent is of its worth no measure true; Its worth is as the worth of him to whom the act you do
kurals.drew: The benefit itself is not the measure of the benefit; the worth of those who have received it is its measure

kurals.translit: Maravarka Maasatraar Kenmai Thuravarka / Thunpaththul Thuppaayaar Natpu
kurals.pope: Kindness of men of stainless soul remember evermoreForsake thou never friends who were thy stay in sorrow sore
kurals.drew: Forsake not the friendship of those who have been your staff in adversity Forget not be benevolence of the blameless

kurals.translit: Ezhumai Ezhupirappum Ulluvar Thangan / Vizhuman Thutaiththavar Natpu
kurals.pope: Through all seven worlds, in seven-fold birth, Remains in mem'ry of the wiseFriendship of those who wiped on earth, The tears of sorrow from their eyes
kurals.drew: (The wise) will remember throughout their seven-fold births the love of those who have wiped away their affliction

kurals.translit: Nandri Marappadhu Nandrandru Nandralladhu / Andre Marappadhu Nandru
kurals.pope: 'Tis never good to let the thought of good things done thee pass away; Of things not good, 'tis good to rid thy memory that very day
kurals.drew: It is not good to forget a benefit; it is good to forget an injury even in the very moment (in which it is inflicted)

kurals.translit: Kondranna Innaa Seyinum Avarseydha / Ondrunandru Ullak Ketum
kurals.pope: Effaced straightway is deadliest injury, By thought of one kind act in days gone by
kurals.drew: Though one inflict an injury great as murder, it will perish before the thought of one benefit (formerly) conferred

kurals.translit: Ennandri Kondraarkkum Uyvuntaam Uyvillai / Seynnandri Kondra Makarku
kurals.pope: Who every good have killed, may yet destruction flee; Who 'benefit' has killed, that man shall ne'er 'scape free
kurals.drew: He who has killed every virtue may yet escape; there is no escape for him who has killed a benefit

kurals.translit: Thakudhi Enavondru Nandre Pakudhiyaal / Paarpattu Ozhukap Perin
kurals.pope: If justice, failing not, its quality maintain, Giving to each his due, -'tis man's one highest gain
kurals.drew: That equity which consists in acting with equal regard to each of (the three) divisions of men [enemies, strangers and friends] is a pre-eminent virtue

kurals.translit: Seppam Utaiyavan Aakkanj Chidhaivindri / Echchaththir Kemaappu Utaiththu
kurals.pope: The just man's wealth unwasting shall endure, And to his race a lasting joy ensure
kurals.drew: The wealth of the man of rectitude will not perish, but will bring happiness also to his posterity

kurals.translit: Nandre Tharinum Natuvikandhaam Aakkaththai / Andre Yozhiya Vital
kurals.pope: Though only good it seem to give, yet gainBy wrong acquired, not e'en one day retain
kurals.drew: Forsake in the very moment (of acquisition) that gain which, though it should bring advantage, is without equity

kurals.translit: Thakkaar Thakavilar Enpadhu Avaravar / Echchaththaar Kaanap Patum
kurals.pope: Who just or unjust lived shall soon appear:By each one's offspring shall the truth be clear
kurals.drew: The worthy and unworthy may be known by the existence or otherwise of good offsprings

kurals.translit: Ketum Perukkamum Illalla Nenjaththuk / Kotaamai Saandrork Kani
kurals.pope: The gain and loss in life are not mere accident; Just mind inflexible is sages' ornament
kurals.drew: Loss and gain come not without cause; it is the ornament of the wise to preserve evenness of mind (under both)

kurals.translit: Ketuvalyaan Enpadhu Arikadhan Nenjam / Natuvoreei Alla Seyin
kurals.pope: If, right deserting, heart to evil turn, Let man impending ruin's sign discern
kurals.drew: Let him whose mind departing from equity commits sin well consider thus within himself, "I shall perish."

kurals.translit: Ketuvaaka Vaiyaadhu Ulakam Natuvaaka / Nandrikkan Thangiyaan Thaazhvu
kurals.pope: The man who justly lives, tenacious of the right, In low estate is never low to wise man's sight
kurals.drew: The great will not regard as poverty the low estate of that man who dwells in the virtue of equity

kurals.translit: Samanseydhu Seerdhookkung Kolpol Amaindhorupaal / Kotaamai Saandrork Kani
kurals.pope: To stand, like balance-rod that level hangs and rightly weighs, With calm unbiassed equity of soul, is sages' praise
kurals.drew: To incline to neither side, but to rest impartial as the even-fixed scale is the ornament of the wise

kurals.translit: Sorkottam Illadhu Seppam Orudhalaiyaa / Utkottam Inmai Perin
kurals.pope: Inflexibility in word is righteousness, If men inflexibility of soul possess
kurals.drew: Freedom from obliquity of speech is rectitude, if there be (corresponding) freedom from bias of mind

kurals.translit: Vaanikam Seyvaarkku Vaanikam Penip / Piravum Thamapol Seyin
kurals.pope: As thriving trader is the trader known, Who guards another's interests as his own
kurals.drew: The true merchandize of merchants is to guard and do by the things of others as they do by their own

kurals.translit: Atakkam Amararul Uykkum Atangaamai / Aarirul Uyththu Vitum
kurals.pope: Control of self does man conduct to bliss th' immortals share; Indulgence leads to deepest night, and leaves him there
kurals.drew: Self-control will place (a man) among the Gods; the want of it will drive (him) into the thickest darkness (of hell)

kurals.translit: Kaakka Porulaa Atakkaththai Aakkam / Adhaninooung Killai Uyirkku
kurals.pope: Guard thou as wealth the power of self-control; Than this no greater gain to living soul
kurals.drew: Let self-control be guarded as a treasure; there is no greater source of good for man than that

kurals.translit: Serivarindhu Seermai Payakkum Arivarindhu / Aatrin Atangap Perin
kurals.pope: If versed in wisdom's lore by virtue's law you self restrainYour self-repression known will yield you glory's gain
kurals.drew: Knowing that self-control is knowledge, if a man should control himself, in the prescribed course, such self-control will bring him distinction among the wise

kurals.translit: Nilaiyin Thiriyaadhu Atangiyaan Thotram / Malaiyinum Maanap Peridhu
kurals.pope: In his station, all unswerving, if man self subdue, Greater he than mountain proudly rising to the view
kurals.drew: More lofty than a mountain will be the greatness of that man who without swerving from his domestic state, controls himself

kurals.translit: Ellaarkkum Nandraam Panidhal Avarullum / Selvarkke Selvam Thakaiththu
kurals.pope: To all humility is goodly grace; but chief to themWith fortune blessed, -'tis fortune's diadem
kurals.drew: Humility is good in all; but especially in the rich it is (the excellence of) higher riches

kurals.translit: Orumaiyul Aamaipol Aindhatakkal Aatrin / Ezhumaiyum Emaap Putaiththu
kurals.pope: Like tortoise, who the five restrainsIn one, through seven world bliss obtains
kurals.drew: Should one throughout a single birth, like a tortoise keep in his five senses, the fruit of it will prove a safe-guard to him throughout the seven-fold births.

kurals.translit: Yaakaavaa Raayinum Naakaakka Kaavaakkaal / Sokaappar Sollizhukkup Pattu
kurals.pope: Whate'er they fail to guard, o'er lips men guard should keep; If not, through fault of tongue, they bitter tears shall weep
kurals.drew: Whatever besides you leave unguarded, guard your tongue; otherwise errors of speech and the consequent misery will ensue

kurals.translit: Ondraanun Theechchol Porutpayan Untaayin / Nandraakaa Thaaki Vitum
kurals.pope: Though some small gain of good it seem to bring, The evil word is parent still of evil thing
kurals.drew: If a man's speech be productive of a single evil, all the good by him will be turned into evil

kurals.translit: Theeyinaar Suttapun Ullaarum Aaraadhe / Naavinaar Sutta Vatu
kurals.pope: In flesh by fire inflamed, nature may thoroughly heal the sore; In soul by tongue inflamed, the ulcer healeth never more
kurals.drew: The wound which has been burnt in by fire may heal, but a wound burnt in by the tongue will never heal

kurals.translit: Kadhangaaththuk Katratangal Aatruvaan Sevvi / Arampaarkkum Aatrin Nuzhaindhu
kurals.pope: Who learns restraint, and guards his soul from wrath, Virtue, a timely aid, attends his path
kurals.drew: Virtue, seeking for an opportunity, will come into the path of that man who, possessed of learning and self-control, guards himself against anger

kurals.translit: Ozhukkam Vizhuppan Tharalaan Ozhukkam / Uyirinum Ompap Patum
kurals.pope: 'Decorum' gives especial excellence; with greater care'Decorum' should men guard than life, which all men share
kurals.drew: Propriety of conduct leads to eminence, it should therefore be preserved more carefully than life

kurals.translit: Parindhompik Kaakka Ozhukkam Therindhompith / Therinum Aqdhe Thunai
kurals.pope: Searching, duly watching, learning, 'decorum' still we find; Man's only aid; toiling, guard thou this with watchful mind
kurals.drew: Let propriety of conduct be laboriously preserved and guarded; though one know and practise and excel in many virtues, that will be an eminent aid

kurals.translit: Ozhukkam Utaimai Kutimai Izhukkam / Izhindha Pirappaai Vitum
kurals.pope: 'Decorum's' true nobility on earth;'Indecorum's' issue is ignoble birth
kurals.drew: Propriety of conduct is true greatness of birth, and impropriety will sink into a mean birth

kurals.translit: Marappinum Oththuk Kolalaakum Paarppaan / Pirappozhukkang Kundrak Ketum
kurals.pope: Though he forget, the Brahman may regain his Vedic lore; Failing in 'decorum due,' birthright's gone for evermore
kurals.drew: A Brahman though he should forget the Vedas may recover it by reading; but, if he fail in propriety of conduct even his high birth will be destroyed

kurals.translit: Azhukkaa Rutaiyaankan Aakkampondru Illai / Ozhukka Milaankan Uyarvu
kurals.pope: The envious soul in life no rich increase of blessing gains, So man of 'due decorum' void no dignity obtains
kurals.drew: Just as the envious man will be without wealth, so will the man of destitute of propriety of conduct be without greatness

kurals.translit: Ozhukkaththin Olkaar Uravor Izhukkaththin / Edham Patupaak Karindhu
kurals.pope: The strong of soul no jot abate of 'strict decorum's' laws, Knowing that 'due decorum's' breach foulest disgrace will cause
kurals.drew: Those firm in mind will not slacken in their observance of the proprieties of life, knowing, as they do, the misery that flows from the transgression from them

kurals.translit: Ozhukkaththin Eydhuvar Menmai Izhukkaththin / Eydhuvar Eydhaap Pazhi
kurals.pope: 'Tis source of dignity when 'true decorum' is preserved; Who break 'decorum's' rules endure e'en censures undeserved
kurals.drew: From propriety of conduct men obtain greatness; from impropriety comes insufferable disgrace

kurals.translit: Nandrikku Viththaakum Nallozhukkam Theeyozhukkam / Endrum Itumpai Tharum
kurals.pope: 'Decorum true' observed a seed of good will be;'Decorum's breach' will sorrow yield eternally
kurals.drew: Propriety of conduct is the seed of virtue; impropriety will ever cause sorrow

kurals.translit: Ozhukka Mutaiyavarkku Ollaave Theeya / Vazhukkiyum Vaayaar Solal
kurals.pope: It cannot be that they who 'strict decorum's' law fulfil, E'en in forgetful mood, should utter words of ill
kurals.drew: Those who study propriety of conduct will not speak evil, even forgetfully

kurals.translit: Ulakaththotu Otta Ozhukal Palakatrum / Kallaar Arivilaa Thaar
kurals.pope: Who know not with the world in harmony to dwell, May many things have learned, but nothing well
kurals.drew: Those who know not how to act agreeably to the world, though they have learnt many things, are still ignorant

kurals.translit: Piranporulaal Pettozhukum Pedhaimai Gnaalaththu / Aramporul Kantaarkan Il
kurals.pope: Who laws of virtue and possession's rights have known, Indulge no foolish love of her by right another's own
kurals.drew: The folly of desiring her who is the property of another will not be found in those who know (the attributes of) virtue and (the rights of) property

kurals.translit: Arankatai Nindraarul Ellaam Pirankatai / Nindraarin Pedhaiyaar Il
kurals.pope: No fools, of all that stand from virtue's pale shut out, Like those who longing lurk their neighbour's gate without
kurals.drew: Among all those who stand on the outside of virtue, there are no greater fools than those who stand outside their neighbour's door

kurals.translit: Vilindhaarin Verallar Mandra Thelindhaaril / Theemai Purindhu Ozhuku Vaar
kurals.pope: They're numbered with the dead, e'en while they live, -how otherwise?With wife of sure confiding friend who evil things devise
kurals.drew: Certainly they are no better than dead men who desire evil towards the wife of those who

kurals.translit: Enaiththunaiyar Aayinum Ennaam Thinaiththunaiyum / Theraan Piranil Pukal
kurals.pope: How great soe'er they be, what gain have they of life, Who, not a whit reflecting, seek a neighbour's wife
kurals.drew: However great one may be, what does it avail if, without at all considering his guilt, he goes unto the wife of another ?

kurals.translit: Elidhena Illirappaan Eydhumenj Gnaandrum / Viliyaadhu Nirkum Pazhi
kurals.pope: 'Mere triflel' saying thus, invades the home, so he ensuresA gain of guilt that deathless aye endures
kurals.drew: He who thinks lightly of going into the wife of another acquires guilt that will abide with him imperishably and for ever

kurals.translit: Pakaipaavam Achcham Pazhiyena Naankum / Ikavaavaam Illirappaan Kan
kurals.pope: Who home ivades, from him pass nevermore, Hatred and sin, fear, foul disgrace; these four
kurals.drew: Hatred, sin, fear, disgrace; these four will never leave him who goes in to his neighbour's wife

kurals.translit: Araniyalaan Ilvaazhvaan Enpaan Piraniyalaal / Penmai Nayavaa Thavan
kurals.pope: Who sees the wife, another's own, with no desiring eyeIn sure domestic bliss he dwelleth ever virtuously
kurals.drew: He who desires not the womanhood of her who should walk according to the will of another will be praised as a virtuous house-holder

kurals.translit: Piranmanai Nokkaadha Peraanmai Saandrorkku / Aranondro Aandra Vozhukku
kurals.pope: Manly excellence, that looks not on another's wife, Is not virtue merely, 'tis full 'propriety' of life
kurals.drew: That noble manliness which looks not at the wife of another is the virtue and dignity of the great

kurals.translit: Nalakkuriyaar Yaarenin Naamaneer Vaippin / Pirarkkuriyaal Tholdhoyaa Thaar
kurals.pope: Who 're good indeed, on earth begirt by ocean's gruesome tide?The men who touch not her that is another's bride
kurals.drew: Is it asked, "who are those who shall obtain good in this world surrounded by the terror-producing sea ?" Those who touch not the shoulder of her who belongs to another

kurals.translit: Aranvaraiyaan Alla Seyinum Piranvaraiyaal / Penmai Nayavaamai Nandru
kurals.pope: Though virtue's bounds he pass, and evil deeds hath wrought; At least, 'tis good if neighbour's wife he covet not
kurals.drew: Though a man perform no virtuous deeds and commit (every) vice, it will be well if he desire not the womanhood of her who is within the limit (of the house) of another

kurals.translit: Akazhvaaraith Thaangum Nilampolath Thammai / Ikazhvaarp Poruththal Thalai
kurals.pope: As earth bears up the men who delve into her breast, To bear with scornful men of virtues is the best
kurals.drew: To bear with those who revile us, just as the earth bears up those who dig it, is the first of virtues

kurals.translit: Poruththal Irappinai Endrum Adhanai / Maraththal Adhaninum Nandru
kurals.pope: Forgiving trespasses is good always; Forgetting them hath even higher praise;
kurals.drew: Bear with reproach even when you can retaliate; but to forget it will be still better than that

kurals.translit: Inmaiyul Inmai Virundhoraal Vanmaiyul / Vanmai Matavaarp Porai
kurals.pope: The sorest poverty is bidding guest unfed depart; The mightiest might to bear with men of foolish heart
kurals.drew: To neglect hospitality is poverty of poverty To bear with the ignorant is might of might

kurals.translit: Niraiyutaimai Neengaamai Ventin Poraiyutaimai / Potri Yozhukap Patum
kurals.pope: Seek'st thou honour never tarnished to retain; So must thou patience, guarding evermore, maintain
kurals.drew: If you desire that greatness should never leave, you preserve in your conduct the exercise of patience

kurals.translit: Oruththaarai Ondraaka Vaiyaare Vaippar / Poruththaaraip Ponpor Podhindhu
kurals.pope: Who wreak their wrath as worthless are despised; Who patiently forbear as gold are prized
kurals.drew: (The wise) will not at all esteem the resentful They will esteem the patient just as the gold which they lay up with care

kurals.translit: Oruththaarkku Orunaalai Inpam Poruththaarkkup / Pondrun Thunaiyum Pukazh
kurals.pope: Who wreak their wrath have pleasure for a day; Who bear have praise till earth shall pass away
kurals.drew: The pleasure of the resentful continues for a day The praise of the patient will continue until (the final destruction of) the world

kurals.translit: Thiranalla Tharpirar Seyyinum Nonondhu / Aranalla Seyyaamai Nandru
kurals.pope: Though others work thee ill, thus shalt thou blessing reap; Grieve for their sin, thyself from vicious action keep
kurals.drew: Though others inflict injuries on you, yet compassionating the evil (that will come upon them) it will be well not to do them anything contrary to virtue

kurals.translit: Mikudhiyaan Mikkavai Seydhaaraith Thaandham / Thakudhiyaan Vendru Vital
kurals.pope: With overweening pride when men with injuries assail, By thine own righteous dealing shalt thou mightily prevail
kurals.drew: Let a man by patience overcome those who through pride commit excesses

kurals.translit: Thurandhaarin Thooimai Utaiyar Irandhaarvaai / Innaachchol Norkir Pavar
kurals.pope: They who transgressors' evil words endureWith patience, are as stern ascetics pure
kurals.drew: Those who bear with the uncourteous speech of the insolent are as pure as the ascetics

kurals.translit: Unnaadhu Norpaar Periyar Pirarsollum / Innaachchol Norpaarin Pin
kurals.pope: Though 'great' we deem the men that fast and suffer pain, Who others' bitter words endure, the foremost place obtain
kurals.drew: Those who endure abstinence from food are great, next to those who endure the uncourteous speech of others

kurals.translit: Ozhukkaaraak Kolka Oruvandhan Nenjaththu / Azhukkaaru Ilaadha Iyalpu
kurals.pope: As 'strict decorum's' laws, that all men bind, Let each regard unenvying grace of mind
kurals.drew: Let a man esteem that disposition which is free from envy in the same manner as propriety of conduct

kurals.translit: Vizhuppetrin Aqdhoppadhu Illaiyaar Maattum / Azhukkaatrin Anmai Perin
kurals.pope: If man can learn to envy none on earth,'Tis richest gift, -beyond compare its worth
kurals.drew: Amongst all attainable excellences there is none equal to that of being free from envy towords others

kurals.translit: Aranaakkam Ventaadhaan Enpaan Piranaakkam / Penaadhu Azhukkarup Paan
kurals.pope: Nor wealth nor virtue does that man desire 'tis plain, Whom others' wealth delights not, feeling envious pain
kurals.drew: Of him who instead of rejoicing in the wealth of others, envies it, it will be said "he neither desires virtue not wealth."

kurals.translit: Azhukkaatrin Allavai Seyyaar Izhukkaatrin / Edham Patupaakku Arindhu
kurals.pope: The wise through envy break not virtue's laws, Knowing ill-deeds of foul disgrace the cause
kurals.drew: (The wise) knowing the misery that comes from transgression will not through envy commit unrighteous deeds

kurals.translit: Azhukkaaru Utaiyaarkku Adhusaalum Onnaar / Vazhukka�yum Keteen Padhu
kurals.pope: Envy they have within! Enough to seat their fate!Though foemen fail, envy can ruin consummate
kurals.drew: To those who cherish envy that is enough Though free from enemies that (envy) will bring destruction

kurals.translit: Kotuppadhu Azhukkaruppaan Sutram Utuppadhooum / Unpadhooum Indrik Ketum
kurals.pope: Who scans good gifts to others given with envious eye, His kin, with none to clothe or feed them, surely die
kurals.drew: He who is envious at a gift (made to another) will with his relations utterly perish destitute of food and rainment

kurals.translit: Avviththu Azhukkaaru Utaiyaanaich Cheyyaval / Thavvaiyaik Kaatti Vitum
kurals.pope: From envious man good fortune's goddess turns away, Grudging him good, and points him out misfortune's prey
kurals.drew: Lakshmi envying (the prosperity) of the envious man will depart and introduce him to her sister

kurals.translit: Azhukkaaru Enaoru Paavi Thiruchchetruth / Theeyuzhi Uyththu Vitum
kurals.pope: Envy, embodied ill, incomparable bane, Good fortune slays, and soul consigns to fiery pain
kurals.drew: Envy will destroy (a man's) wealth (in his world) and drive him into the pit of fire (in the world to come.)

kurals.translit: Avviya Nenjaththaan Aakkamum Sevviyaan / Ketum Ninaikkap Patum
kurals.pope: To men of envious heart, when comes increase of joy, Or loss to blameless men, the 'why' will thoughtful hearts employ
kurals.drew: The wealth of a man of envious mind and the poverty of the righteous will be pondered

kurals.translit: Azhukkatru Akandraarum Illai Aqdhuillaar / Perukkaththil Theerndhaarum Il
kurals.pope: No envious men to large and full felicity attain; No men from envy free have failed a sure increase to gain
kurals.drew: Never have the envious become great; never have those who are free from envy been without greatness

kurals.translit: Natuvindri Nanporul Veqkin Kutipondrik / Kutramum Aange Tharum
kurals.pope: With soul unjust to covet others' well-earned store, Brings ruin to the home, to evil opes the door
kurals.drew: If a man departing from equity covet the property (of others), at that very time will his family be destroyed and guilt be incurred

kurals.translit: Patupayan Veqkip Pazhippatuva Seyyaar / Natuvanmai Naanu Pavar
kurals.pope: Through lust of gain, no deeds that retribution bring, Do they, who shrink with shame from every unjust thing
kurals.drew: Those who blush at the want of equity will not commit disgraceful acts through desire of the profit that may be gained

kurals.translit: Sitrinpam Veqki Aranalla Seyyaare / Matrinpam Ventu Pavar
kurals.pope: No deeds of ill, misled by base desire, Do they, whose souls to other joys aspire
kurals.drew: Those who desire the higher pleasures (of heaven) will not act unjustly through desire of the trifling joy. (in this life.)

kurals.translit: Ilamendru Veqkudhal Seyyaar Pulamvendra / Punmaiyil Kaatchi Yavar
kurals.pope: Men who have conquered sense, with sight from sordid vision freed, Desire not other's goods, e'en in the hour of sorest need
kurals.drew: The wise who have conquered their senses and are free from crime, will not covet (the things of others), with the thought "we are destitute."

kurals.translit: Aqki Akandra Arivennaam Yaarmaattum / Veqki Veriya Seyin
kurals.pope: What gain, though lore refined of amplest reach he learn, His acts towards all mankind if covetous desire to folly turn
kurals.drew: What is the advantage of extensive and accurate knowledge if a man through covetousness act senselessly towards all ?

kurals.translit: Arulveqki Aatrinkan Nindraan Porulveqkip / Pollaadha Soozhak Ketum
kurals.pope: Though, grace desiring, he in virtue's way stand strong, He's lost who wealth desires, and ponders deeds of wrong
kurals.drew: If he, who through desire of the virtue of kindness abides in the domestic state ie, the path in which it may be obtained, covet (the property of others) and think of evil methods (to obtain it), he will perish

kurals.translit: Ventarka Veqkiyaam Aakkam Vilaivayin / Maantar Karidhaam Payan
kurals.pope: Seek not increase by greed of gain acquired; That fruit matured yields never good desired
kurals.drew: Desire not the gain of covetousness In the enjoyment of its fruits there is no glory

kurals.translit: Aqkaamai Selvaththirku Yaadhenin Veqkaamai / Ventum Pirankaip Porul
kurals.pope: What saves prosperity from swift decline?Absence of lust to make another's cherished riches thine
kurals.drew: If it is weighed, "what is the indestructibility of wealth," it is freedom from covetousness

kurals.translit: Aranarindhu Veqkaa Arivutaiyaarch Cherum / Thiranarin Thaange Thiru
kurals.pope: Good fortune draws anigh in helpful time of need, To him who, schooled in virtue, guards his soul from greed
kurals.drew: Lakshmi, knowing the manner (in which she may approach) will immediately come to those wise men who, knowing that it is virtue, covet not the property of others

kurals.translit: Iraleenum Ennaadhu Veqkin Viraleenum / Ventaamai Ennunj Cherukku
kurals.pope: From thoughtless lust of other's goods springs fatal ill, Greatness of soul that covets not shall triumph still
kurals.drew: To covet (the wealth of another) regardless of consequences will bring destruction That greatness (of mind) which covets not will give victory

kurals.translit: Arangooraan Alla Seyinum Oruvan / Purangooraan Endral Inidhu
kurals.pope: Though virtuous words his lips speak not, and all his deeds are illIf neighbour he defame not, there's good within him still
kurals.drew: Though one do not even speak of virtue and live in sin, it will be well if it be said of him "he does not backbite."

kurals.translit: Aranazheei Allavai Seydhalin Theedhe / Puranazheeip Poiththu Nakai
kurals.pope: Than he who virtue scorns, and evil deeds performs, more vile, Is he that slanders friend, then meets him with false smile
kurals.drew: To smile deceitfully (in another's presence) after having reviled him to his destruction (behind his back) is a greater evil than the commission of (every other) sin and the destruction of (every) virtue

kurals.translit: Purangoorip Poiththuyir Vaazhdhalin Saadhal / Arangootrum Aakkath Tharum
kurals.pope: 'Tis greater gain of virtuous good for man to die, Than live to slander absent friend, and falsely praise when nigh
kurals.drew: Death rather than life will confer upon the deceitful backbiter the profit which (the treatises on) virtue point out

kurals.translit: Kannindru Kannarach Chollinum Sollarka / Munnindru Pinnokkaach Chol
kurals.pope: In presence though unkindly words you speak, say notIn absence words whose ill result exceeds your thought
kurals.drew: Though you speak without kindness before another's face speak not in his absence words which regard not the evil subsequently resulting from it

kurals.translit: Aranjollum Nenjaththaan Anmai Puranjollum / Punmaiyaar Kaanap Patum
kurals.pope: The slanderous meanness that an absent friend defames,'This man in words owns virtue, not in heart,' proclaims
kurals.drew: The emptiness of that man's mind who (merely) praises virtue will be seen from the meanness of reviling another behind his back

kurals.translit: Piranpazhi Kooruvaan Thanpazhi Yullum / Thirandherindhu Koorap Patum
kurals.pope: Who on his neighbours' sins delights to dwell, The story of his sins, culled out with care, the world will tell
kurals.drew: The character of the faults of that man who publishes abroad the faults of others will be sought out and published

kurals.translit: Pakachchollik Kelirp Pirippar Nakachcholli / Natpaatal Thetraa Thavar
kurals.pope: With friendly art who know not pleasant words to say, Speak words that sever hearts, and drive choice friends away
kurals.drew: Those who know not to live in friendship with amusing conversation will by back-biting estrange even their relatives

kurals.translit: Thunniyaar Kutramum Thootrum Marapinaar / Ennaikol Edhilaar Maattu
kurals.pope: Whose nature bids them faults of closest friends proclaimWhat mercy will they show to other men's good name
kurals.drew: What will those not do to strangers whose nature leads them to publish abroad the faults of their intimate friends ?

kurals.translit: Arannokki Aatrungol Vaiyam Purannokkip / Punsol Uraippaan Porai
kurals.pope: 'Tis charity, I ween, that makes the earth sustain their loadWho, neighbours' absence watching, tales or slander tell abroad
kurals.drew: The world through charity supports the weight of those who reproach others observing their absence

kurals.translit: Edhilaar Kutrampol Thangutrang Kaankirpin / Theedhunto Mannum Uyirkku
kurals.pope: If each his own, as neighbours' faults would scan, Could any evil hap to living man
kurals.drew: If they observed their own faults as they observe the faults of others, would any evil happen to men ?

kurals.translit: Pallaar Muniyap Payanila Solluvaan / Ellaarum Ellap Patum
kurals.pope: Words without sense, while chafe the wise, Who babbles, him will all despise
kurals.drew: He who to the disgust of many speaks useless things will be despised by all

kurals.translit: Payanila Pallaarmun Sollal Nayanila / Nattaarkan Seydhalir Reedhu
kurals.pope: Words without sense, where many wise men hear, to pourThan deeds to friends ungracious done offendeth more
kurals.drew: To speak useless things in the presence of many is a greater evil than to do unkind things towards friends

kurals.translit: Nayanilan Enpadhu Sollum Payanila / Paarith Thuraikkum Urai
kurals.pope: Diffusive speech of useless words proclaimsA man who never righteous wisdom gains
kurals.drew: That conversation in which a man utters forth useless things will say of him "he is without virtue."

kurals.translit: Nayansaaraa Nanmaiyin Neekkum Payansaaraap / Panpilsol Pallaa Rakaththu
kurals.pope: Unmeaning, worthless words, said to the multitude, To none delight afford, and sever men from good
kurals.drew: The words devoid of profit or pleasure which a man speaks will, being inconsistent with virtue,

kurals.translit: Seermai Sirappotu Neengum Payanila / Neermai Yutaiyaar Solin
kurals.pope: Gone are both fame and boasted excellence, When men of worth speak of words devoid of sense
kurals.drew: If the good speak vain words their eminence and excellence will leave them

kurals.translit: Payanil Sol Paaraattu Vaanai / Makanenal Makkat Padhati Yenal
kurals.pope: Who makes display of idle words' inanity, Call him not man, -chaff of humanity
kurals.drew: Call not him a man who parades forth his empty words Call him the chaff of men

kurals.translit: Nayanila Sollinunj Cholluka Saandror / Payanila Sollaamai Nandru
kurals.pope: Let those who list speak things that no delight afford,'Tis good for men of worth to speak no idle word
kurals.drew: Let the wise if they will, speak things without excellence; it will be well for them not to speak useless things

kurals.translit: Arumpayan Aayum Arivinaar Sollaar / Perumpayan Illaadha Sol
kurals.pope: The wise who weigh the worth of every utterance, Speak none but words of deep significance
kurals.drew: The wise who seek after rare pleasures will not speak words that have not much weight in them

kurals.translit: Poruldheerndha Pochchaandhunj Chollaar Maruldheerndha / Maasaru Kaatchi Yavar
kurals.pope: The men of vision pure, from wildering folly free, Not e'en in thoughtless hour, speak words of vanity
kurals.drew: Those wise men who are without faults and are freed from ignorance will not even forgetfully speak things that profit not

kurals.translit: Solluka Sollir Payanutaiya Sollarka / Sollir Payanilaach Chol
kurals.pope: If speak you will, speak words that fruit afford, If speak you will, speak never fruitless word
kurals.drew: Speak what is useful, and speak not useless words

kurals.translit: Theevinaiyaar Anjaar Vizhumiyaar Anjuvar / Theevinai Ennum Serukku
kurals.pope: With sinful act men cease to feel the dread of ill within, The excellent will dread the wanton pride of cherished sin
kurals.drew: Those who have experience of evil deeds will not fear, but the excellent will fear the pride of sin

kurals.translit: Theeyavai Theeya Payaththalaal Theeyavai / Theeyinum Anjap Patum
kurals.pope: Since evils new from evils ever grow, Evil than fire works out more dreaded woe
kurals.drew: Because evil produces evil, therefore should evil be feared more than fire

kurals.translit: Arivinul Ellaan Thalaiyenpa Theeya / Seruvaarkkum Seyyaa Vital
kurals.pope: Even to those that hate make no return of ill; So shalt thou wisdom's highest law, 'tis said, fulfil
kurals.drew: So shalt thou wisdom's highest law, 'tis said, fulfil

kurals.translit: Marandhum Piranketu Soozharka Soozhin / Aranjoozham Soozhndhavan Ketu
kurals.pope: Though good thy soul forget, plot not thy neighbour's fall, Thy plans shall 'virtue's Power' by ruin to thyself forestall
kurals.drew: Even though forgetfulness meditate not the ruin of another Virtue will meditate the ruin of him who thus meditates

kurals.translit: Ilan Endru Theeyavai Seyyarka / Seyyin Ilanaakum Matrum Peyarththu
kurals.pope: Make not thy poverty a plea for ill; Thy evil deeds will make thee poorer still
kurals.drew: Commit not evil, saying, "I am poor": if you do, you will become poorer still

kurals.translit: Theeppaala Thaanpirarkan Seyyarka Noippaala / Thannai Atalventaa Thaan
kurals.pope: What ranks as evil spare to do, if thou would'st shunAffliction sore through ill to thee by others done
kurals.drew: Let him not do evil to others who desires not that sorrows should pursue him

kurals.translit: Enaippakai Yutraarum Uyvar Vinaippakai / Veeyaadhu Pinsendru Atum
kurals.pope: From every enmity incurred there is to 'scape, a way; The wrath of evil deeds will dog men's steps, and slay
kurals.drew: However great be the enmity men have incurred they may still live The enmity of sin will incessantly pursue and kill

kurals.translit: Theeyavai Seydhaar Ketudhal Nizhaldhannai / Veeyaadhu Atiurain Thatru
kurals.pope: Man's shadow dogs his steps where'er he wends; Destruction thus on sinful deeds attends
kurals.drew: Destruction will dwell at the heels of those who commit evil even as their shadow that leaves them not

kurals.translit: Thannaiththaan Kaadhala Naayin Enaiththondrum / Thunnarka Theevinaip Paal
kurals.pope: Beware, if to thyself thyself is dear, Lest thou to aught that ranks as ill draw near
kurals.drew: If a man love himself, let him not commit any sin however small

kurals.translit: Arungetan Enpadhu Arika Marungotith / Theevinai Seyyaan Enin
kurals.pope: The man, to devious way of sin that never turned aside, From ruin rests secure, whatever ills betide
kurals.drew: Know ye that he is freed from destruction who commits no evil, going to neither side of the right path

kurals.translit: Kaimmaaru Ventaa Katappaatu Maarimaattu / En Aatrung Kollo Ulaku
kurals.pope: Duty demands no recompense; to clouds of heaven, By men on earth, what answering gift is given
kurals.drew: Benevolence seeks not a return. What does the world give back to the clouds ?

kurals.translit: Thaalaatrith Thandha Porulellaam Thakkaarkku / Velaanmai Seydhar Poruttu
kurals.pope: The worthy say, when wealth rewards their toil-spent hours, For uses of beneficence alone 'tis ours
kurals.drew: All the wealth acquired with perseverance by the worthy is for the exercise of benevolence

kurals.translit: Puththe Lulakaththum Eentum Peralaridhe / Oppuravin Nalla Pira
kurals.pope: To 'due beneficence' no equal good we know, Amid the happy gods, or in this world below
kurals.drew: It is difficult to obtain another good equal to benevolence either in this world or in that of the gods

kurals.translit: Oththa Tharavon Uyirvaazhvaan Matraiyaan / Seththaarul Vaikkap Patum
kurals.pope: Who knows what's human life's befitting grace, He lives; the rest 'mongst dead men have their place
kurals.drew: He truly lives who knows (and discharges) the proper duties (of benevolence) He who knows them not will be reckoned among the dead

kurals.translit: Ooruni Neernirain Thatre Ulakavaam / Perari Vaalan Thiru
kurals.pope: The wealth of men who love the 'fitting way,' the truly wise, Is as when water fills the lake that village needs supplies
kurals.drew: The wealth of that man of eminent knowledge who desires to exercise the benevolence approved of by the world, is like the full waters of a city-tank

kurals.translit: Payanmaram Ulloorp Pazhuththatraal Selvam / Nayanutai Yaankan Patin
kurals.pope: A tree that fruits in th' hamlet's central mart, Is wealth that falls to men of liberal heart
kurals.drew: The wealth of a man (possessed of the virtue) of benevolence is like the ripening of a fruitful tree in the midst of a town

kurals.translit: Marundhaakith Thappaa Maraththatraal Selvam / Perundhakai Yaankan Patin
kurals.pope: Unfailing tree that healing balm distils from every part, Is ample wealth that falls to him of large and noble heart
kurals.drew: If wealth be in the possession of a man who has the great excellence (of benevolence), it is like a tree which as a medicine is an infallible cure for disease

kurals.translit: Itanil Paruvaththum Oppuravirku Olkaar / Katanari Kaatchi Yavar
kurals.pope: E'en when resources fall, they weary not of 'kindness due,'-They to whom Duty's self appears in vision true
kurals.drew: The wise who know what is duty will not scant their benevolence even when they are without wealth

kurals.translit: Nayanutaiyaan Nalkoorndhaa Naadhal Seyumneera / Seyyaadhu Amaikalaa Vaaru
kurals.pope: The kindly-hearted man is poor in this alone, When power of doing deeds of goodness he finds none
kurals.drew: The poverty of a benevolent man, is nothing but his inability to exercise the same

kurals.translit: Oppuravi Naalvarum Ketenin Aqdhoruvan / Vitrukkol Thakka Thutaiththu
kurals.pope: Though by 'beneficence,' the loss of all should come,'Twere meet man sold himself, and bought it with the sum
kurals.drew: If it be said that loss will result from benevolence, such loss is worth being procured even by the sale of one's self

kurals.translit: Variyaarkkondru Eevadhe Eekaimar Rellaam / Kuriyedhirppai Neera Thutaiththu
kurals.pope: Call that a gift to needy men thou dost dispense, All else is void of good, seeking for recompense
kurals.drew: To give to the destitute is true charity All other gifts have the nature of (what is done for) a measured return

kurals.translit: Nallaaru Eninum Kolaldheedhu Melulakam / Illeninum Eedhale Nandru
kurals.pope: Though men declare it heavenward path, yet to receive is ill; Though upper heaven were not, to give is virtue still
kurals.drew: To beg is evil, even though it were said that it is a good path (to heaven) To give is good, even though it were said that those who do so cannot obtain heaven

kurals.translit: Ilanennum Evvam Uraiyaamai Eedhal / Kulanutaiyaan Kanne Yula
kurals.pope: 'I've nought' is ne'er the high-born man's reply; He gives to those who raise themselves that cry
kurals.drew: (Even in a low state) not to adopt the mean expedient of saying "I have nothing," but to give, is the characteristic of the mad of noble birth

kurals.translit: Innaadhu Irakkap Patudhal Irandhavar / Inmukang Kaanum Alavu
kurals.pope: The suppliants' cry for aid yields scant delight, Until you see his face with grateful gladness bright
kurals.drew: To see men begging from us in disagreeable, until we see their pleasant countenance

kurals.translit: Aatruvaar Aatral Pasiaatral Appasiyai / Maatruvaar Aatralin Pin
kurals.pope: 'Mid devotees they're great who hunger's pangs sustain, Who hunger's pangs relieve a higher merit gain
kurals.drew: The power of those who perform penance is the power of enduring hunger It is inferior to the power of those who remove the hunger (of others)

kurals.translit: Atraar Azhipasi Theerththal Aqdhoruvan / Petraan Porulvaip Puzhi
kurals.pope: Let man relieve the wasting hunger men endure; For treasure gained thus finds he treasure-house secure
kurals.drew: The removal of the killing hunger of the poor is the place for one to lay up his wealth

kurals.translit: Paaththoon Mareei Yavanaip Pasiyennum / Theeppini Theental Aridhu
kurals.pope: Whose soul delights with hungry men to share his meal, The hand of hunger's sickness sore shall never feel
kurals.drew: The fiery disease of hunger shall never touch him who habitually distributes his food to others

kurals.translit: Eeththuvakkum Inpam Ariyaarkol Thaamutaimai / Vaiththizhakkum Vanka Navar
kurals.pope: Delight of glad'ning human hearts with gifts do they not know.Men of unpitying eye, who hoard their wealth and lose it so
kurals.drew: Do the hard-eyed who lay up and lose their possessions not know the happiness which springs from the pleasure of giving ?

kurals.translit: Iraththalin Innaadhu Mandra Nirappiya / Thaame Thamiyar Unal
kurals.pope: They keep their garners full, for self alone the board they spread;-'Tis greater pain, be sure, than begging daily bread
kurals.drew: Solitary and unshared eating for the sake of filling up one's own riches is certainly much more

kurals.translit: Saadhalin Innaadha Thillai Inidhadhooum / Eedhal Iyaiyaak Katai
kurals.pope: 'Tis bitter pain to die, 'Tis worse to live.For him who nothing finds to give
kurals.drew: Nothing is more unpleasant than death: yet even that is pleasant where charity cannot be exercised

kurals.translit: Eedhal Isaipata Vaazhdhal Adhuvalladhu / Oodhiyam Illai Uyirkku
kurals.pope: See that thy life the praise of generous gifts obtain; Save this for living man exists no real gain
kurals.drew: Give to the poor and live with praise There is no greater profit to man than that

kurals.translit: Uraippaar Uraippavai Ellaam Irappaarkkondru / Eevaarmel Nirkum Pukazh
kurals.pope: The speech of all that speak agrees to crownThe men that give to those that ask, with fair renown
kurals.drew: Whatsoever is spoken in the world will abide as praise upon that man who gives alms to the poor

kurals.translit: Ondraa Ulakaththu Uyarndha Pukazhallaal / Pondraadhu Nirpadhon Ril
kurals.pope: Save praise alone that soars on high, Nought lives on earth that shall not die
kurals.drew: There is nothing that stands forth in the world imperishable, except fame, exalted in solitary greatness

kurals.translit: Nilavarai Neelpukazh Aatrin Pulavaraip / Potraadhu Puththel Ulaku
kurals.pope: If men do virtuous deeds by world-wide ample glory crowned, The heavens will cease to laud the sage for other gifts renowned
kurals.drew: If one has acquired extensive fame within the limits of this earth, the world of the Gods will no longer praise those sages who have attained that world

kurals.translit: Naththampol Ketum Uladhaakum Saakkaatum / Viththakark Kallaal Aridhu
kurals.pope: Loss that is gain, and death of life's true bliss fulfilled, Are fruits which only wisdom rare can yield
kurals.drew: Prosperity to the body of fame, resulting in poverty to the body of flesh and the stability to the former arising from the death of the latter, are achievable only by the wise

kurals.translit: Thondrin Pukazhotu Thondruka Aqdhilaar / Thondralin Thondraamai Nandru
kurals.pope: If man you walk the stage, appear adorned with glory's grace; Save glorious you can shine, 'twere better hide your face
kurals.drew: If you are born (in this world), be born with qualities conductive to fame From those who are destitute of them it will be better not to be born

kurals.translit: Pukazhpata Vaazhaadhaar Thannovaar Thammai / Ikazhvaarai Novadhu Evan?
kurals.pope: If you your days will spend devoid of goodly fame, When men despise, why blame them? You've yourself to blame
kurals.drew: Why do those who cannot live with praise, grieve those who despise them, instead of grieving themselves for their own inability

kurals.translit: Vasaiyenpa Vaiyaththaark Kellaam Isaiyennum / Echcham Peraaa Vitin
kurals.pope: Fame is virtue's child, they say; if, then, You childless live, you live the scorn of men
kurals.drew: Not to beget fame will be esteemed a disgrace by the wise in this world

kurals.translit: Vasaiyilaa Vanpayan Kundrum Isaiyilaa / Yaakkai Poruththa Nilam
kurals.pope: The blameless fruits of fields' increase will dwindle down, If earth the burthen bear of men without renown
kurals.drew: The ground which supports a body without fame will diminish in its rich produce

kurals.translit: Vasaiyozhiya Vaazhvaare Vaazhvaar Isaiyozhiya / Vaazhvaare Vaazhaa Thavar
kurals.pope: Who live without reproach, them living men we deem; Who live without renown, live not, though living men they seem
kurals.drew: Those live who live without disgrace Those who live without fame live not

kurals.translit: Arutchelvam Selvaththul Selvam Porutchelvam / Pooriyaar Kannum Ula
kurals.pope: Wealth 'mid wealth is wealth 'kindliness'; Wealth of goods the vilest too possess
kurals.drew: The wealth of kindness is wealth of wealth, in as much as the wealth of property is possessed by the basest of men
