kurals.drew: The measure of his wealth will quickly perish, whose liberality weighs not the measure of his property

kurals.translit: Pakalvellum Kookaiyaik Kaakkai Ikalvellum / Vendharkku Ventum Pozhudhu
kurals.pope: A crow will conquer owl in broad daylight; The king that foes would crush, needs fitting time to fight
kurals.drew: A crow will overcome an owl in the day time; so the king who would conquer his enemy must have (a suitable) time

kurals.translit: Paruvaththotu Otta Ozhukal Thiruvinaith / Theeraamai Aarkkung Kayiru
kurals.pope: The bond binds fortune fast is ordered effort made, Strictly observant still of favouring season's aid
kurals.drew: Acting at the right season, is a cord that will immoveably bind success (to a king)

kurals.translit: Aruvinai Yenpa Ulavo Karuviyaan / Kaalam Arindhu Seyin
kurals.pope: Can any work be hard in very fact, If men use fitting means in timely act
kurals.drew: Is there anything difficult for him to do, who acts, with (the right) instruments at the right time ?

kurals.translit: Gnaalam Karudhinung Kaikootung Kaalam / Karudhi Itaththaar Seyin
kurals.pope: The pendant world's dominion may be won, In fitting time and place by action done
kurals.drew: Though (a man) should meditate (the conquest of) the world, he may accomplish it if he acts in the right time, and at the right place

kurals.translit: Kaalam Karudhi Iruppar Kalangaadhu / Gnaalam Karudhu Pavar
kurals.pope: Who think the pendant world itself to subjugate, With mind unruffled for the fitting time must wait
kurals.drew: They who thoughtfully consider and wait for the (right) time (for action), may successfully meditate (the conquest of) the world

kurals.translit: Ookka Mutaiyaan Otukkam Porudhakar / Thaakkarkup Perun Thakaiththu
kurals.pope: The men of mighty power their hidden energies repress, As fighting ram recoils to rush on foe with heavier stress
kurals.drew: The self-restraint of the energetic (while waiting for a suitable opportunity), is like the drawing back of a fighting-ram in order to butt

kurals.translit: Pollena Aange Puramveraar Kaalampaarththu / Ulverppar Olli Yavar
kurals.pope: The glorious once of wrath enkindled make no outward show, At once; they bide their time, while hidden fires within them glow
kurals.drew: The wise will not immediately and hastily shew out their anger; they will watch their time, and restrain it within

kurals.translit: Serunaraik Kaanin Sumakka Iruvarai / Kaanin Kizhakkaam Thalai
kurals.pope: If foes' detested form they see, with patience let them bear; When fateful hour at last they spy,- the head lies there
kurals.drew: If one meets his enemy, let him show him all respect, until the time for his destruction is come; when that is come, his head will be easily brought low

kurals.translit: Eydhar Kariyadhu Iyaindhakkaal Annilaiye / Seydhar Kariya Seyal
kurals.pope: When hardest gain of opportunity at last is won, With promptitude let hardest deed be done
kurals.drew: If a rare opportunity occurs, while it lasts, let a man do that which is rarely to be accomplished (but for such an opportunity)

kurals.translit: Kokkokka Koompum Paruvaththu Matradhan / Kuththokka Seerththa Itaththu
kurals.pope: As heron stands with folded wing, so wait in waiting hour; As heron snaps its prey, when fortune smiles, put forth your power
kurals.drew: At the time when one should use self-control, let him restrain himself like a heron; and, let him like it, strike, when there is a favourable opportunity

kurals.translit: Thotangarka Evvinaiyum Ellarka Mutrum / Itanganta Pinal Ladhu
kurals.pope: Begin no work of war, depise no foe, Till place where you can wholly circumvent you know
kurals.drew: Let not (a king) despise (an enemy), nor undertake any thing (against him), until he has obtained (a suitable) place for besieging him

kurals.translit: Muranserndha Moimpi Navarkkum Aranserndhaam / Aakkam Palavun Tharum
kurals.pope: Though skill in war combine with courage tried on battle-field, The added gain of fort doth great advantage yield
kurals.drew: Even to those who are men of power and expedients, an attack in connection with a fortification will yield many advantages

kurals.translit: Aatraarum Aatri Atupa Itanarindhu / Potraarkan Potrich Cheyin
kurals.pope: E'en weak ones mightily prevail, if place of strong defence, They find, protect themselves, and work their foes offence
kurals.drew: Even the powerless will become powerful and conquer, if they select a proper field (of action), and guard themselves, while they make war on their enemies

kurals.translit: Enniyaar Ennam Izhappar Itanarindhu / Thunniyaar Thunnich Cheyin
kurals.pope: The foes who thought to triumph, find their thoughts were vain, If hosts advance, seize vantage ground, and thence the fight maintain
kurals.drew: If they who draw near (to fight) choose a suitable place to approach (their enemy), the latter, will have to relinquish the thought which they once entertained, of conquering them

kurals.translit: Netumpunalul Vellum Mudhalai Atumpunalin / Neengin Adhanaip Pira
kurals.pope: The crocodile prevails in its own flow of water wide, If this it leaves, 'tis slain by anything beside
kurals.drew: In deep water, a crocodile will conquer (all other animals); but if it leave the water, other animals will conquer it

kurals.translit: Katalotaa Kaalval Netundher Katalotum / Naavaayum Otaa Nilaththu
kurals.pope: The lofty car, with mighty wheel, sails not o'er watery main, The boat that skims the sea, runs not on earth's hard plain
kurals.drew: Wide chariots, with mighty wheels, will not run on the ocean; neither will ships that the traverse ocean, move on the earth

kurals.translit: Anjaamai Allaal Thunaiventaa Enjaamai / Enni Itaththaal Seyin
kurals.pope: Save their own fearless might they need no other aid, If in right place they fight, all due provision made
kurals.drew: You will need no other aid than fearlessness, if you thoroughly reflect (on what you are to do), and select (a suitable) place for your operations

kurals.translit: Sirupataiyaan Sellitam Serin Urupataiyaan / Ookkam Azhindhu Vitum
kurals.pope: If lord of army vast the safe retreat assailOf him whose host is small, his mightiest efforts fail
kurals.drew: The power of one who has a large army will perish, if he goes into ground where only a small army can act

kurals.translit: Sirainalanum Seerum Ilareninum Maandhar / Urainilaththotu Ottal Aridhu
kurals.pope: Though fort be none, and store of wealth they lack,'Tis hard a people's homesteads to attack
kurals.drew: It is a hazardous thing to attack men in their own country, although they may neither have power nor a good fortress

kurals.translit: Kaalaazh Kalaril Nariyatum Kannanjaa / Velaal Mukaththa Kaliru
kurals.pope: The jackal slays, in miry paths of foot-betraying fen, The elephant of fearless eye and tusks transfixing armed men
kurals.drew: A fox can kill a fearless, warrior-faced elephant, if it go into mud in which its legs sink down

kurals.translit: Aramporul Inpam Uyirachcham Naankin / Thirandherindhu Therap Patum
kurals.pope: How treats he virtue, wealth and pleasure? How, when life's at stake, Comports himself? This four-fold test of man will full assurance make
kurals.drew: Let (a minister) be chosen, after he has been tried by means of these four things, viz,-his virtue, (love of) money, (love of) sexual pleasure, and tear of (losing) life

kurals.translit: Kutippirandhu Kutraththin Neengi Vatuppariyum / Naanutaiyaan Sutte Thelivu
kurals.pope: Of noble race, of faultless worth, of generous prideThat shrinks from shame or stain; in him may king confide
kurals.drew: (The king's) choice should (fall) on him, who is of good family, who is free from faults, and who has the modesty which fears the wounds (of sin)

kurals.translit: Ariyakatru Aasatraar Kannum Theriyungaal / Inmai Aridhe Veliru
kurals.pope: Though deeply learned, unflecked by fault, 'tis rare to see, When closely scanned, a man from all unwisdom free
kurals.drew: When even men, who have studied the most difficult works, and who are free from faults, are (carefully) examined, it is a rare thing to find them without ignorance

kurals.translit: Kunamnaatik Kutramum Naati Avatrul / Mikainaati Mikka Kolal
kurals.pope: Weigh well the good of each, his failings closely scan, As these or those prevail, so estimate the man
kurals.drew: Let (a king) consider (a man's) good qualities, as well as his faults, and then judge (of his character) by that which prevails

kurals.translit: Perumaikkum Enaich Chirumaikkum Thaththam / Karumame Kattalaik Kal
kurals.pope: Of greatness and of meanness too, The deeds of each are touchstone true
kurals.drew: A man's deeds are the touchstone of his greatness and littleness

kurals.translit: Atraaraith Therudhal Ompuka Matravar / Patrilar Naanaar Pazhi
kurals.pope: Beware of trusting men who have no kith of kin; No bonds restrain such men, no shame deters from sin
kurals.drew: Let (a king) avoid choosing men who have no relations; such men have no attachment, and thereforehave no fear of crime

kurals.translit: Kaadhanmai Kandhaa Arivariyaarth Therudhal / Pedhaimai Ellaan Tharum
kurals.pope: By fond affection led who trusts in men of unwise soul, Yields all his being up to folly's blind control
kurals.drew: Yields all his being up to folly's blind control

kurals.translit: Theraan Piranaith Thelindhaan Vazhimurai / Theeraa Itumpai Tharum
kurals.pope: Who trusts an untried stranger, brings disgrace, Remediless, on all his race
kurals.drew: Sorrow that will not leave even his posterity will come upon him chooses a stranger whose character he has not known

kurals.translit: Therarka Yaaraiyum Theraadhu Therndhapin / Theruka Therum Porul
kurals.pope: Trust no man whom you have not fully tried, When tested, in his prudence proved confide
kurals.drew: Let (a king) choose no one without previous consideration; after he has made his choice, let him unhesitatingly select for each such duties as are appropriate

kurals.translit: Theraan Thelivum Thelindhaankan Aiyuravum / Theeraa Itumpai Tharum
kurals.pope: Trust where you have not tried, doubt of a friend to feel, Once trusted, wounds inflict that nought can heal
kurals.drew: To make choice of one who has not been examined, and to entertain doubts respecting one who has been chosen, will produce irremediable sorrow

kurals.translit: Nanmaiyum Theemaiyum Naati Nalampurindha / Thanmaiyaan Aalap Patum
kurals.pope: Who good and evil scanning, ever makes the good his joy; Such man of virtuous mood should king employ
kurals.drew: He should be employed (by a king), whose nature leads him to choose the good, after having weighed both the evil and the good in any undertaking

kurals.translit: Vaari Perukki Valampatuththu Utravai / Aaraaivaan Seyka Vinai
kurals.pope: Who swells the revenues, spreads plenty o'er the land, Seeks out what hinders progress, his the workman's hand
kurals.drew: Let him do (the king's) work who can enlarge the sources (of revenue), increase wealth and considerately prevent the accidents (which would destroy it)

kurals.translit: Anparivu Thetram Avaavinmai Innaankum / Nankutaiyaan Katte Thelivu
kurals.pope: A loyal love with wisdom, clearness, mind from avarice free; Who hath these four good gifts should ever trusted be
kurals.drew: Let the choice (of a king) fall upon him who largely possesses these four things, love, knowledge, a clear mind and freedom from covetousness

kurals.translit: Enaivakaiyaan Theriyak Kannum Vinaivakaiyaan / Veraakum Maandhar Palar
kurals.pope: Even when tests of every kind are multiplied, Full many a man proves otherwise, by action tried
kurals.drew: Even when (a king) has tried them in every possible way, there are many men who change, from the nature of the works (in which they may be employed)

kurals.translit: Arindhaatrich Cheykirpaarku Allaal Vinaidhaan / Sirandhaanendru Evarpaar Randru
kurals.pope: No specious fav'rite should the king's commission bear, But he that knows, and work performs with patient care
kurals.drew: (A king's) work can only be accomplished by a man of wisdom and patient endurance; it is not of a nature to be given to one from mere personal attachment

kurals.translit: Seyvaanai Naati Vinainaatik Kaalaththotu / Eydha Unarndhu Seyal
kurals.pope: Let king first ask, 'Who shall the deed perform?' and 'What the deed?'Of hour befitting both assured, let every work proceed
kurals.drew: Let (a king) act, after having considered the agent (whom he is to employ), the deed (he desires to do), and the time which is suitable to it

kurals.translit: Ithanai Ithanaal Ivanmutikkum Endraaindhu / Adhanai Avankan Vital
kurals.pope: 'This man, this work shall thus work out,' let thoughtful king command; Then leave the matter wholly in his servant's hand
kurals.drew: After having considered, "this man can accomplish this, by these means", let (the king) leave with him the discharge of that duty

kurals.translit: Vinaik Kurimai Naatiya Pindrai / Avanai Adharkuriya Naakach Cheyal
kurals.pope: As each man's special aptitude is known, Bid each man make that special work his own
kurals.drew: Having considered what work a man is fit for, let (the king) employ him in that work

kurals.translit: Vinaikkan Vinaiyutaiyaan Kenmaive Raaka / Ninaippaanai Neengum Thiru
kurals.pope: Fortune deserts the king who ill can bear, Informal friendly ways of men his tolls who share
kurals.drew: Prosperity will leave (the king) who doubts the friendship of the man who steadily labours in the discharge of his duties

kurals.translit: Naatorum Naatuka Mannan Vinaiseyvaan / Kotaamai Kotaa Thulaku
kurals.pope: Let king search out his servants' deeds each day; When these do right, the world goes rightly on its way
kurals.drew: Let a king daily examine the conduct of his servants; if they do not act crookedly, the world will not act crookedly

kurals.translit: Patratra Kannum Pazhaimaipaa Raattudhal / Sutraththaar Kanne Ula
kurals.pope: When wealth is fled, old kindness still to show, Is kindly grace that only kinsmen know
kurals.drew: Even when (a man's) property is all gone, relatives will act towards him with their accustomed (kindness)

kurals.translit: Virupparaach Chutram Iyaiyin Arupparaa / Aakkam Palavum Tharum
kurals.pope: The gift of kin's unfailing love bestowsMuch gain of good, like flower that fadeless blows
kurals.drew: If (a man's) relatives remain attached to him with unchanging love, it will be a source of everincreasing wealth

kurals.translit: Alavalaa Villaadhaan Vaazhkkai Kulavalaak / Kotindri Neernirain Thatru
kurals.pope: His joy of life who mingles not with kinsmen gathered round, Is lake where streams pour in, with no encircling bound
kurals.drew: The wealth of one who does not mingle freely with his relatives, will be like the filling of water in a

kurals.translit: Sutraththaal Sutrap Pataozhukal Selvandhaan / Petraththaal Petra Payan
kurals.pope: The profit gained by wealth's increase, Is living compassed round by relatives in peace
kurals.drew: To live surrounded by relatives, is the advantage to be derived from the acquisition of wealth

kurals.translit: Kotuththalum Insolum Aatrin Atukkiya / Sutraththaal Sutrap Patum
kurals.pope: Who knows the use of pleasant words, and liberal gifts can give, Connections, heaps of them, surrounding him shall live
kurals.drew: He will be surrounded by numerous relatives who manifests generosity and affability

kurals.translit: Perungotaiyaan Penaan Vekuli Avanin / Marungutaiyaar Maanilaththu Il
kurals.pope: Than one who gifts bestows and wrath restrains, Through the wide world none larger following gains
kurals.drew: No one, in all the world, will have so many relatives (about him), as he who makes large gift, and does not give way to anger

kurals.translit: Kaakkai Karavaa Karaindhunnum Aakkamum / Annanee Raarkke Ula
kurals.pope: The crows conceal not, call their friends to come, then eat; Increase of good such worthy ones shall meet
kurals.drew: The crows do not conceal (their prey), but will call out for others (to share with them) while they eat it; wealth will be with those who show a similar disposition (towards their relatives)

kurals.translit: Podhunokkaan Vendhan Varisaiyaa Nokkin / Adhunokki Vaazhvaar Palar
kurals.pope: Where king regards not all alike, but each in his degree,'Neath such discerning rule many dwell happily
kurals.drew: Many relatives will live near a king, when they observe that he does not look on all alike, but that he looks on each man according to his merit

kurals.translit: Thamaraakik Thatrurandhaar Sutram Amaraamaik / Kaaranam Indri Varum
kurals.pope: Who once were his, and then forsook him, as beforeWill come around, when cause of disagreement is no more
kurals.drew: Those who have been friends and have afterwards forsaken him, will return and join themselves (to him), when the cause of disagreement is not to be found in him

kurals.translit: Uzhaippirindhu Kaaranaththin Vandhaanai Vendhan / Izhaith Thirundhu Ennik Kolal
kurals.pope: Who causeless went away, then to return, for any cause, ask leave; The king should sift their motives well, consider, and receive
kurals.drew: When one may have left him, and for some cause has returned to him, let the king fulfil the object (for which he has come back) and thoughtfully receive him again

kurals.translit: Irandha Vekuliyin Theedhe Sirandha / Uvakai Makizhchchiyir Sorvu
kurals.pope: 'Tis greater ill, it rapture of o'erweening gladness to the soulBring self-forgetfulness than if transcendent wrath control
kurals.drew: More evil than excessive anger, is forgetfulness which springs from the intoxication of great joy

kurals.translit: Pochchaappuk Kollum Pukazhai Arivinai / Nichcha Nirappuk Kon Raangu
kurals.pope: Perpetual, poverty is death to wisdom of the wise; When man forgets himself his glory dies
kurals.drew: Forgetfulness will destroy fame, even as constant poverty destroys knowledge

kurals.translit: Pochchaappaark Killai Pukazhmai Adhuulakaththu / Eppaalnoo Lorkkum Thunivu
kurals.pope: 'To self-oblivious men no praise'; this ruleDecisive wisdom sums of every school
kurals.drew: Thoughtlessness will never acquire fame; and this tenet is upheld by all treatises in the world

kurals.translit: Achcha Mutaiyaarkku Aranillai Aangillai / Pochchaap Putaiyaarkku Nanku
kurals.pope: 'To cowards is no fort's defence'; e'en soThe self-oblivious men no blessing know
kurals.drew: Just as the coward has no defence (by whatever fortifications ha may be surrounded), so the thoughtless has no good (whatever advantages he may possess)

kurals.translit: Munnurak Kaavaadhu Izhukkiyaan Thanpizhai / Pinnooru Irangi Vitum
kurals.pope: To him who nought foresees, recks not of anything, The after woe shall sure repentance bring
kurals.drew: The thoughtless man, who provides not against the calamities that may happen, will afterwards repent for his fault

kurals.translit: Izhukkaamai Yaarmaattum Endrum Vazhukkaamai / Vaayin Adhuvoppadhu Il
kurals.pope: Towards all unswerving, ever watchfulness of soul retain, Where this is found there is no greater gain
kurals.drew: There is nothing comparable with the possession of unfailing thoughtfulness at all times; and towards all persons

kurals.translit: Ariyaendru Aakaadha Illaipoch Chaavaak / Karuviyaal Potrich Cheyin
kurals.pope: Though things are arduous deemed, there's nought may not be won, When work with mind's unslumbering energy and thought is done
kurals.drew: There is nothing too difficult to be accomplished, if a man set about it carefully, with unflinching endeavour

kurals.translit: Pukazhndhavai Potrich Cheyalventum Seyyaadhu / Ikazhndhaarkku Ezhumaiyum Il
kurals.pope: Let things that merit praise thy watchful soul employ; Who these despise attain through sevenfold births no joy
kurals.drew: Let (a man) observe and do these things which have been praised (by the wise); if he neglects and fails to perform them, for him there will be no (happiness) throughout the seven births

kurals.translit: Ikazhchchiyin Kettaarai Ulluka Thaandham / Makizhchchiyin Maindhurum Pozhdhu
kurals.pope: Think on the men whom scornful mind hath brought to nought, When exultation overwhelms thy wildered thought
kurals.drew: Let (a king) think of those who have been ruined by neglect, when his mind is elated with joy

kurals.translit: Ulliyadhu Eydhal Elidhuman Matrundhaan / Ulliyadhu Ullap Perin
kurals.pope: 'Tis easy what thou hast in mind to gain, If what thou hast in mind thy mind retain
kurals.drew: It is easy for (one) to obtain whatever he may think of, if he can again think of it

kurals.translit: Orndhukan Notaadhu Iraipurindhu Yaarmaattum / Therndhusey Vaqdhe Murai
kurals.pope: Search out, to no one favour show; with heart that justice lovesConsult, then act; this is the rule that right approves
kurals.drew: To examine into (the crimes which may be committed), to show no favour (to any one), to desire to act with impartiality towards all, and to inflict (such punishments) as may be wisely resolved on,

kurals.translit: Vaanokki Vaazhum Ulakellaam Mannavan / Kol Nokki Vaazhung Kuti
kurals.pope: All earth looks up to heav'n whence raindrops fall; All subjects look to king that ruleth all
kurals.drew: When there is rain, the living creation thrives; and so when the king rules justly, his subjects thrive

kurals.translit: Andhanar Noorkum Araththirkum Aadhiyaai / Nindradhu Mannavan Kol
kurals.pope: Learning and virtue of the sages spring, From all-controlling sceptre of the king
kurals.drew: The sceptre of the king is the firm support of the Vedas of the Brahmin, and of all virtues therein described

kurals.translit: Kutidhazheeik Kolochchum Maanila Mannan / Atidhazheei Nirkum Ulaku
kurals.pope: Whose heart embraces subjects all, lord over mighty landWho rules, the world his feet embracing stands
kurals.drew: The world will constantly embrace the feet of the great king who rules over his subjects with love

kurals.translit: Iyalpulik Kolochchum Mannavan Naatta / Peyalum Vilaiyulum Thokku
kurals.pope: Where king, who righteous laws regards, the sceptre wields, There fall the showers, there rich abundance crowns the fields
kurals.drew: Rain and plentiful crops will ever dwell together in the country of the king who sways his sceptre with justice

kurals.translit: Velandru Vendri Tharuvadhu Mannavan / Koladhooung Kotaa Thenin
kurals.pope: Not lance gives kings the victory, But sceptre swayed with equity
kurals.drew: It is not the javelin that gives victory, but the king's sceptre, if it do no injustice

kurals.translit: Iraikaakkum Vaiyakam Ellaam Avanai / Muraikaakkum Muttaach Cheyin
kurals.pope: The king all the whole realm of earth protects; And justice guards the king who right respects
kurals.drew: The king defends the whole world; and justice, when administered without defect, defends the king

kurals.translit: Enpadhaththaan Oraa Muraiseyyaa Mannavan / Thanpadhaththaan Thaane Ketum
kurals.pope: Hard of access, nought searching out, with partial handThe king who rules, shall sink and perish from the land
kurals.drew: The king who gives not facile audience (to those who approach him), and who does not examine and pass judgment (on their complaints), will perish in disgrace

kurals.translit: Kutipurang Kaaththompik Kutram Katidhal / Vatuvandru Vendhan Thozhil
kurals.pope: Abroad to guard, at home to punish, bringsNo just reproach; 'tis work assigned to kings
kurals.drew: In guarding his subjects (against injury from others), and in preserving them himself; to punish crime

kurals.translit: Kolaiyir Kotiyaarai Vendhoruththal Paingoozh / Kalaikat Tadhanotu Ner
kurals.pope: By punishment of death the cruel to restrain, Is as when farmer frees from weeds the tender grain
kurals.drew: For a king to punish criminals with death, is like pulling up the weeds in the green corn

kurals.translit: Kolaimerkon Taarir Kotidhe Alaimerkontu / Allavai Seydhozhukum Vendhu
kurals.pope: Than one who plies the murderer's trade, more cruel is the kingWho all injustice works, his subjects harassing
kurals.drew: The king who gives himself up to oppression and acts unjustly (towards his subjects) is more cruel than the man who leads the life of a murderer

kurals.translit: Velotu Nindraan Ituven Radhupolum / Kolotu Nindraan Iravu
kurals.pope: As 'Give' the robber cries with lance uplift, So kings with sceptred hand implore a gift
kurals.drew: The request (for money) of him who holds the sceptre is like the word of a highway robber who stands with a weapon in hand and says "give up your wealth"

kurals.translit: Naatorum Naati Muraiseyyaa Mannavan / Naatorum Naatu Ketum
kurals.pope: Who makes no daily search for wrongs, nor justly rules, that kingDoth day by day his realm to ruin bring
kurals.drew: The country of the king who does not daily examine into the wrongs done and distribute justice, will daily fall to ruin

kurals.translit: Koozhung Kutiyum Orungizhakkum Kolkotich / Choozhaadhu Seyyum Arasu
kurals.pope: Whose rod from right deflects, who counsel doth refuse, At once his wealth and people utterly shall lose
kurals.drew: The king, who, without reflecting (on its evil consequences), perverts justice, will lose at once both his wealth and his subjects

kurals.translit: Allarpattu Aatraadhu Azhudhakan Neerandre / Selvaththaith Theykkum Patai
kurals.pope: His people's tears of sorrow past endurance, are not theySharp instruments to wear the monarch's wealth away
kurals.drew: Will not the tears, shed by a people who cannot endure the oppression which they suffer (from their king), become a saw to waste away his wealth ?

kurals.translit: Mannarkku Mannudhal Sengonmai Aqdhindrel / Mannaavaam Mannark Koli
kurals.pope: To rulers' rule stability is sceptre right; When this is not, quenched is the rulers' light
kurals.drew: Righteous government gives permanence to (the fame of) kings; without that their fame will have no endurance

kurals.translit: Thuliyinmai Gnaalaththirku Etratre Vendhan / Aliyinmai Vaazhum Uyirkku
kurals.pope: As lack of rain to thirsty lands beneath, Is lack of grace in kings to all that breathe
kurals.drew: As is the world without rain, so live a people whose king is without kindness

kurals.translit: Inmaiyin Innaadhu Utaimai Muraiseyyaa / Mannavan Korkeezhp Patin
kurals.pope: To poverty it adds a sharper sting, To live beneath the sway of unjust king
kurals.drew: Property gives more sorrow than poverty, to those who live under the sceptre of a king without justice

kurals.translit: Muraikoti Mannavan Seyyin Uraikoti / Ollaadhu Vaanam Peyal
kurals.pope: Where king from right deflecting, makes unrighteous gain, The seasons change, the clouds pour down no rain
kurals.drew: If the king acts contrary to justice, rain will become unseasonable, and the heavens will withhold their showers

kurals.translit: Aapayan Kundrum Arudhozhilor Noolmarappar / Kaavalan Kaavaan Enin
kurals.pope: Where guardian guardeth not, udder of kine grows dry, And Brahmans' sacred lore will all forgotten lie
kurals.drew: If the guardian (of the country) neglects to guard it, the produce of the cows will fail, and the men of six duties viz, the Brahmins will forget the vedas

kurals.translit: Thakkaangu Naatith Thalaichchellaa Vannaththaal / Oththaangu Oruppadhu Vendhu
kurals.pope: Who punishes, investigation made in due degree, So as to stay advance of crime, a king is he
kurals.drew: He is a king who having equitably examined (any injustice which has been brought to his notice), suitably punishes it, so that it may not be again committed

kurals.translit: Katidhochchi Mella Erika Netidhaakkam / Neengaamai Ventu Pavar
kurals.pope: For length of days with still increasing joys on Heav'n who call, Should raise the rod with brow severe, but let it gently fall
kurals.drew: Let the king, who desires that his prosperity may long remain, commence his preliminary enquires with strictness, and then punish with mildness

kurals.translit: Veruvandha Seydhozhukum Vengola Naayin / Oruvandham Ollaik Ketum
kurals.pope: Where subjects dread of cruel wrongs endure, Ruin to unjust king is swift and sure
kurals.drew: The cruel-sceptred king, who acts so as to put his subjects in fear, will certainly and quickly come to ruin

kurals.translit: Iraikatiyan Endruraikkum Innaachchol Vendhan / Uraikatuki Ollaik Ketum
kurals.pope: 'Ah! cruel is our king', where subjects sadly say, His age shall dwindle, swift his joy of life decay
kurals.drew: The king who is spoken of as cruel will quickly perish; his life becoming shortened

kurals.translit: Arunjevvi Innaa Mukaththaan Perunjelvam / Peeykan Tannadhu Utaiththu
kurals.pope: Whom subjects scarce may see, of harsh forbidding countenance; His ample wealth shall waste, blasted by demon's glance
kurals.drew: The great wealth of him who is difficult of access and possesses a sternness of countenance, is like that which has been obtained by a devil

kurals.translit: Katunjollan Kannilan Aayin Netunjelvam / Neetindri Aange Ketum
kurals.pope: The tyrant, harsh in speach and hard of eye, His ample joy, swift fading, soon shall die
kurals.drew: The abundant wealth of the king whose words are harsh and whose looks are void of kindness, will instantly perish instead of abiding long, with him

kurals.translit: Katumozhiyum Kaiyikandha Thantamum Vendhan / Atumuran Theykkum Aram
kurals.pope: Harsh words and punishments severe beyond the right, Are file that wears away the monarch's conquering might
kurals.drew: Severe words and excessive punishments will be a file to waste away a king's power for destroying (his enemies)

kurals.translit: Inaththaatri Ennaadha Vendhan Sinaththaatrich / Cheerir Sirukum Thiru
kurals.pope: Who leaves the work to those around, and thinks of it no more; If he in wrathful mood reprove, his prosperous days are o'er
kurals.drew: The prosperity of that king will waste away, who without reflecting (on his affairs himself), commits them to his ministers, and (when a failure occurs) gives way to anger, and rages against them

kurals.translit: Seruvandha Pozhdhir Siraiseyyaa Vendhan / Veruvandhu Veydhu Ketum
kurals.pope: Who builds no fort whence he may foe defy, In time of war shall fear and swiftly die
kurals.drew: The king who has not provided himself with a place of defence, will in times of war be seized with fear and quickly perish

kurals.translit: Kallaarp Pinikkum Katungol Adhuvalladhu / Illai Nilakkup Porai
kurals.pope: Tyrants with fools their counsels share:Earth can no heavier burthen bear
kurals.drew: The earth bears up no greater burden than ignorant men whom a cruel sceptre attaches to itself (as the ministers of its evil deeds)

kurals.translit: Kannottam Ennum Kazhiperung Kaarikai / Unmaiyaan Untiv Vulaku
kurals.pope: Since true benignity, that grace exceeding great, residesIn kingly souls, world in happy state abides
kurals.drew: The world exists through that greatest ornament (of princes), a gracious demeanour

kurals.translit: Kannottath Thulladhu Ulakiyal Aqdhilaar / Unmai Nilakkup Porai
kurals.pope: The world goes on its wonted way, since grace benign is there; All other men are burthen for the earth to bear
kurals.drew: The prosperity of the world springs from the kindliness, the existence of those who have no (kindliness) is a burden to the earth

kurals.translit: Panennaam Paatarku Iyaipindrel Kanennaam / Kannottam Illaadha Kan
kurals.pope: Where not accordant with the song, what use of sounding chordsWhat gain of eye that no benignant light affords
kurals.drew: Of what avail is a song if it be inconsistent with harmony ? what is the use of eyes which possess no kindliness

kurals.translit: Ulapol Mukaththevan Seyyum Alavinaal / Kannottam Illaadha Kan
kurals.pope: The seeming eye of face gives no expressive light, When not with duly meted kindness bright
kurals.drew: Beyond appearing to be in the face, what good do they do, those eyes in which is no well-regulated kindness ?

kurals.translit: Kannirku Anikalam Kannottam Aqdhindrel / Punnendru Unarap Patum
kurals.pope: Benignity is eyes' adorning grace; Without it eyes are wounds disfiguring face
kurals.drew: Kind looks are the ornaments of the eyes; without these they will be considered (by the wise) to be merely two sores

kurals.translit: Manno Tiyaindha Maraththanaiyar Kanno / Tiyaindhukan Notaa Thavar
kurals.pope: Whose eyes 'neath brow infixed diffuse no rayOf grace; like tree in earth infixed are they
kurals.drew: They resemble the trees of the earth, who although they have eyes, never look kindly (on others)

kurals.translit: Kannottam Illavar Kannilar Kannutaiyaar / Kannottam Inmaiyum Il
kurals.pope: Eyeless are they whose eyes with no benignant lustre shine; Who've eyes can never lack the light of grace benign
kurals.drew: Men without kind looks are men without eyes; those who (really) have eyes are also not devoid of kind looks

kurals.translit: Karumam Sidhaiyaamal Kannota Vallaarkku / Urimai Utaiththiv Vulaku
kurals.pope: Who can benignant smile, yet leave no work undone; By them as very own may all the earth be won
kurals.drew: The world is theirs (kings) who are able to show kindness, without injury to their affairs, (administration of justice)

kurals.translit: Oruththaatrum Panpinaar Kannumkan Notip / Poruththaatrum Panpe Thalai
kurals.pope: To smile on those that vex, with kindly face, Enduring long, is most excelling grace
kurals.drew: Patiently to bear with, and show kindness to those who grieve us, is the most excellent of all dispositions

kurals.translit: Peyakkantum Nanjun Tamaivar Nayaththakka / Naakarikam Ventu Pavar
kurals.pope: They drink with smiling grace, though poison interfused they see, Who seek the praise of all-esteemed courtesy
kurals.drew: Those who desire (to cultivate that degree of) urbanity which all shall love, even after swallowing the poison served to them by their friends, will be friendly with them

kurals.translit: Otrum Uraisaandra Noolum Ivaiyirantum / Thetrenka Mannavan Kan
kurals.pope: These two: the code renowned and spies, In these let king confide as eyes
kurals.drew: Let a king consider as his eyes these two things, a spy and a book (of laws) universally esteemed

kurals.translit: Ellaarkkum Ellaam Nikazhpavai Egngnaandrum / Vallaridhal Vendhan Thozhil
kurals.pope: Each day, of every subject every deed,'Tis duty of the king to learn with speed
kurals.drew: 'Tis duty of the king to learn with speed

kurals.translit: Otrinaan Otrip Poruldheriyaa Mannavan / Kotrang Kolakkitandhadhu Il
kurals.pope: By spies who spies, not weighing things they bring, Nothing can victory give to that unwary king
kurals.drew: There is no way for a king to obtain conquests, who knows not the advantage of discoveries made by a spy

kurals.translit: Vinaiseyvaar Thamsutram Ventaadhaar Endraangu / Anaivaraiyum Aaraaivadhu Otru
kurals.pope: His officers, his friends, his enemies, All these who watch are trusty spies
kurals.drew: He is a spy who watches all men, to wit, those who are in the king's employment, his relatives, and his enemies

kurals.translit: Kataaa Uruvotu Kannanjaadhu Yaantum / Ukaaamai Valladhe Otru
kurals.pope: Of unsuspected mien and all-unfearing eyes, Who let no secret out, are trusty spies
kurals.drew: A spy is one who is able to assume an appearance which may create no suspicion (in the minds of others), who fears no man's face, and who never reveals (his purpose)

kurals.translit: Thurandhaar Pativaththa Raaki Irandhaaraaindhu / Enseyinum Sorviladhu Otru
kurals.pope: As monk or devotee, through every hindrance making way, A spy, whate'er men do, must watchful mind display
kurals.drew: He is a spy who, assuming the appearance of an ascetic, goes into (whatever place he wishes), examines into (all, that is needful), and never discovers himself, whatever may be done to him

kurals.translit: Maraindhavai Ketkavar Raaki Arindhavai / Aiyappaatu Illadhe Otru
kurals.pope: A spy must search each hidden matter out, And full report must render, free from doubt
kurals.drew: A spy is one who is able to discover what is hidden and who retains no doubt concerning what he has known

kurals.translit: Otrotrith Thandha Porulaiyum Matrumor / Otrinaal Otrik Kolal
kurals.pope: Spying by spies, the things they tellTo test by other spies is well
kurals.drew: Let not a king receive the information which a spy has discovered and made known to him, until he has examined it by another spy

kurals.translit: Otrer Runaraamai Aalka Utanmoovar / Sotrokka Therap Patum
kurals.pope: One spy must not another see: contrive it so; And things by three confirmed as truth you know
kurals.drew: Let a king employ spies so that one may have no knowledge of the other; and when the information of three agrees together, let him receive it

kurals.translit: Sirappariya Otrinkan Seyyarka Seyyin / Purappatuththaan Aakum Marai
kurals.pope: Reward not trusty spy in others' sight, Or all the mystery will come to light
kurals.drew: Let not a king publicly confer on a spy any marks of his favour; if he does, he will divulge his own secret

kurals.translit: Utaiyar Enappatuvadhu Ookkam Aqdhillaar / Utaiyadhu Utaiyaro Matru
kurals.pope: 'Tis energy gives men o'er that they own a true control; They nothing own who own not energy of soul
kurals.drew: Energy makes out the man of property; as for those who are destitute of it, do they (really) possess what they possess ?

kurals.translit: Ullam Utaimai Utaimai Porulutaimai / Nillaadhu Neengi Vitum
kurals.pope: The wealth of mind man owns a real worth imparts, Material wealth man owns endures not, utterly departs
kurals.drew: The possession of (energy of) mind is true property; the possession of wealth passes away and abides not

kurals.translit: Aakkam Izhandhemendru Allaavaar Ookkam / Oruvandham Kaiththutai Yaar
kurals.pope: 'Lost is our wealth,' they utter not this cry distressed, The men of firm concentred energy of soul possessed
kurals.drew: They who are possessed of enduring energy will not trouble themselves, saying, "we have lost our property."

kurals.translit: Aakkam Adharvinaaich Chellum Asaivilaa / Ookka Mutaiyaa Nuzhai
kurals.pope: The man of energy of soul inflexible, Good fortune seeks him out and comes a friend to dwell
kurals.drew: Wealth will find its own way to the man of unfailing energy

kurals.translit: Vellath Thanaiya Malarneettam Maandhardham / Ullath Thanaiyadhu Uyarvu
kurals.pope: With rising flood the rising lotus flower its stem unwinds; The dignity of men is measured by their minds
kurals.drew: The stalks of water-flowers are proportionate to the depth of water; so is men's greatness proportionate to their minds

kurals.translit: Ulluva Thellaam Uyarvullal Matradhu / Thallinun Thallaamai Neerththu
kurals.pope: Whate'er you ponder, let your aim be loftly still, Fate cannot hinder always, thwart you as it will
kurals.drew: In all that a king thinks of, let him think of his greatness; and if it should be thrust from him (by fate), it will have the nature of not being thrust from him

kurals.translit: Sidhaivitaththu Olkaar Uravor Pudhaiyampir / Pattuppaa Toondrung Kaliru
kurals.pope: The men of lofty mind quail not in ruin's fateful hour, The elephant retains his dignity mind arrows' deadly shower
kurals.drew: The strong minded will not faint, even when all is lost; the elephant stands firm, even when wounded by a shower of arrows

kurals.translit: Ullam Ilaadhavar Eydhaar Ulakaththu / Valliyam Ennunj Cherukku
kurals.pope: The soulless man can never gainTh' ennobling sense of power with men
kurals.drew: Those who have no (greatness of) mind, will not acquire the joy of saying in the world, "we have excercised liaberality"

kurals.translit: Pariyadhu Koorngottadhu Aayinum Yaanai / Veruum Pulidhaak Kurin
kurals.pope: Huge bulk of elephant with pointed tusk all armed, When tiger threatens shrinks away alarmed
kurals.drew: Although the elephant has a large body, and a sharp tusk, yet it fears the attack of the tiger

kurals.translit: Uramoruvarku Ulla Verukkaiaq Thillaar / Marammakka Laadhale Veru
kurals.pope: Firmness of soul in man is real excellance; Others are trees, their human form a mere pretence
kurals.drew: Energy is mental wealth; those men who are destitute of it are only trees in the form of men

kurals.translit: Kutiyennum Kundraa Vilakkam Matiyennum / Maasoora Maaindhu Ketum
kurals.pope: Of household dignity the lustre beaming bright, Flickers and dies when sluggish foulness dims its light
kurals.drew: By the darkness, of idleness, the indestructible lamp of family (rank) will be extinguished

kurals.translit: Matiyai Matiyaa Ozhukal Kutiyaik / Kutiyaaka Ventu Pavar
kurals.pope: Let indolence, the death of effort, die, If you'd uphold your household's dignity
kurals.drew: Let those, who desire that their family may be illustrious, put away all idleness from their conduct

kurals.translit: Matimatik Kontozhukum Pedhai Pirandha / Kutimatiyum Thanninum Mundhu
kurals.pope: Who fosters indolence within his breast, the silly elf!The house from which he springs shall perish ere himself
kurals.drew: The (lustre of the) family of the ignorant man, who acts under the influence of destructive laziness will perish, even before he is dead

kurals.translit: Kutimatindhu Kutram Perukum Matimatindhu / Maanta Ugnatri Lavarkku
kurals.pope: His family decays, and faults unheeded thrive, Who, sunk in sloth, for noble objects doth not strive
kurals.drew: Family (greatness) will be destroyed, and faults will increase, in those men who give way to laziness, and put forth no dignified exertions

kurals.translit: Netuneer Maravi Matidhuyil Naankum / Ketuneeraar Kaamak Kalan
kurals.pope: Delay, oblivion, sloth, and sleep: these fourAre pleasure-boat to bear the doomed to ruin's shore
kurals.drew: Procrastination, forgetfulness, idleness, and sleep, these four things, form the vessel which is desired by those destined to destruction

kurals.translit: Patiyutaiyaar Patramaindhak Kannum Matiyutaiyaar / Maanpayan Eydhal Aridhu
kurals.pope: Though lords of earth unearned possessions gain, The slothful ones no yield of good obtain
kurals.drew: It is a rare thing for the idle, even when possessed of the riches of kings who ruled over the whole earth, to derive any great benefit from it

kurals.translit: Itipurindhu Ellunj Chol Ketpar / Matipurindhu Maanta Ugnatri Lavar
kurals.pope: Who hug their sloth, nor noble works attempt, Shall bear reproofs and words of just contempt
kurals.drew: Those who through idleness, and do not engage themselves in dignified exertion, will subject

kurals.translit: Matimai Kutimaikkan Thangindhan Onnaarkku / Atimai Pukuththi Vitum
kurals.pope: If sloth a dwelling find mid noble family, Bondsmen to them that hate them shall they be
kurals.drew: If idleness take up its abode in a king of high birth, it will make him a slave of his enemies

kurals.translit: Kutiyaanmai Yulvandha Kutram Oruvan / Matiyaanmai Maatrak Ketum
kurals.pope: Who changes slothful habits savesHimself from all that household rule depraves
kurals.drew: When a man puts away idleness, the reproach which has come upon himself and his family will disappear

kurals.translit: Matiyilaa Mannavan Eydhum Atiyalandhaan / Thaaaya Thellaam Orungu
kurals.pope: The king whose life from sluggishness is rid, Shall rule o'er all by foot of mighty god bestrid
kurals.drew: The king who never gives way to idleness will obtain entire possession of (the whole earth) passed over by him who measured (the worlds) with His foot

kurals.translit: Arumai Utaiththendru Asaavaamai Ventum / Perumai Muyarsi Tharum
kurals.pope: Say not, 'Tis hard', in weak, desponding hour, For strenuous effort gives prevailing power
kurals.drew: Yield not to the feebleness which says, "this is too difficult to be done"; labour will give the greatness (of mind) which is necessary (to do it)

kurals.translit: Vinaikkan Vinaiketal Ompal Vinaikkurai / Theerndhaarin Theerndhandru Ulaku
kurals.pope: In action be thou, 'ware of act's defeat; The world leaves those who work leave incomplete
kurals.drew: Take care not to give up exertion in the midst of a work; the world will abandon those who abandon their unfinished work

kurals.translit: Thaalaanmai Ennum Thakaimaikkan Thangitre / Velaanmai Ennunj Cherukku
kurals.pope: In strenuous effort doth resideThe power of helping others: noble pride
kurals.drew: The lustre of munificence will dwell only with the dignity of laboriousness or efforts

kurals.translit: Thaalaanmai Illaadhaan Velaanmai Petikai / Vaalaanmai Polak Ketum
kurals.pope: Beneficent intent in men by whom no strenuous work is wrought, Like battle-axe in sexless being's hand availeth nought
kurals.drew: The liberality of him, who does not labour, will fail, like the manliness of a hermaphrodite, who has a sword in its hand

kurals.translit: Inpam Vizhaiyaan Vinaivizhaivaan Thankelir / Thunpam Thutaiththoondrum Thoon
kurals.pope: Whose heart delighteth not in pleasure, but in action finds delight, He wipes away his kinsmen's grief and stands the pillar of their might
kurals.drew: He who desires not pleasure, but desires labour, will be a pillar to sustain his relations, wiping away their sorrows

kurals.translit: Muyarsi Thiruvinai Aakkum Muyatrinmai / Inmai Pukuththi Vitum
kurals.pope: Effort brings fortune's sure increase, Its absence brings to nothingness
kurals.drew: Labour will produce wealth; idleness will bring poverty

kurals.translit: Matiyulaal Maamukati Enpa Matiyilaan / Thaalulaan Thaamaraiyi Naal
kurals.pope: In sluggishness is seen misfortune's lurid form, the wise declare; Where man unslothful toils, she of the lotus flower is there
kurals.drew: They say that the black Mudevi (the goddess of adversity) dwells with laziness, and the Latchmi (the goddess of prosperity) dwells with the labour of the industrious

kurals.translit: Poriyinmai Yaarkkum Pazhiyandru Arivarindhu / Aalvinai Inmai Pazhi
kurals.pope: 'Tis no reproach unpropitious fate should ban; But not to do man's work is foul disgrace to man
kurals.drew: Adverse fate is no disgrace to any one; to be without exertion and without knowing what should be known, is disgrace

kurals.translit: Theyvaththaan Aakaa Theninum Muyarsidhan / Meyvaruththak Kooli Tharum
kurals.pope: Though fate-divine should make your labour vain; Effort its labour's sure reward will gain
kurals.drew: Although it be said that, through fate, it cannot be attained, yet labour, with bodily exertion, will yield its reward

kurals.translit: Oozhaiyum Uppakkam Kaanpar Ulaivindrith / Thaazhaadhu Ugnatru Pavar
kurals.pope: Who strive with undismayed, unfaltering mind, At length shall leave opposing fate behind
kurals.drew: They who labour on, without fear and without fainting will see even fate (put) behind their back

kurals.translit: Itukkan Varungaal Nakuka Adhanai / Atuththoorvadhu Aqdhoppa Thil
kurals.pope: Smile, with patient, hopeful heart, in troublous hour; Meet and so vanquish grief; nothing hath equal power
kurals.drew: If troubles come, laugh; there is nothing like that, to press upon and drive away sorrow

kurals.translit: Vellath Thanaiya Itumpai Arivutaiyaan / Ullaththin Ullak Ketum
kurals.pope: Though sorrow, like a flood, comes rolling on, When wise men's mind regards it,- it is gone
kurals.drew: A flood of troubles will be overcome by the (courageous) thought which the minds of the wise will entertain, even in sorrow

kurals.translit: Itumpaikku Itumpai Patuppar Itumpaikku / Itumpai Pataaa Thavar
kurals.pope: Who griefs confront with meek, ungrieving heart, From them griefs, put to grief, depart
kurals.drew: They give sorrow to sorrow, who in sorrow do not suffer sorrow

kurals.translit: Matuththavaa Yellaam Pakatannaan Utra / Itukkan Itarppaatu Utaiththu
kurals.pope: Like bullock struggle on through each obstructed way; From such an one will troubles, troubled, roll away
kurals.drew: Troubles will vanish (i.e., will be troubled) before the man who (struggles against difficulties) as a

kurals.translit: Atukki Varinum Azhivilaan Utra / Itukkan Itukkat Patum
kurals.pope: When griefs press on, but fail to crush the patient heart, Then griefs defeated, put to grief, depart
kurals.drew: The troubles of that man will be troubled (and disappear) who, however thickly they may come upon him, does not abandon (his purpose)

kurals.translit: Atremendru Allar Patupavo Petremendru / Ompudhal Thetraa Thavar
kurals.pope: Who boasted not of wealth, nor gave it all their heart, Will not bemoan the loss, when prosperous days depart
kurals.drew: Will those men ever cry out in sorrow, "we are destitute" who, (in their prosperity), give not way to (undue desire) to keep their wealth

kurals.translit: Ilakkam Utampitumpaik Kendru Kalakkaththaik / Kaiyaaraak Kollaadhaam Mel
kurals.pope: 'Man's frame is sorrow's target', the noble mind reflects, Nor meets with troubled mind the sorrows it expects
kurals.drew: The great will not regard trouble as trouble, knowing that the body is the butt of trouble

kurals.translit: Inpam Vizhaiyaan Itumpai Iyalpenpaan / Thunpam Urudhal Ilan
kurals.pope: He seeks not joy, to sorrow man is born, he knows; Such man will walk unharmed by touch of human woes
kurals.drew: That man never experiences sorrow, who does not seek for pleasure, and who considers distress to be natural (to man)

kurals.translit: Inpaththul Inpam Vizhaiyaadhaan Thunpaththul / Thunpam Urudhal Ilan
kurals.pope: Mid joys he yields not heart to joys' controlMid sorrows, sorrow cannot touch his soul
kurals.drew: He does not suffer sorrow, in sorrow who does not look for pleasure in pleasure

kurals.translit: Innaamai Inpam Enakkolin Aakundhan / Onnaar Vizhaiyunj Chirappu
kurals.pope: Who pain as pleasure takes, he shall acquireThe bliss to which his foes in vain aspire
kurals.drew: The elevation, which even his enemies will esteem, will be gained by him, who regards pain as pleasure

kurals.chapter_en: The Office of Minister of state
kurals.translit: Karuviyum Kaalamum Seykaiyum Seyyum / Aruvinaiyum Maantadhu Amaichchu
kurals.pope: A minister is he who grasps, with wisdom large, Means, time, work's mode, and functions rare he must discharge
kurals.drew: The minister is one who can make an excellent choice of means, time, manner of execution, and the difficult undertaking (itself)

kurals.chapter_en: The Office of Minister of state
kurals.translit: Vankan Kutikaaththal Katraridhal Aalvinaiyotu / Aindhutan Maantadhu Amaichchu
kurals.pope: A minister must greatness own of guardian power, determined mind, Learn'd wisdom, manly effort with the former five combined
kurals.drew: The minister is one who in addition to the aforesaid five things excels in the possession of firmness,

kurals.chapter_en: The Office of Minister of state
kurals.translit: Piriththalum Penik Kolalum Pirindhaarp / Poruththalum Valla Thamaichchu
kurals.pope: A minister is he whose power can foes divide, Attach more firmly friends, of severed ones can heal the breaches wide
kurals.drew: The minister is one who can effect discord (among foes), maintain the good-will of his friends and restore to friendship those who have seceded (from him)

kurals.chapter_en: The Office of Minister of state
kurals.translit: Theridhalum Therndhu Seyalum Orudhalaiyaach / Chollalum Valladhu Amaichchu
kurals.pope: A minister has power to see the methods help afford, To ponder long, then utter calm conclusive word
kurals.drew: The minister is one who is able to comprehend (the whole nature of an undertaking), execute it in the best manner possible, and offer assuring advice (in time of necessity)

kurals.chapter_en: The Office of Minister of state
kurals.translit: Aranarindhu Aandramaindha Sollaanenj Gnaandrun / Thiranarindhaan Therchchith Thunai
kurals.pope: The man who virtue knows, has use of wise and pleasant wordsWith plans for every season apt, in counsel aid affords
kurals.drew: He is the best helper (of the king) who understanding the duties, of the latter, is by his special learning, able to tender the fullest advice, and at all times conversant with the best method (of

kurals.chapter_en: The Office of Minister of state
kurals.translit: Madhinutpam Noolotu Utaiyaarkku Adhinutpam / Yaavula Munnir Pavai
kurals.pope: When native subtilty combines with sound scholastic lore,'Tis subtilty surpassing all, which nothing stands before
kurals.drew: What (contrivances) are there so acute as to resist those who possess natural acuteness in addition to learning ?

kurals.chapter_en: The Office of Minister of state
kurals.translit: Seyarkai Arindhak Kataiththum Ulakaththu / Iyarkai Arindhu Seyal
kurals.pope: Though knowing all that books can teach, 'tis truest tactTo follow common sense of men in act
kurals.drew: Though you are acquainted with the (theoretical) methods (of performing an act), understand the ways of the world and act accordingly

kurals.chapter_en: The Office of Minister of state
kurals.translit: Arikondru Ariyaan Eninum Urudhi / Uzhaiyirundhaan Kooral Katan
kurals.pope: 'Tis duty of the man in place aloud to sayThe very truth, though unwise king may cast his words away
kurals.drew: Although the king be utterly ignorant, it is the duty of the minister to give (him) sound advice

kurals.chapter_en: The Office of Minister of state
kurals.translit: Pazhudhennum Mandhiriyin Pakkadhadhul Thevvor / Ezhupadhu Koti Urum
kurals.pope: A minister who by king's side plots evil thingsWorse woes than countless foemen brings
kurals.drew: Far better are seventy crores of enemies (for a king) than a minister at his side who intends (his) ruin

kurals.chapter_en: The Office of Minister of state
kurals.translit: Muraippatach Choozhndhum Mutivilave Seyvar / Thirappaatu Ilaaa Thavar
kurals.pope: For gain of end desired just counsel nought availsTo minister, when tact in execution fails
kurals.drew: Those ministers who are destitute of (executive) ability will fail to carry out their projects, although they may have contrived aright

kurals.translit: Naanalam Ennum Nalanutaimai Annalam / Yaanalaththu Ulladhooum Andru
kurals.pope: A tongue that rightly speaks the right is greatest gain, It stands alone midst goodly things that men obtain
kurals.drew: The possession of that goodness which is called the goodness of speech is (even to others) better than any other goodness

kurals.translit: Aakkamung Ketum Adhanaal Varudhalaal / Kaaththompal Sollinkat Sorvu
kurals.pope: Since gain and loss in life on speech depend, From careless slip in speech thyself defend
kurals.drew: Since (both) wealth and evil result from (their) speech, ministers should most carefully guard themselves against faultiness therein

kurals.translit: Kettaarp Pinikkum Thakaiyavaaik Kelaarum / Vetpa Mozhivadhaam Sol
kurals.pope: 'Tis speech that spell-bound holds the listening ear, While those who have not heard desire to hear
kurals.drew: The (minister's) speech is that which seeks (to express) elements as bind his friends (to himself) and is so delivered as to make even his enemies desire (his friendship)

kurals.translit: Thiranarindhu Solluka Sollai Aranum / Porulum Adhaninooungu Il
kurals.pope: Speak words adapted well to various hearers' state; No higher virtue lives, no gain more surely great
kurals.drew: Understand the qualities (of your hearers) and (then) make your speech; for superior to it, there is neither virtue nor wealth

kurals.translit: Solluka Sollaip Piridhorsol Achchollai / Vellunjol Inmai Arindhu
kurals.pope: Speak out your speech, when once 'tis past disputeThat none can utter speech that shall your speech refute
kurals.drew: Deliver your speech, after assuring yourself that no counter speech can defeat your own

kurals.translit: Vetpaththaanj Chollip Pirarsol Payankotal / Maatchiyin Maasatraar Kol
kurals.pope: Charming each hearer's ear, of others' words to seize the sense, Is method wise of men of spotless excellence
kurals.drew: It is the opinion of those who are free from defects in diplomacy that the minister should speak so as to make his hearers desire (to hear more) and grasp the meaning of what he hears himself

kurals.translit: Solalvallan Sorvilan Anjaan Avanai / Ikalvellal Yaarkkum Aridhu
kurals.pope: Mighty in word, of unforgetful mind, of fearless speech,'Tis hard for hostile power such man to overreach
kurals.drew: It is impossible for any one to conquer him by intrique who possesses power of speech, and is neither faulty nor timid

kurals.translit: Viraindhu Thozhilketkum Gnaalam Nirandhinidhu / Solludhal Vallaarp Perin
kurals.pope: Swiftly the listening world will gather round, When men of mighty speech the weighty theme propound
kurals.drew: If there be those who can speak on various subjects in their proper order and in a pleasing manner, the world would readily accept them

kurals.translit: Palasollak Kaamuruvar Mandramaa Satra / Silasollal Thetraa Thavar
kurals.pope: Who have not skill ten faultless words to utter plain, Their tongues will itch with thousand words man's ears to pain
kurals.drew: They will desire to utter many words, who do not know how to speak a few faultless ones

kurals.translit: Inaruzhththum Naaraa Malaranaiyar Katradhu / Unara Viriththuraiyaa Thaar
kurals.pope: Like scentless flower in blooming garland boundAre men who can't their lore acquired to other's ears expound
kurals.drew: Those who are unable to set forth their acquirements (before others) are like flowers blossoming in a cluster and yet without fragrance

kurals.translit: Thunainalam Aakkam Tharuum Vinainalam / Ventiya Ellaan Tharum
kurals.pope: The good external help confers is worldly gain; By action good men every needed gift obtain
kurals.drew: The efficacy of support will yield (only) wealth; (but) the efficacy of action will yield all that is desired

kurals.translit: Endrum Oruvudhal Ventum Pukazhotu / Nandri Payavaa Vinai
kurals.pope: From action evermore thyself restrainOf glory and of good that yields no gain
kurals.drew: Ministers should at all times avoid acts which, in addition to fame, yield no benefit (for the future)

kurals.translit: Oodhal Ventum Olimaazhkum Seyvinai / Aaadhum Ennu Mavar
kurals.pope: Who tell themselves that nobler things shall yet be wonAll deeds that dim the light of glory must they shun
kurals.drew: Those who say, "we will become (better)" should avoid the performance of acts that would destroy (their fame)

kurals.translit: Itukkan Patinum Ilivandha Seyyaar / Natukkatra Kaatchi Yavar
kurals.pope: Though troubles press, no shameful deed they do, Whose eyes the ever-during vision view
kurals.drew: Those who have infallible judgement though threatened with peril will not do acts which have brought disgrace (on former ministers)

kurals.translit: Etrendru Iranguva Seyyarka Seyvaanel / Matranna Seyyaamai Nandru
kurals.pope: Do nought that soul repenting must deplore, If thou hast sinned, 'tis well if thou dost sin no more
kurals.drew: Let a minister never do acts of which he would have to grieve saying, "what is this I have done"; (but) should he do (them), it were good that he grieved not

kurals.translit: Eendraal Pasikaanpaan Aayinunj Cheyyarka / Saandror Pazhikkum Vinai
kurals.pope: Though her that bore thee hung'ring thou behold, no deedDo thou, that men of perfect soul have crime decreed
kurals.drew: Though a minister may see his mother starve; let him do not act which the wise would (treat with contempt)

kurals.translit: Pazhimalaindhu Eydhiya Aakkaththin Saandror / Kazhinal Kurave Thalai
kurals.pope: Than store of wealth guilt-laden souls obtain, The sorest poverty of perfect soul is richer gain
kurals.drew: Far more excellent is the extreme poverty of the wise than wealth obtained by heaping up of sinful

kurals.translit: Katindha Katindhoraar Seydhaarkku Avaidhaam / Mutindhaalum Peezhai Tharum
kurals.pope: To those who hate reproof and do forbidden thingWhat prospers now, in after days shall anguish bring
kurals.drew: The actions of those, who have not desisted from doing deeds forbidden (by the great), will, even if they succeed, cause them sorrow

kurals.translit: Azhak Konta Ellaam Azhappom / Izhappinum Pirpayakkum Narpaa Lavai
kurals.pope: What's gained through tears with tears shall go; From loss good deeds entail harvests of blessings grow
kurals.drew: All that has been obtained with tears (to the victim) will depart with tears (to himself); but what has been by fair means; though with loss at first, will afterwards yield fruit

kurals.translit: Salaththaal Porulseydhe Maarththal Pasuman / Kalaththulneer Peydhireei Yatru
kurals.pope: In pot of clay unburnt he water pours and would retain, Who seeks by wrong the realm in wealth and safety to maintain
kurals.drew: (For a minister) to protect (his king) with wealth obtained by foul means is like preserving a vessel of wet clay by filling it with water

kurals.translit: Vinaiththitpam Enpadhu Oruvan Manaththitpam / Matraiya Ellaam Pira
kurals.pope: What men call 'power in action' know for 'power of mind'Externe to man all other aids you find
kurals.drew: Firmness in action is (simply) one's firmness of mind; all other (abilities) are not of this nature

kurals.translit: Oororaal Utrapin Olkaamai Ivvirantin / Aarenpar Aaindhavar Kol
kurals.pope: 'Each hindrance shun', 'unyielding onward press, If obstacle be there,'These two define your way, so those that search out truth declare
kurals.drew: Not to perform a ruinous act, and not to be discouraged by the ruinous termination of an act, are the two maxims which, the wise say, from the principles of those who have investigated the subject

kurals.translit: Kataikkotkach Cheydhakka Thaanmai Itaikkotkin / Etraa Vizhuman Tharum
kurals.pope: Man's fitting work is known but by success achieved; In midst the plan revealed brings ruin ne'er to be retrieved
kurals.drew: So to perform an act as to publish it (only) at its termination is (true) manliness; for to announce it beforehand, will cause irremediable sorrow

kurals.translit: Solludhal Yaarkkum Eliya Ariyavaam / Solliya Vannam Seyal
kurals.pope: Easy to every man the speech that shows the way; Hard thing to shape one's life by words they say
kurals.drew: To say (how an act is to be performed) is (indeed) easy for any one; but far difficult it is to do according to what has been said

kurals.translit: Veereydhi Maantaar Vinaiththitpam Vendhankan / Ooreydhi Ullap Patum
kurals.pope: The power in act of men renowned and great, With king acceptance finds and fame through all the state
kurals.drew: The firmness in action of those who have become great by the excellence (of their counsel) will, by attaining its fulfilment in the person of the king, be esteemed (by all).

kurals.translit: Enniya Enniyaangu Eydhu Enniyaar / Thinniyar Aakap Perin
kurals.pope: Whate'er men think, ev'n as they think, may men obtain, If those who think can steadfastness of will retain
kurals.drew: If those who have planned (an undertaking) possess firmness (in executing it) they will obtain what they have desired even as they have desired it

kurals.translit: Uruvukantu Ellaamai Ventum Urulperundherkku / Achchaani Annaar Utaiththu
kurals.pope: Despise not men of modest bearing; Look not at form, but what men are:For some there live, high functions sharing, Like linch-pin of the mighty car
kurals.drew: Let none be despised for (their) size; (for) the world has those who resemble the linch-pin of the big rolling car

kurals.translit: Kalangaadhu Kanta Vinaikkan Thulangaadhu / Thookkang Katindhu Seyal
kurals.pope: What clearly eye discerns as right, with steadfast will, And mind unslumbering, that should man fulfil
kurals.drew: An act that has been firmly resolved on must be as firmly carried out without delay

kurals.translit: Thunpam Uravarinum Seyka Thunivaatri / Inpam Payakkum Vinai
kurals.pope: Though toil and trouble face thee, firm resolve hold fast, And do the deeds that pleasure yield at last
kurals.drew: Though it should cause increasing sorrow (at the outset), do with firmness the act that yield bliss (in the end)

kurals.translit: Enaiththitpam Ey Thiyak Kannum / Vinaiththitpam Ventaarai Ventaadhu Ulaku
kurals.pope: The world desires not men of every power possessed, Who power in act desire not,- crown of all the rest
kurals.drew: The great will not esteem those who esteem not firmness of action, whatever other abilities the latter may possess

kurals.translit: Soozhchchi Mutivu Thuniveydhal Aththunivu / Thaazhchchiyul Thangudhal Theedhu
kurals.pope: The Resolve is counsel's end, If resolutions halt In weak delays, still unfulfilled, 'tis grievous fault
kurals.drew: Consultation ends in forming a resolution (to act); (but) delay in the execution of that resolve is an evil

kurals.translit: Thoonguka Thoongich Cheyarpaala Thoongarka / Thoongaadhu Seyyum Vinai
kurals.pope: Slumber when sleepy work's in hand beware Thou slumber not when action calls for sleepless care
kurals.drew: Sleep over such (actions) as may be slept over; (but) never over such as may not be slept over

kurals.translit: Ollumvaa Yellaam Vinainandre Ollaakkaal / Sellumvaai Nokkich Cheyal
kurals.pope: When way is clear, prompt let your action be; When not, watch till some open path you see
kurals.drew: Whenever it is possible (to overcome your enemy) the act (of fighting) is certainly good; if not, endeavour to employ some more successful method

kurals.translit: Vinaipakai Endrirantin Echcham Ninaiyungaal / Theeyechcham Polath Therum
kurals.pope: With work or foe, when you neglect some little thing, If you reflect, like smouldering fire, 'twill ruin bring
kurals.drew: When duly considered, the incomplete execution of an undertaking and hostility will grow and destroy one like the (unextinguished) remnant of a fire

kurals.translit: Porulkaruvi Kaalam Vinaiyitanotu Aindhum / Iruldheera Ennich Cheyal
kurals.pope: Treasure and instrument and time and deed and place of act These five, till every doubt remove, think o'er with care exact
kurals.drew: Do an act after a due consideration of the (following) five, viz money, means, time, execution and place

kurals.translit: Mutivum Itaiyoorum Mutriyaangu Eydhum / Patupayanum Paarththuch Cheyal
kurals.pope: Accomplishment, the hindrances, large profits won By effort these compare,- then let the work be done
kurals.drew: An act is to be performed after considering the exertion required, the obstacles to be encountered, and the great profit to be gained (on its completion)

kurals.translit: Seyvinai Seyvaan Seyanmurai Avvinai / Ullarivaan Ullam Kolal
kurals.pope: Who would succeed must thus begin first let him ask The thoughts of them who thoroughly know the task
kurals.drew: The method of performance for one who has begun an act is to ascertain the mind of him who knows the secret thereof

kurals.translit: Vinaiyaan Vinaiyaakkik Kotal Nanaikavul / Yaanaiyaal Yaanaiyaath Thatru
kurals.pope: By one thing done you reach a second work's accomplishment; So furious elephant to snare its fellow brute is sent
kurals.drew: To make one undertaking the means of accomplishing another (similar to it) is like making one rutting elephant the means of capturing another

kurals.translit: Nattaarkku Nalla Seyalin Viraindhadhe / Ottaarai Ottik Kolal
kurals.pope: Than kindly acts to friends more urgent thing to do, Is making foes to cling as friends attached to you
kurals.drew: One should rather hasten to secure the alliance of the foes (of one's foes) than perform good offices to one's friends

kurals.translit: Uraisiriyaar Ulnatungal Anjik Kuraiperin / Kolvar Periyaarp Panindhu
kurals.pope: The men of lesser realm, fearing the people's inward dread, Accepting granted terms, to mightier ruler bow the head
kurals.drew: Ministers of small states, afraid of their people being frightened, will yield to and acknowledge their superior foes, if the latter offer them a chance of reconciliation

kurals.translit: Anputaimai Aandra Kutippiraththal Vendhavaam / Panputaimai Thoodhuraippaan Panpu
kurals.pope: Benevolence high birth, the courtesy kings love:-These qualities the envoy of a king approve
kurals.drew: The qualification of an ambassador are affection (for his relations) a fitting birth, and the possession of attributes pleasing to royalty

kurals.translit: Anparivu Aaraaindha Solvanmai Thoodhuraippaarkku / Indri Yamaiyaadha Moondru
kurals.pope: Love, knowledge, power of chosen words, three things, Should he possess who speaks the words of kings
kurals.drew: Love (to his sovereign), knowledge (of his affairs), and a discriminating power of speech (before other sovereigns) are the three sine qua non qualifications of an ambassador

kurals.translit: Noolaarul Noolvallan Aakudhal Velaarul / Vendri Vinaiyuraippaan Panpu
kurals.pope: Mighty in lore amongst the learned must he be, Midst jav'lin-bearing kings who speaks the words of victory
kurals.drew: To be powerful in politics among those who are learned (in ethics) is the character of him who speaks

kurals.translit: Arivuru Vaaraaindha Kalviim Moondran / Serivutaiyaan Selka Vinaikku
kurals.pope: Sense, goodly grace, and knowledge exquisiteWho hath these three for envoy's task is fit
kurals.drew: He may go on a mission (to foreign rulers) who has combined in him all these three viz, (natural) sense, an attractive bearing and well-tried learning

kurals.translit: Thokach Chollith Thoovaadha Neekki / Nakachcholli Nandri Payappadhaan Thoodhu
kurals.pope: In terms concise, avoiding wrathful speech, who utters pleasant word, An envoy he who gains advantage for his lord
kurals.drew: He is an ambassador who (in the presence of foreign rulers) speaks briefly, avoids harshness, talks so as to make them smile, and thus brings good (to his own sovereign)

kurals.translit: Katrukkan Anjaan Selachchollik Kaalaththaal / Thakkadhu Arivadhaam Thoodhu
kurals.pope: An envoy meet is he, well-learned, of fearless eyeWho speaks right home, prepared for each emergency
kurals.drew: He is an ambassador who having studied (politics) talks impressively, is not afraid of angry looks, and knows (to employ) the art suited to the time

kurals.translit: Katanarindhu Kaalang Karudhi Itanarindhu / Enni Uraippaan Thalai
kurals.pope: He is the best who knows what's due, the time considered well, The place selects, then ponders long ere he his errand tell
kurals.drew: He is chief (among ambassadors) who understands the proper decorum (before foreign princes), seeks the (proper) occasion, knows the (most suitable) place, and delivers his message after (due)

kurals.translit: Thooimai Thunaimai Thunivutaimai Immoondrin / Vaaimai Vazhiyuraippaan Panpu
kurals.pope: Integrity, resources, soul determined, truthfulnessWho rightly speaks his message must these marks possess
kurals.drew: The qualifications of him who faithfully delivers his (sovereign's) message are purity, the support (of foreign ministers), and boldness, with truthfulness in addition to the (aforesaid) three

kurals.translit: Vitumaatram Vendharkku Uraippaan Vatumaatram / Vaaiseraa Vanka Navan
kurals.pope: His faltering lips must utter no unworthy thing, Who stands, with steady eye, to speak the mandates of his king
kurals.drew: He alone is fit to communicate (his sovereign's) reply, who possesses the firmness not to utter even inadvertently what may reflect discredit (on the latter)

kurals.translit: Irudhi Payappinum Enjaadhu Iraivarku / Urudhi Payappadhaam Thoodhu
kurals.pope: Death to the faithful one his embassy may bring; To envoy gains assured advantage for his king
kurals.drew: He is the ambassador who fearlessly seeks his sovereign's good though it should cost him his life (to deliver his message)

kurals.chapter_en: Conduct in the Presence of the King
kurals.translit: Akalaadhu Anukaadhu Theekkaaivaar Polka / Ikalvendharch Cherndhozhuku Vaar
kurals.pope: Who warm them at the fire draw not too near, nor keep too much aloof; Thus let them act who dwell beneath of warlike kings the palace-roof
kurals.drew: Thus let them act who dwell beneath of warlike kings the palace-roof

kurals.chapter_en: Conduct in the Presence of the King
kurals.translit: Mannar Vizhaipa Vizhaiyaamai Mannaraal / Manniya Aakkan Tharum
kurals.pope: To those who prize not state that kings are wont to prize, The king himself abundant wealth supplies
kurals.drew: For ministers not to cover the things desired by their kings will through the kings themselves yield them everlasting wealth

kurals.chapter_en: Conduct in the Presence of the King
kurals.translit: Potrin Ariyavai Potral Katuththapin / Thetrudhal Yaarkkum Aridhu
kurals.pope: Who would walk warily, let him of greater faults beware; To clear suspicions once aroused is an achievement rare
kurals.drew: Ministers who would save themselves should avoid (the commission of) serious errors for if the king's suspicion is once roused, no one can remove it

kurals.chapter_en: Conduct in the Presence of the King
kurals.translit: Sevichchollum Serndha Nakaiyum Aviththozhukal / Aandra Periyaa Rakaththu
kurals.pope: All whispered words and interchange of smiles repress, In presence of the men who kingly power possess
kurals.drew: While in the presence of the sovereign, ministers should neither whisper to nor smile at others

kurals.chapter_en: Conduct in the Presence of the King
kurals.translit: Epporulum Oraar Thotaraarmar Rapporulai / Vittakkaal Ketka Marai
kurals.pope: Seek not, ask not, the secret of the king to hear; But if he lets the matter forth, give ear
kurals.drew: (When the king is engaged) in secret counsel (with others), ministers should neither over-hear anything whatever nor pry into it with inquisitive questions, but (wait to) listen when it is divulged (by

kurals.chapter_en: Conduct in the Presence of the King
kurals.translit: Kuripparindhu Kaalang Karudhi Veruppila / Ventupa Vetpach Cholal
kurals.pope: Knowing the signs, waiting for fitting time, with courteous care, Things not displeasing, needful things, declare
kurals.drew: Knowing the (king's disposition and seeking the right time, (the minister) should in a pleasing manner suggest things such as are desirable and not disagreeable

kurals.chapter_en: Conduct in the Presence of the King
kurals.translit: Vetpana Solli Vinaiyila Egngnaandrum / Ketpinum Sollaa Vital
kurals.pope: Speak pleasant things, but never utter idle word; Not though by monarch's ears with pleasure heard
kurals.drew: Ministers should (always) give agreeable advice but on no occasion recommend useless actions, though requested (to do so)

kurals.chapter_en: Conduct in the Presence of the King
kurals.translit: Ilaiyar Inamuraiyar Endrikazhaar Nindra / Oliyotu Ozhukap Patum
kurals.pope: Say not, 'He's young, my kinsman,' despising thus your king; But reverence the glory kingly state doth bring
kurals.drew: Ministers should behave in accordance with the (Divine) light in the person of kings and not despise them saying, "He is our junior (in age) and connected with our family!"

kurals.chapter_en: Conduct in the Presence of the King
kurals.translit: Kolappattem Endrennik Kollaadha Seyyaar / Thulakkatra Kaatchi Yavar
kurals.pope: 'We've gained his grace, boots nought what graceless acts we do', So deem not sages who the changeless vision view
kurals.drew: Those whose judgement is firm will not do what is disagreeable (to the sovereign) saying (within

kurals.chapter_en: Conduct in the Presence of the King
kurals.translit: Pazhaiyam Enakkarudhip Panpalla Seyyum / Kezhudhakaimai Ketu Tharum
kurals.pope: Who think 'We're ancient friends' and do unseemly things; To these familiarity sure ruin brings
kurals.drew: The (foolish) claim with which a minister does unbecoming acts because of his (long) familiarity (with the king) will ensure his ruin

kurals.translit: Kooraamai Nokkake Kuripparivaan Egngnaandrum / Maaraaneer Vaiyak Kani
kurals.pope: Who knows the sign, and reads unuttered thought, the gem is he, Of earth round traversed by the changeless sea
kurals.drew: The minister who by looking (at the king) understands his mind without being told (of it), will be a perpetual ornament to the world which is surrounded by a never-drying sea

kurals.translit: Aiyap Pataaadhu Akaththadhu Unarvaanaith / Theyvaththo Toppak Kolal
kurals.pope: Undoubting, who the minds of men can scan, As deity regard that gifted man
kurals.drew: He is to be esteemed a god who is able to ascertain without a doubt what is within (one's mind)

kurals.translit: Kurippir Kurippunar Vaarai Uruppinul / Yaadhu Kotuththum Kolal
kurals.pope: Who by the sign the signs interprets plain, Give any member up his aid to gain
kurals.drew: The king should ever give whatever (is asked) of his belongings and secure him who, by the indications (of his own mind) is able to read those of another

kurals.translit: Kuriththadhu Kooraamaik Kolvaaro Tenai / Uruppo Ranaiyaraal Veru
kurals.pope: Who reads what's shown by signs, though words unspoken be, In form may seem as other men, in function nobler far is he
kurals.drew: Those who understand one's thoughts without being informed (thereof) and those who do not, may (indeed) resemble one another bodily; still are they different (mentally)

kurals.translit: Kurippir Kurippunaraa Vaayin Uruppinul / Enna Payaththavo Kan?
kurals.pope: By sign who knows not sings to comprehend, what gain,'Mid all his members, from his eyes does he obtain
kurals.drew: Of what use are the eyes amongst one's members, if they cannot by their own indications dive those of another ?

kurals.translit: Atuththadhu Kaattum Palingupol Nenjam / Katuththadhu Kaattum Mukam
kurals.pope: As forms around in crystal mirrored clear we find, The face will show what's throbbing in the mind
kurals.drew: As the mirror reflects what is near so does the face show what is uppermost in the mind

kurals.translit: Mukaththin Mudhukkuraindhadhu Unto Uvappinum / Kaayinum Thaanmun Thurum
kurals.pope: Than speaking countenance hath aught more prescient skill?Rejoice or burn with rage, 'tis the first herald still
kurals.drew: Is there anything so full of knowledge as the face ? (No) it precedes the mind, whether (the latter is) pleased or vexed

kurals.translit: Mukamnokki Nirka Amaiyum Akamnokki / Utra Thunarvaarp Perin
kurals.pope: To see the face is quite enough, in presence brought, When men can look within and know the lurking thought
kurals.drew: If the king gets those who by looking into his mind can understand (and remove) what has occurred (to him) it is enough that he stand looking at their face

kurals.translit: Pakaimaiyum Kenmaiyum Kannuraikkum Kannin / Vakaimai Unarvaarp Perin
kurals.pope: The eye speaks out the hate or friendly soul of man; To those who know the eye's swift varying moods to scan
kurals.drew: If a king gets ministers who can read the movements of the eye, the eyes (of foreign kings) will (themselves) reveal (to him) their hatred or friendship

kurals.translit: Nunniyam Enpaar Alakkungol Kaanungaal / Kannalladhu Illai Pira
kurals.pope: The men of keen discerning soul no other test apply(When you their secret ask) than man's revealing eye
kurals.drew: The measuring-rod of those (ministers) who say "we are acute" will on inquiry be found to be their (own) eyes and nothing else

kurals.chapter_en: The Knowledge of the Council Chamber
kurals.translit: Avaiyarinadhu Aaraaindhu Solluka Sollin / Thokaiyarindha Thooimai Yavar
kurals.pope: Men pure in heart, who know of words the varied force, Should to their audience known adapt their well-arranged discourse
kurals.drew: Let the pure who know the arrangement of words speak with deliberation after ascertaining (the nature of) the court (then assembled)

kurals.chapter_en: The Knowledge of the Council Chamber
kurals.translit: Itaidherindhu Nankunarndhu Solluka Sollin / Nataidherindha Nanmai Yavar
kurals.pope: Good men to whom the arts of eloquence are known, Should seek occasion meet, and say what well they've made their own
kurals.drew: Let the good who know the uses of words speak with a clear knowledge after ascertaining the time (suited to the court)
