kurals.drew: The learned (physician) should ascertain the condition of his patient; the nature of his disease, and the season (of the year) and (then) proceed (with his treatment)

kurals.translit: Utravan Theerppaan Marundhuzhaich Chelvaanendru / Appaal Naar Kootre Marundhu
kurals.pope: For patient, leech, and remedies, and him who waits by patient's side, The art of medicine must fourfold code of laws provide
kurals.drew: Medical science consists of four parts, viz, patient, physician, medicine and compounder; and each of these (again) contains four sub-divisions

kurals.translit: Irpirandhaar Kanalladhu Illai Iyalpaakach / Cheppamum Naanum Orungu
kurals.pope: Save in the scions of a noble house, you never findInstinctive sense of right and virtuous shame combined
kurals.drew: Consistency (of thought, word and deed) and fear (of sin) are conjointly natural only to the high-born

kurals.translit: Ozhukkamum Vaaimaiyum Naanum Im / Moondrum Izhukkaar Kutippiran Thaar
kurals.pope: In these three things the men of noble birth fail not:In virtuous deed and truthful word, and chastened thought
kurals.drew: The high-born will never deviate from these three; good manners, truthfulness and modesty

kurals.translit: Nakaieekai Insol Ikazhaamai Naankum / Vakaiyenpa Vaaimaik Kutikku
kurals.pope: The smile, the gift, the pleasant word, unfailing courtesyThese are the signs, they say, of true nobility
kurals.drew: A cheerful countenance, liberality, pleasant words, and an unreviling disposition, these four are said to be the proper qualities of the truly high-born

kurals.translit: Atukkiya Koti Perinum Kutippirandhaar / Kundruva Seydhal Ilar
kurals.pope: Millions on millions piled would never winThe men of noble race to soul-degrading sin
kurals.drew: Though blessed with immense wealth, the noble will never do anything unbecoming

kurals.translit: Vazhanguva Thulveezhndhak Kannum Pazhanguti / Panpil Thalaippiridhal Indru
kurals.pope: Though stores for charity should fail within, the ancient raceWill never lose its old ancestral grace
kurals.drew: Though their means fall off, those born in ancient families, will not lose their character (for liberality)

kurals.translit: Salampatrich Chaalpila Seyyaarmaa Satra / Kulampatri Vaazhdhum En Paar
kurals.pope: Whose minds are set to live as fits their sire's unspotted fame, Stooping to low deceit, commit no deeds that gender shame
kurals.drew: Those who seek to preserve the irreproachable honour of their families will not viciously do what is detrimental thereto

kurals.translit: Kutippirandhaar Kanvilangum Kutram Visumpin / Madhikkan Maruppol Uyarndhu
kurals.pope: The faults of men of noble race are seen by every eye, As spots on her bright orb that walks sublime the evening sky
kurals.drew: As spots on her bright orb that walks sublime the evening sky

kurals.translit: Nalaththinkan Naarinmai Thondrin Avanaik / Kulaththinkan Aiyap Patum
kurals.pope: If lack of love appear in those who bear some goodly name,'Twill make men doubt the ancestry they claim
kurals.drew: If one of a good family betrays want of affection, his descent from it will be called in question

kurals.translit: Nilaththil Kitandhamai Kaalkaattum Kaattum / Kulaththil Pirandhaarvaaich Chol
kurals.pope: Of soil the plants that spring thereout will show the worth:The words they speak declare the men of noble birth
kurals.drew: As the sprout indicates the nature of the soil, (so) the speech of the noble indicates (that of one's birth)

kurals.translit: Nalamventin Naanutaimai Ventum Kulam / Ventin Ventuka Yaarkkum Panivu
kurals.pope: Who seek for good the grace of virtuous shame must know; Who seek for noble name to all must reverence show
kurals.drew: He who desires a good name must desire modesty; and he who desires (the continuance of) a family greatness must be submissive to all

kurals.translit: Indri Amaiyaach Chirappina Aayinum / Kundra Varupa Vital
kurals.pope: Though linked to splendours man no otherwise may gain, Reject each act that may thine honour's clearness stain
kurals.drew: Actions that would degrade (one's) family should not be done; though they may be so important that not doing them would end in death

kurals.translit: Seerinum Seeralla Seyyaare Seerotu / Peraanmai Ventu Pavar
kurals.pope: Who seek with glory to combine honour's untarnished fame, Do no inglorious deeds, though men accord them glory's name
kurals.drew: Those who desire (to maintain their) honour, will surely do nothing dishonourable, even for the sake of fame

kurals.translit: Perukkaththu Ventum Panidhal Siriya / Surukkaththu Ventum Uyarvu
kurals.pope: Bow down thy soul, with increase blest, in happy hour; Lift up thy heart, when stript of all by fortune's power
kurals.drew: In great prosperity humility is becoming; dignity, in great adversity

kurals.translit: Thalaiyin Izhindha Mayiranaiyar Maandhar / Nilaiyin Izhindhak Katai
kurals.pope: Like hairs from off the head that fall to earth, When fall'n from high estate are men of noble birth
kurals.drew: They who have fallen from their (high) position are like the hair which has fallen from the head

kurals.translit: Kundrin Anaiyaarum Kundruvar Kundruva / Kundri Anaiya Seyin
kurals.pope: If meanness, slight as 'abrus' grain, by men be wrought, Though like a hill their high estate, they sink to nought
kurals.drew: Even those who are exalted like a hill will be thought low, if they commit deeds that are debasing

kurals.translit: Pukazhindraal Puththelnaattu Uyyaadhaal Enmatru / Ikazhvaarpin Sendru Nilai
kurals.pope: It yields no praise, nor to the land of Gods throws wide the gate:Why follow men who scorn, and at their bidding wait
kurals.drew: Why follow men who scorn, and at their bidding wait?

kurals.translit: Ottaarpin Sendroruvan Vaazhdhala�n Annilaiye / Kettaan Enappatudhal Nandru
kurals.pope: Better 'twere said, 'He's perished!' than to gainThe means to live, following in foeman's train
kurals.drew: It is better for a man to be said of him that he died in his usual state than that he eked out his life by following those who disgraced him

kurals.translit: Marundhomatru Oonompum Vaazhkkai Perundhakaimai / Peetazhiya Vandha Itaththu
kurals.pope: When high estate has lost its pride of honour meet, Is life, that nurses this poor flesh, as nectar sweet
kurals.drew: For the high-born to keep their body in life when their honour is gone will certainly not prove a remedy against death

kurals.translit: Mayirneeppin Vaazhaak Kavarimaa Annaar / Uyirneeppar Maanam Varin
kurals.pope: Like the wild ox that, of its tuft bereft, will pine away, Are those who, of their honour shorn, will quit the light of day
kurals.drew: Those who give up (their) life when (their) honour is at stake are like the yark which kills itself at the loss of (even one of) its hairs

kurals.translit: Ilivarin Vaazhaadha Maanam Utaiyaar / Olidhozhudhu Eththum Ulaku
kurals.pope: Who, when dishonour comes, refuse to live, their honoured memoryWill live in worship and applause of all the world for aye
kurals.drew: The world will (always) praise and adore the fame of the honourable who would rather die than suffer indignity

kurals.translit: Olioruvarku Ulla Verukkai Ilioruvarku / Aqdhirandhu Vaazhdhum Enal
kurals.pope: The light of life is mental energy; disgrace is hisWho says, 'I 'ill lead a happy life devoid of this.'
kurals.drew: One's light is the abundance of one's courage; one's darkness is the desire to live destitute of such (a state of mind.)

kurals.translit: Pirappokkum Ellaa Uyirkkum Sirappovvaa / Seydhozhil Vetrumai Yaan
kurals.pope: All men that live are one in circumstances of birth; Diversities of works give each his special worth
kurals.drew: All human beings agree as regards their birth but differ as regards their characteristics, because of the different qualities of their actions

kurals.translit: Melirundhum Melallaar Melallar Keezhirundhum / Keezhallaar Keezhal Lavar
kurals.pope: The men of lofty line, whose souls are mean, are never greatThe men of lowly birth, when high of soul, are not of low estate
kurals.drew: Though (raised) above, the base cannot become great; though (brought) low, the great cannot become base

kurals.translit: Orumai Makalire Polap Perumaiyum / Thannaiththaan Kontozhukin Untu
kurals.pope: Like single-hearted women, greatness too, Exists while to itself is true
kurals.drew: Exists while to itself is true

kurals.translit: Perumai Yutaiyavar Aatruvaar Aatrin / Arumai Utaiya Seyal
kurals.pope: The man endowed with greatness true, Rare deeds in perfect wise will do
kurals.drew: (Though reduced) the great will be able to perform, in the proper way, deeds difficult (for others to do)

kurals.translit: Siriyaar Unarchchiyul Illai Periyaaraip / Penikkol Vemennum Nokku
kurals.pope: 'As votaries of the truly great we will ourselves enroll,'Is thought that enters not the mind of men of little soul
kurals.drew: It is never in the nature of the base to seek the society of the great and partake of their nature

kurals.translit: Irappe Purindha Thozhitraam Sirappundhaan / Seeral Lavarkan Patin
kurals.pope: Whene'er distinction lights on some unworthy head, Then deeds of haughty insolence are bred
kurals.drew: Even nobility of birth, wealth and learning, if in (the possession of) the base, will (only) produce everincreasing pride

kurals.translit: Paniyumaam Endrum Perumai Sirumai / Aniyumaam Thannai Viyandhu
kurals.pope: Greatness humbly bends, but littleness alwaysSpreads out its plumes, and loads itself with praise
kurals.drew: The great will always humble himself; but the mean will exalt himself in self-admiration

kurals.translit: Perumai Perumidham Inmai Sirumai / Perumidham Oorndhu Vital
kurals.pope: Greatness is absence of conceit; meanness, we deem, Riding on car of vanity supreme
kurals.drew: Freedom from conceit is (the nature of true) greatness; (while) obstinacy therein is (that of) meanness

kurals.translit: Atram Maraikkum Perumai Sirumaidhaan / Kutrame Koori Vitum
kurals.pope: Greatness will hide a neighbour's shame; Meanness his faults to all the world proclaim
kurals.drew: The great hide the faults of others; the base only divulge them

kurals.translit: Katanenpa Nallavai Ellaam Katanarindhu / Saandraanmai Merkol Pavarkku
kurals.pope: All goodly things are duties to the men, they sayWho set themselves to walk in virtue's perfect way
kurals.drew: It is said that those who are conscious of their duty and behave with a perfect goodness will regard as natural all that is good

kurals.translit: Kunanalam Saandror Nalane Piranalam / Ennalaththu Ulladhooum Andru
kurals.pope: The good of inward excellence they claim, The perfect men; all other good is only good in name
kurals.drew: The only delight of the perfect is that of their goodness; all other (sensual) delights are not to be included among any (true) delights

kurals.translit: Anpunaan Oppuravu Kannottam Vaaimaiyotu / Aindhusaal Oondriya Thoon
kurals.pope: Love, modesty, beneficence, benignant grace, With truth, are pillars five of perfect virtue's resting-place
kurals.drew: Affection, fear (of sin), benevolence, favour and truthfulness; these are the five pillars on which perfect goodness rests

kurals.translit: Kollaa Nalaththadhu Nonmai Pirardheemai / Sollaa Nalaththadhu Saalpu
kurals.pope: The type of 'penitence' is virtuous good that nothing slays; To speak no ill of other men is perfect virtue's praise
kurals.drew: Penance consists in the goodness that kills not , and perfection in the goodness that tells not others' faults

kurals.translit: Aatruvaar Aatral Panidhal Adhusaandror / Maatraarai Maatrum Patai
kurals.pope: Submission is the might of men of mighty acts; the sageWith that same weapon stills his foeman's rage
kurals.drew: Stooping (to inferiors) is the strength of those who can accomplish (an undertaking); and that is the weapon with which the great avert their foes

kurals.translit: Saalpirkuk Kattalai Yaadhenin Tholvi / Thulaiyallaar Kannum Kolal
kurals.pope: What is perfection's test? The equal mindTo bear repulse from even meaner men resigned
kurals.drew: The touch-stone of perfection is to receive a defeat even at the hands of one's inferiors

kurals.translit: Innaasey Thaarkkum Iniyave Seyyaakkaal / Enna Payaththadho Saalpu
kurals.pope: What fruit doth your perfection yield you, say!Unless to men who work you ill good repay
kurals.drew: Of what avail is perfect goodness if it cannot do pleasing things even to those who have pained (it) ?

kurals.translit: Inmai Oruvarku Ilivandru Saalpennum / Thinmai Un Taakap Perin
kurals.pope: To soul with perfect virtue's strength endued, Brings no disgrace the lack of every earthly good
kurals.drew: Poverty is no disgrace to one who abounds in good qualities

kurals.translit: Oozhi Peyarinum Thaampeyaraar Saandraanmaikku / Aazhi Enappatu Vaar
kurals.pope: Call them of perfect virtue's sea the shore, Who, though the fates should fail, fail not for evermore
kurals.drew: Those who are said to be the shore of the sea of perfection will never change, though ages may change

kurals.translit: Saandravar Saandraanmai Kundrin Irunilandhaan / Thaangaadhu Manno Porai
kurals.pope: The mighty earth its burthen to sustain must cease, If perfect virtue of the perfect men decrease
kurals.drew: If there is a defect in the character of the perfect, (even) the great world cannot bear (its) burden

kurals.translit: Enpadhaththaal Eydhal Elidhenpa Yaarmaattum / Panputaimai Ennum Vazhakku
kurals.pope: Who easy access give to every man, they say, Of kindly courtesy will learn with ease the way
kurals.drew: If one is easy of access to all, it will be easy for one to obtain the virtue called goodness

kurals.translit: Anputaimai Aandra Kutippiraththal Ivvirantum / Panputaimai Ennum Vazhakku
kurals.pope: Benevolence and high born dignity, These two are beaten paths of courtesy
kurals.drew: Affectionateness and birth in a good family, these two constitute what is called a proper behaviour to all

kurals.translit: Uruppoththal Makkaloppu Andraal Veruththakka / Panpoththal Oppadhaam Oppu
kurals.pope: Men are not one because their members seem alike to outward view; Similitude of kindred quality makes likeness true
kurals.drew: Resemblance of bodies is no resemblance of souls; true resemblance is the resemblance of qualities that attract

kurals.translit: Nayanotu Nandri Purindha Payanutaiyaar / Panpupaa Raattum Ulaku
kurals.pope: Of men of fruitful life, who kindly benefits dispense, The world unites to praise the 'noble excellence.'
kurals.drew: The world applauds the character of those whose usefulness results from their equity and charity

kurals.translit: Nakaiyullum Innaa Thikazhchchi Pakaiyullum / Panpula Paatarivaar Maattu
kurals.pope: Contempt is evil though in sport They who man's nature know, E'en in their wrath, a courteous mind will show
kurals.drew: Reproach is painful to one even in sport; those (therefore) who know the nature of others exhibit (pleasing) qualities even when they are hated

kurals.translit: Panputaiyaarp Pattuntu Ulakam Adhuindrel / Manpukku Maaivadhu Man
kurals.pope: The world abides; for 'worthy' men its weight sustainWere it not so, 'twould fall to dust again
kurals.drew: The (way of the) world subsists by contact with the good; if not, it would bury itself in the earth and perish

kurals.translit: Arampolum Koormaiya Renum Marampolvar / Makkatpanpu Illaa Thavar
kurals.pope: Though sharp their wit as file, as blocks they must remain, Whose souls are void of 'courtesy humane'
kurals.drew: He who is destitute of (true) human qualities (only) resembles a tree, though he may possess the sharpness of a file

kurals.translit: Nanpaatraar Aaki Nayamila Seyvaarkkum / Panpaatraar Aadhal Katai
kurals.pope: Though men with all unfriendly acts and wrongs assail,'Tis uttermost disgrace in 'courtesy' to fail
kurals.drew: It is wrong (for the wise) not to exhibit (good) qualities even towards those who bearing no friendship (for them) do only what is hateful

kurals.translit: Nakalvallar Allaarkku Maayiru Gnaalam / Pakalumpaar Pattandru Irul
kurals.pope: To him who knows not how to smile in kindly mirth, Darkness in daytime broods o'er all the vast and mighty earth
kurals.drew: To those who cannot rejoice, the wide world is buried darkness even in (broad) day light

kurals.translit: Panpilaan Petra Perunjelvam Nanpaal / Kalandheemai Yaaldhirin Thatru
kurals.pope: Like sweet milk soured because in filthy vessel poured, Is ample wealth in churlish man's unopened coffers stored
kurals.drew: The great wealth obtained by one who has no goodness will perish like pure milk spoilt by the

kurals.translit: Vaiththaanvaai Saandra Perumporul Aqdhunnaan / Seththaan Seyakkitandhadhu Il
kurals.pope: Who fills his house with ample store, enjoying none, Is dead Nought with the useless heap is done
kurals.drew: He who does not enjoy the immense riches he has heaped up in his house, is (to be reckoned as) dead, (for) there is nothing achieved (by him)

kurals.translit: Porulaanaam Ellaamendru Eeyaadhu Ivarum / Marulaanaam Maanaap Pirappu
kurals.pope: Who giving nought, opines from wealth all blessing springs, Degraded birth that doting miser's folly brings
kurals.drew: He who knows that wealth yields every pleasure and yet is so blind as to lead miserly life will be born a demon

kurals.translit: Eettam Ivari Isaiventaa Aatavar / Thotram Nilakkup Porai
kurals.pope: Who lust to heap up wealth, but glory hold not dear, It burthens earth when on the stage of being they appear
kurals.drew: A burden to the earth are men bent on the acquisition of riches and not (true) fame

kurals.translit: Echchamendru Enennung Kollo Oruvaraal / Nachchap Pataaa Thavan
kurals.pope: Whom no one loves, when he shall pass away, What doth he look to leave behind, I pray
kurals.drew: What will the miser who is not liked (by any one) regard as his own (in the world to come) ?

kurals.translit: Kotuppadhooum Thuyppadhooum Illaarkku Atukkiya / Kotiyun Taayinum Il
kurals.pope: Amid accumulated millions they are poor, Who nothing give and nought enjoy of all they store
kurals.drew: Those who neither give (to others) nor enjoy (their property) are (truly) destitute, though possessing immense riches

kurals.translit: Edham Perunjelvam Thaandhuvvaan Thakkaarkkondru / Eedhal Iyalpilaa Thaan
kurals.pope: Their ample wealth is misery to men of churlish heart, Who nought themselves enjoy, and nought to worthy men impart
kurals.drew: He who enjoys not (his riches) nor relieves the wants of the worthy is a disease to his wealth

kurals.translit: Atraarkkondru Aatraadhaan Selvam Mikanalam / Petraal Thamiyalmooth Thatru
kurals.pope: Like woman fair in lonelihood who aged grows, Is wealth of him on needy men who nought bestows
kurals.drew: The wealth of him who never bestows anything on the destitute is like a woman of beauty growing old without a husband

kurals.translit: Nachchap Pataadhavan Selvam Natuvoorul / Nachchu Marampazhuth Thatru
kurals.pope: When he whom no man loves exults in great prosperity,'Tis as when fruits in midmost of the town some poisonous tree
kurals.drew: The wealth of him who is disliked (by all) is like the fruit-bearing of the etty tree in the midst of a town

kurals.translit: Anporeeith Tharsetru Aranokkaadhu Eettiya / Onporul Kolvaar Pirar
kurals.pope: Who love abandon, self-afflict, and virtue's way forsakeTo heap up glittering wealth, their hoards shall others take
kurals.drew: To heap up glittering wealth, their hoards shall others take

kurals.translit: Seerutaich Chelvar Sirudhuni Maari / Varangoorn Thanaiyadhu Utaiththu
kurals.pope: 'Tis as when rain cloud in the heaven grows day, When generous wealthy man endures brief poverty
kurals.drew: The short-lived poverty of those who are noble and rich is like the clouds becoming poor (for a while)

kurals.translit: Karumaththaal Naanudhal Naanun Thirunudhal / Nallavar Naanup Pira
kurals.pope: To shrink abashed from evil deed is 'generous shame'; Other is that of bright-browed one of virtuous fame
kurals.drew: True modesty is the fear of (evil) deeds; all other modesty is (simply) the bashfulness of virtuous maids

kurals.translit: Oonutai Echcham Uyirkkellaam Veralla / Naanutaimai Maandhar Sirappu
kurals.pope: Food, clothing, and other things alike all beings own; By sense of shame the excellence of men is known
kurals.drew: Food, clothing and the like are common to all men but modesty is peculiar to the good

kurals.translit: Oonaik Kuriththa Uyirellaam Naanennum / Nanmai Kuriththadhu Saalpu
kurals.pope: All spirits homes of flesh as habitation claim, And perfect virtue ever dwells with shame
kurals.drew: As the body is the abode of the spirit, so the excellence of modesty is the abode of perfection

kurals.translit: Aniandro Naanutaimai Saandrorkku Aqdhindrel / Piniandro Peetu Natai
kurals.pope: And is not shame an ornament to men of dignity?Without it step of stately pride is piteous thing to see
kurals.drew: Is not the modesty ornament of the noble ? Without it, their haughtiness would be a pain (to others)

kurals.translit: Pirarpazhiyum Thampazhiyum Naanuvaar Naanukku / Uraipadhi Ennum Ulaku
kurals.pope: As home of virtuous shame by all the world the men are known, Who feel ashamed for others, guilt as for their own
kurals.drew: The world regards as the abode of modesty him who fear his own and other's guilt

kurals.translit: Naanveli Kollaadhu Manno Viyangnaalam / Penalar Melaa Yavar
kurals.pope: Unless the hedge of shame inviolate remain, For men of lofty soul the earth's vast realms no charms retain
kurals.drew: The great make modesty their barrier (of defence) and not the wide world

kurals.translit: Naanaal Uyiraith Thurappar Uyirpporuttaal / Naandhuravaar Naanaal Pavar
kurals.pope: The men of modest soul for shame would life an offering make, But ne'er abandon virtuous shame for life's dear sake
kurals.drew: The modest would rather lose their life for the sake of modesty than lose modesty for the sake of life

kurals.translit: Pirarnaanath Thakkadhu Thaannaanaa Naayin / Aramnaanath Thakkadhu Utaiththu
kurals.pope: Though know'st no shame, while all around asha med must be:Virtue will shrink away ashamed of thee
kurals.drew: Virtue is likely to forsake him who shamelessly does what others are ashamed of

kurals.translit: Kulanjutum Kolkai Pizhaippin Nalanjutum / Naaninmai Nindrak Katai
kurals.pope: 'Twill race consume if right observance fail;'Twill every good consume if shamelessness prevail
kurals.drew: Want of manners injures one's family; but want of modesty injures one's character

kurals.translit: Naanakath Thillaar Iyakkam Marappaavai / Naanaal Uyirmarutti Atru
kurals.pope: 'Tis as with strings a wooden puppet apes life's functions, whenThose void of shame within hold intercourse with men
kurals.drew: The actions of those who are without modesty at heart are like those of puppet moved by a string

kurals.chapter_en: The Way of Maintaining the Family
kurals.translit: Karumam Seyaoruvan Kaidhooven Ennum / Perumaiyin Peetutaiyadhu Il
kurals.pope: Who says 'I'll do my work, nor slack my hand', His greatness, clothed with dignity supreme, shall stand
kurals.drew: There is no higher greatness than that of one saying I will not cease in my effort (to raise my family)

kurals.chapter_en: The Way of Maintaining the Family
kurals.translit: Aalvinaiyum Aandra Arivum Enairantin / Neelvinaiyaal Neelum Kuti
kurals.pope: The manly act and knowledge full, when these combineIn deed prolonged, then lengthens out the race's line
kurals.drew: One's family is raised by untiring perseverance in both effort and wise contrivances

kurals.chapter_en: The Way of Maintaining the Family
kurals.translit: Kutiseyval Ennum Oruvarkuth Theyvam / Matidhatruth Thaanmun Thurum
kurals.pope: 'I'll make my race renowned,' if man shall say, With vest succinct the goddess leads the way
kurals.drew: The Deity will clothe itself and appear before him who resolves on raising his family

kurals.chapter_en: The Way of Maintaining the Family
kurals.translit: Soozhaamal Thaane Mutiveydhum Thamkutiyaith / Thaazhaadhu Ugnatru Pavarkku
kurals.pope: Who labours for his race with unremitting pain, Without a thought spontaneously, his end will gain
kurals.drew: Those who are prompt in their efforts (to better their family) need no deliberation, such efforts will of themselves succeed

kurals.chapter_en: The Way of Maintaining the Family
kurals.translit: Kutram Ilanaaik Kutiseydhu Vaazhvaanaich / Chutramaach Chutrum Ulaku
kurals.pope: With blameless life who seeks to build his race's fame, The world shall circle him, and kindred claim
kurals.drew: People will eagerly seek the friendship of the prosperous soul who has raised his family without foul means

kurals.chapter_en: The Way of Maintaining the Family
kurals.translit: Nallaanmai Enpadhu Oruvarkuth Thaanpirandha / Illaanmai Aakkik Kolal
kurals.pope: Of virtuous manliness the world accords the praiseTo him who gives his powers, the house from which he sprang to raise
kurals.drew: A man's true manliness consists in making himself the head and benefactor of his family

kurals.chapter_en: The Way of Maintaining the Family
kurals.translit: Amarakaththu Vankannar Polath Thamarakaththum / Aatruvaar Metre Porai
kurals.pope: The fearless hero bears the brunt amid the warrior throng; Amid his kindred so the burthen rests upon the strong
kurals.drew: Amid his kindred so the burthen rests upon the strong

kurals.chapter_en: The Way of Maintaining the Family
kurals.translit: Kutiseyvaark Killai Paruvam Matiseydhu / Maanang Karudhak Ketum
kurals.pope: Wait for no season, when you would your house uprear;'Twill perish, if you wait supine, or hold your honour dear
kurals.drew: As a family suffers by (one's) indolence and false dignity there is to be so season (good or bad) to those who strive to raise their family

kurals.chapter_en: The Way of Maintaining the Family
kurals.translit: Itumpaikke Kolkalam Kollo Kutumpaththaik / Kutra Maraippaan Utampu
kurals.pope: Is not his body vase that various sorrows fill, Who would his household screen from every ill
kurals.drew: Is it only to suffering that his body is exposed who undertakes to preserve his family from evil ?

kurals.chapter_en: The Way of Maintaining the Family
kurals.translit: Itukkankaal Kondrita Veezhum Atuththoondrum / Nallaal Ilaadha Kuti
kurals.pope: When trouble the foundation saps the house must fall, If no strong hand be nigh to prop the tottering wall
kurals.drew: If there are none to prop up and maintain a family (in distress), it will fall at the stroke of the axe of misfortune

kurals.translit: Suzhandrumerp Pinnadhu Ulakam Adhanaal / Uzhandhum Uzhave Thalai
kurals.pope: Howe'er they roam, the world must follow still the plougher's team; Though toilsome, culture of the ground as noblest toil esteem
kurals.drew: Agriculture, though laborious, is the most excellent (form of labour); for people, though they go about (in search of various employments), have at last to resort to the farmer

kurals.translit: Uzhuvaar Ulakaththaarkku Aaniaq Thaatraadhu / Ezhuvaarai Ellaam Poruththu
kurals.pope: The ploughers are the linch-pin of the world; they bearThem up who other works perform, too weak its toils to share
kurals.drew: Agriculturists are (as it were) the linch-pin of the world for they support all other workers who cannot till the soil

kurals.translit: Uzhudhuntu Vaazhvaare Vaazhvaarmar Rellaam / Thozhudhuntu Pinsel Pavar
kurals.pope: Who ploughing eat their food, they truly live:The rest to others bend subservient, eating what they give
kurals.drew: They alone live who live by agriculture; all others lead a cringing, dependent life

kurals.translit: Palakutai Neezhalum Thangutaikkeezhk Kaanpar / Alakutai Neezha Lavar
kurals.pope: O'er many a land they 'll see their monarch reign, Whose fields are shaded by the waving grain
kurals.drew: Patriotic farmers desire to bring all other states under the control of their own king

kurals.translit: Iravaar Irappaarkkondru Eevar Karavaadhu / Kaiseydhoon Maalai Yavar
kurals.pope: They nothing ask from others, but to askers give, Who raise with their own hands the food on which they live
kurals.drew: Those whose nature is to live by manual labour will never beg but give something to those who beg

kurals.translit: Uzhavinaar Kaimmatangin Illai Vizhaivadhooum / Vittemen Paarkkum Nilai
kurals.pope: For those who 've left what all men love no place is found, When they with folded hands remain who till the ground
kurals.drew: If the farmer's hands are slackened, even the ascetic state will fail

kurals.translit: Thotippuzhudhi Kaqsaa Unakkin Pitiththeruvum / Ventaadhu Saalap Patum
kurals.pope: Reduce your soil to that dry state, When ounce is quarter-ounce's weight; Without one handful of manure, Abundant crops you thus secure
kurals.drew: If the land is dried so as to reduce one ounce of earth to a quarter, it will grow plentifully even without a handful of manure

kurals.translit: Erinum Nandraal Eruvitudhal Kattapin / Neerinum Nandradhan Kaappu
kurals.pope: To cast manure is better than to plough; Weed well; to guard is more than watering now
kurals.drew: Manuring is better than ploughing; after weeding, watching is better than watering (it)

kurals.translit: Sellaan Kizhavan Iruppin Nilampulandhu / Illaalin Ooti Vitum
kurals.pope: When master from the field aloof hath stood; Then land will sulk, like wife in angry mood
kurals.drew: If the owner does not (personally) attend to his cultivation, his land will behave like an angry wife and yield him no pleasure

kurals.translit: Ilamendru Asaii Iruppaaraik Kaanin / Nilamennum Nallaal Nakum
kurals.pope: The earth, that kindly dame, will laugh to see, Men seated idle pleading poverty
kurals.drew: The maiden, Earth, will laugh at the sight of those who plead poverty and lead an idle life

kurals.translit: Inmaiyin Innaadhadhu Yaadhenin Inmaiyin / Inmaiye Innaa Thadhu
kurals.pope: You ask what sharper pain than poverty is known; Nothing pains more than poverty, save poverty alone
kurals.drew: There is nothing that afflicts (one) like poverty

kurals.translit: Inmai Enavoru Paavi Marumaiyum / Immaiyum Indri Varum
kurals.pope: Malefactor matchless! poverty destroysThis world's and the next world's joys
kurals.drew: When cruel poverty comes on, it deprives one of both the present and future (bliss)

kurals.translit: Tholvaravum Tholum Ketukkum Thokaiyaaka / Nalkuravu Ennum Nasai
kurals.pope: Importunate desire, which poverty men name, Destroys both old descent and goodly fame
kurals.drew: Hankering poverty destroys at once the greatness of (one's) ancient descent and (the dignity of one's) speech

kurals.translit: Irpirandhaar Kanneyum Inmai Ilivandha / Sorpirakkum Sorvu Tharum
kurals.pope: From penury will spring, 'mid even those of noble race, Oblivion that gives birth to words that bring disgrace
kurals.drew: Even in those of high birth, poverty will produce the fault of uttering mean words

kurals.translit: Nalkuravu Ennum Itumpaiyul Palkuraith / Thunpangal Sendru Patum
kurals.pope: From poverty, that grievous woe, Attendant sorrows plenteous grow
kurals.drew: The misery of poverty brings in its train many (more) miseries

kurals.translit: Narporul Nankunarndhu Sollinum Nalkoorndhaar / Sorporul Sorvu Patum
kurals.pope: Though deepest sense, well understood, the poor man's words convey, Their sense from memory of mankind will fade away
kurals.drew: The words of the poor are profitless, though they may be sound in thought and clear in expression

kurals.translit: Aranjaaraa Nalkuravu Eendradhaa Yaanum / Piranpola Nokkap Patum
kurals.pope: From indigence devoid of virtue's grace, The mother e'en that bare, estranged, will turn her face
kurals.drew: He that is reduced to absolute poverty will be regarded as a stranger even by his own mother

kurals.translit: Indrum Varuvadhu Kollo Nerunalum / Kondradhu Polum Nirappu
kurals.pope: And will it come today as yesterday, The grief of want that eats my soul away
kurals.drew: Is the poverty that almost killed me yesterday, to meet me today too ?

kurals.translit: Neruppinul Thunjalum Aakum Nirappinul / Yaadhondrum Kanpaatu Aridhu
kurals.pope: Amid the flames sleep may men's eyelids close, In poverty the eye knows no repose
kurals.drew: One may sleep in the midst of fire; but by no means in the midst of poverty

kurals.translit: Thuppura Villaar Thuvarath Thuravaamai / Uppirkum Kaatikkum Kootru
kurals.pope: Unless the destitute will utterly themselves deny, They cause their neighbour's salt and vinegar to die
kurals.drew: The destitute poor, who do not renounce their bodies, only consume their neighbour's salt and water

kurals.translit: Irakka Iraththakkaark Kaanin Karappin / Avarpazhi Thampazhi Andru
kurals.pope: When those you find from whom 'tis meet to ask,- for aid apply; Theirs is the sin, not yours, if they the gift deny
kurals.drew: If you meet with those that may be begged of, you may beg; (but) if they withhold (their gift) it is their blame and not yours

kurals.translit: Inpam Oruvarku Iraththal Irandhavai / Thunpam Uraaa Varin
kurals.pope: Even to ask an alms may pleasure give, If what you ask without annoyance you receive
kurals.drew: Even begging may be pleasant, if what is begged for is obtained without grief (to him that begs)

kurals.translit: Karappilaa Nenjin Katanarivaar Munnindru / Irappumo Reer Utaiththu
kurals.pope: The men who nought deny, but know what's due, before their faceTo stand as suppliants affords especial grace
kurals.drew: There is even a beauty in standing before and begging of those who are liberal in their gifts and understand their duty (to beggars)

kurals.translit: Iraththalum Eedhale Polum Karaththal / Kanavilum Thetraadhaar Maattu
kurals.pope: Like giving alms, may even asking pleasant seem, From men who of denial never even dream
kurals.drew: To beg of such as never think of withholding (their charity) even in their dreams, is in fact the same as giving (it oneself);

kurals.translit: Karappilaar Vaiyakaththu Unmaiyaal Kannindru / Irappavar Merkol Vadhu
kurals.pope: Because on earth the men exist, who never say them nay, Men bear to stand before their eyes for help to pray
kurals.drew: As there are in the world those that give without refusing, there are (also) those that prefer to beg by simply standing before them

kurals.translit: Karappitumpai Yillaaraik Kaanin Nirappitumpai / Ellaam Orungu Ketum
kurals.pope: It those you find from evil of 'denial' free, At once all plague of poverty will flee
kurals.drew: All the evil of begging will be removed at the sight of those who are far from the evil of refusing

kurals.translit: Ikazhndhellaadhu Eevaaraik Kaanin Makizhndhullam / Ullul Uvappadhu Utaiththu
kurals.pope: If men are found who give and no harsh words of scorn employ, The minds of askers, through and through, will thrill with joy
kurals.drew: Beggars rejoice exceedingly when they behold those who bestow (their alms) with kindness and courtesy

kurals.translit: Irappaarai Illaayin Eernganmaa Gnaalam / Marappaavai Sendruvan Thatru
kurals.pope: If askers cease, the mighty earth, where cooling fountains flow, Will be a stage where wooden puppets come and go
kurals.drew: If there were no beggars, (the actions done in) the cool wide world would only resemble the movement of a puppet

kurals.translit: Eevaarkan Ennuntaam Thotram Irandhukol / Mevaar Ilaaak Katai
kurals.pope: What glory will there be to men of generous soul, When none are found to love the askers' role
kurals.drew: What (praise) would there be to givers (of alms) if there were no beggars to ask for and reveive (them)

kurals.translit: Irappaan Vekulaamai Ventum Nirappitumpai / Thaaneyum Saalum Kari
kurals.pope: Askers refused from wrath must stand aloof; The plague of poverty itself is ample proof
kurals.drew: He who begs ought not to be angry (at a refusal); for even the misery of (his own) poverty should be a sufficient reason (for so doing)

kurals.translit: Karavaadhu Uvandheeyum Kannannaar Kannum / Iravaamai Koti Urum
kurals.pope: Ten million-fold 'tis greater gain, asking no alms to live, Even from those, like eyes in worth, who nought concealing gladly give
kurals.drew: Not to beg (at all) even from those excellent persons who cheerfully give without refusing, will do immense good

kurals.translit: Irandhum Uyirvaazhdhal Ventin Parandhu / Ketuka Ulakiyatri Yaan
kurals.pope: If he that shaped the world desires that men should begging go, Through life's long course, let him a wanderer be and perish so
kurals.drew: If the Creator of the world has decreed even begging as a means of livelihood, may he too go abegging and perish

kurals.translit: Inmai Itumpai Irandhudheer Vaamennum / Vanmaiyin Vanpaatta Thil
kurals.pope: Nothing is harder than the hardness that will say,'The plague of penury by asking alms we'll drive away.'
kurals.drew: There is no greater folly than the boldness with which one seeks to remedy the evils of poverty by begging (rather than by working)

kurals.translit: Itamellaam Kollaath Thakaiththe Itamillaak / Kaalum Iravollaach Chaalpu
kurals.pope: Who ne'er consent to beg in utmost need, their worthHas excellence of greatness that transcends the earth
kurals.drew: Even the whole world cannot sufficiently praise the dignity that would not beg even in the midst of destitution

kurals.translit: Thenneer Atupurkai Aayinum Thaaldhandhadhu / Unnalin Oonginiya Thil
kurals.pope: Nothing is sweeter than to taste the toil-won cheer, Though mess of pottage as tasteless as the water clear
kurals.drew: Even thin gruel is ambrosia to him who has obtained it by labour

kurals.translit: Aavirku Neerendru Irappinum Naavirku / Iravin Ilivandha Thil
kurals.pope: E'en if a draught of water for a cow you ask, Nought's so distasteful to the tongue as beggar's task
kurals.drew: There is nothing more disgraceful to one's tongue than to use it in begging water even for a cow

kurals.translit: Irappan Irappaarai Ellaam Irappin / Karappaar Iravanmin Endru
kurals.pope: One thing I beg of beggars all, 'If beg ye may, Of those who hide their wealth, beg not, I pray.'
kurals.drew: I beseech all beggars and say, "If you need to beg, never beg of those who give unwillingly."

kurals.translit: Iravennum Emaappil Thoni Karavennum / Paardhaakkap Pakku Vitum
kurals.pope: The fragile bark of beggaryWrecked on denial's rock will lie
kurals.drew: The unsafe raft of begging will split when it strikes on the rock of refusal

kurals.translit: Iravulla Ullam Urukum Karavulla / Ulladhooum Indrik Ketum
kurals.pope: The heart will melt away at thought of beggary, With thought of stern repulse 'twill perish utterly
kurals.drew: To think of (the evil of) begging is enough to melt one's heart; but to think of refusal is enough to break it

kurals.translit: Karappavarkku Yaangolikkum Kollo Irappavar / Sollaatap Poom Uyir
kurals.pope: E'en as he asks, the shamefaced asker dies; Where shall his spirit hide who help denies
kurals.drew: Saying "No" to a beggar takes away his life. (but as that very word will kill the refuser) where then would the latter's life hide itself ?

kurals.translit: Makkale Polvar Kayavar Avaranna / Oppaari Yaanganta Thil
kurals.pope: The base resemble men in outward form, I ween; But counterpart exact to them I've never seen
kurals.drew: The base resemble men perfectly (as regards form); and we have not seen such (exact) resemblance (among any other species)

kurals.translit: Nandrari Vaarir Kayavar Thiruvutaiyar / Nenjaththu Avalam Ilar
kurals.pope: Than those of grateful heart the base must luckier be, Their minds from every anxious thought are free
kurals.drew: The low enjoy more felicity than those who know what is good; for the former are not troubled with anxiety (as to the good)

kurals.translit: Thevar Anaiyar Kayavar Avarundhaam / Mevana Seydhozhuka Laan
kurals.pope: The base are as the Gods; they tooDo ever what they list to do
kurals.drew: The base resemble the Gods; for the base act as they like

kurals.translit: Akappatti Aavaaraik Kaanin Avarin / Mikappattuch Chemmaakkum Keezh
kurals.pope: When base men those behold of conduct vile, They straight surpass them, and exulting smile
kurals.drew: The base feels proud when he sees persons whose acts meaner than his own

kurals.translit: Achchame Keezhkaladhu Aasaaram Echcham / Avaavuntel Untaam Siridhu
kurals.pope: Fear is the base man's virtue; if that fail, Intense desire some little may avail
kurals.drew: (The principle of) behaviour in the mean is chiefly fear; if not, hope of gain, to some extent

kurals.translit: Araiparai Annar Kayavardhaam Ketta / Maraipirarkku Uyththuraikka Laan
kurals.pope: The base are like the beaten drum; for, when they hearThe sound the secret out in every neighbour's ear
kurals.drew: The base are like a drum that is beaten, for they unburden to others the secrets they have heard

kurals.translit: Eerngai Vidhiraar Kayavar Kotirutaikkum / Koonkaiyar Allaa Thavarkku
kurals.pope: From off their moistened hands no clinging grain they shake, Unless to those with clenched fist their jaws who break
kurals.drew: The mean will not (even) shake off (what sticks to) their hands (soon after a meal) to any but those who would break their jaws with their clenched fists

kurals.translit: Sollap Payanpatuvar Saandror Karumpupol / Kollap Payanpatum Keezh
kurals.pope: The good to those will profit yield fair words who use; The base, like sugar-cane, will profit those who bruise
kurals.drew: The great bestow (their alms) as soon as they are informed; (but) the mean, like the sugar-cane, only when they are tortured to death

kurals.translit: Utuppadhooum Unpadhooum Kaanin Pirarmel / Vatukkaana Vatraakum Keezh
kurals.pope: If neighbours clothed and fed he see, the baseIs mighty man some hidden fault to trace
kurals.drew: The base will bring an evil (accusation) against others, as soon as he sees them (enjoying) good food

kurals.translit: Etrir Kuriyar Kayavarondru Utrakkaal / Vitrarku Uriyar Viraindhu
kurals.pope: For what is base man fit, if griefs assail?Himself to offer, there and then, for sale
kurals.drew: The base will hasten to sell themselves as soon as a calamity has befallen them. For what else are they fitted ?

kurals.translit: Anangukol Aaimayil Kollo Kananguzhai / Maadharkol Maalum En Nenju
kurals.pope: Goddess? or peafowl rare? She whose ears rich jewels wear, Is she a maid of human kind? All wildered is my mind
kurals.drew: Is this jewelled female a celestial, a choice peahen, or a human being ? My mind is perplexed

kurals.translit: Nokkinaal Nokkedhir Nokkudhal Thaakkanangu / Thaanaikkon Tanna Thutaiththu
kurals.pope: She of the beaming eyes, To my rash look her glance replies, As if the matchless goddess' hand Led forth an armed band
kurals.drew: This female beauty returning my looks is like a celestial maiden coming with an army to contend against me

kurals.translit: Pantariyen Kootren Padhanai Iniyarindhen / Pentakaiyaal Peramark Kattu
kurals.pope: Death's form I formerly Knew not; but now 'tis plain to me; He comes in lovely maiden's guise, With soul-subduing eyes
kurals.drew: I never knew before what is called Yama; I see it now; it is the eyes that carry on a great fight with (the help of) female qualities

kurals.translit: Kantaar Uyirunnum Thotraththaal Pentakaip / Pedhaikku Amarththana Kan
kurals.pope: In sweet simplicity, A woman's gracious form hath she; But yet those eyes, that drink my life, Are with the form at strife
kurals.drew: These eyes that seem to kill those who look at them are as it were in hostilities with this feminine simplicity

kurals.translit: Kootramo Kanno Pinaiyo Matavaral / Nokkamim Moondrum Utaiththu
kurals.pope: The light that on me gleams, Is it death's dart? or eye's bright beams?Or fawn's shy glance? All three appear In form of maiden here
kurals.drew: Is it Yama, (a pair of) eyes or a hind ?- Are not all these three in the looks of this maid ?

kurals.translit: Kotumpuruvam Kotaa Maraippin Natungagnar / Seyyala Manival Kan
kurals.pope: If cruel eye-brow's bow, Unbent, would veil those glances now; The shafts that wound this trembling heart Her eyes no more would dart
kurals.drew: Her eyes will cause (me) no trembling sorrow, if they are properly hidden by her cruel arched eyebrows

kurals.translit: Kataaak Kalitrinmer Katpataam Maadhar / Pataaa Mulaimel Thukil
kurals.pope: As veil o'er angry eyes Of raging elephant that lies, The silken cincture's folds invest This maiden's panting breast
kurals.drew: The cloth that covers the firm bosom of this maiden is (like) that which covers the eyes of a rutting elephant

kurals.translit: Onnudhar Koo Utaindhadhe Gnaatpinul / Nannaarum Utkumen Peetu
kurals.pope: Ah woe is me my might, That awed my foemen in the fight, By lustre of that beaming brow Borne down, lies broken now
kurals.drew: On her bright brow alone is destroyed even that power of mine that used to terrify the most fearless

kurals.translit: Pinaiyer Matanokkum Naanum Utaiyaatku / Aniyevano Edhila Thandhu
kurals.pope: Like tender fawn's her eye; Clothed on is she with modesty; What added beauty can be lent; By alien ornament
kurals.drew: Of what use are other jewels to her who is adorned with modesty, and the meek looks of a hind ?

kurals.translit: Untaarkan Alladhu Atunaraak Kaamampol / Kantaar Makizhseydhal Indru
kurals.pope: The palm-tree's fragrant wine, To those who taste yields joys divine; But love hath rare felicity For those that only see
kurals.drew: Unlike boiled honey which yields delight only when it is drunk, love gives pleasure even when looked at

kurals.translit: Irunokku Ivalunkan Ulladhu Orunokku / Noinokkon Rannoi Marundhu
kurals.pope: A double witchery have glances of her liquid eye; One glance is glance that brings me pain; the other heals again
kurals.drew: There are two looks in the dyed eyes of this (fair one); one causes pain, and the other is the cure thereof

kurals.translit: Kankalavu Kollum Sirunokkam Kaamaththil / Sempaakam Andru Peridhu
kurals.pope: The furtive glance, that gleams one instant bright, Is more than half of love's supreme delight
kurals.drew: A single stolen glance of her eyes is more than half the pleasure (of sexual embrace)

kurals.translit: Nokkinaal Nokki Irainjinaal Aqdhaval / Yaappinul Attiya Neer
kurals.pope: She looked, and looking drooped her head:On springing shoot of love 'its water shed
kurals.drew: She has looked (at men) and stooped (her head); and that (sign) waters as it were (the corn of) our love

kurals.translit: Yaannokkum Kaalai Nilannokkum Nokkaakkaal / Thaannokki Mella Nakum
kurals.pope: I look on her: her eyes are on the ground the while:I look away: she looks on me with timid smile
kurals.drew: When I look, she looks down; when I do not, she looks and smiles gently

kurals.translit: Kurikkontu Nokkaamai Allaal Orukan / Sirakkaniththaal Pola Nakum
kurals.pope: She seemed to see me not; but yet the maidHer love, by smiling side-long glance, betrayed
kurals.drew: She not only avoids a direct look at me, but looks as it were with a half-closed eye and smiles

kurals.translit: Uraaa Thavarpol Solinum Seraaarsol / Ollai Unarap Patum
kurals.pope: Though with their lips affection they disown, Yet, when they hate us not, 'tis quickly known
kurals.drew: Though they may speak harshly as if they were strangers, the words of the friendly are soon understood

kurals.translit: Seraaach Chirusollum Setraarpol Nokkum / Uraaarpondru Utraar Kurippu
kurals.pope: The slighting words that anger feign, while eyes their love revealAre signs of those that love, but would their love conceal
kurals.drew: Little words that are harsh and looks that are hateful are (but) the expressions of lovers who wish to act like strangers

kurals.translit: Asaiyiyarku Untaantor Eeryaan Nokkap / Pasaiyinal Paiya Nakum
kurals.pope: I gaze, the tender maid relents the while; And, oh the matchless grace of that soft smile
kurals.drew: When I look, the pitying maid looks in return and smiles gently; and that is a comforting sign for me

kurals.translit: Edhilaar Polap Podhunokku Nokkudhal / Kaadhalaar Kanne Ula
kurals.pope: The look indifferent, that would its love disguise, Is only read aright by lovers' eyes
kurals.drew: Both the lovers are capable of looking at each other in an ordinary way, as if they were perfect strangers

kurals.translit: Kannotu Kaninai Nokkokkin Vaaichchorkal / Enna Payanum Ila
kurals.pope: When eye to answering eye reveals the tale of love, All words that lips can say must useless prove
kurals.drew: The words of the mouths are of no use whatever, when there is perfect agreement between the eyes (of lovers)

kurals.translit: Kantukettu Untuyirththu Utrariyum Aimpulanum / Ondhoti Kanne Ula
kurals.pope: All joys that senses five- sight, hearing, taste, smell, touch- can give, In this resplendent armlets-bearing damsel live
kurals.drew: The (simultaneous) enjoyment of the five senses of sight, hearing, taste, smell and touch can only be found with bright braceleted (women)

kurals.translit: Pinikku Marundhu Piraman Aniyizhai / Thannoikkuth Thaane Marundhu
kurals.pope: Disease and medicine antagonists we surely see; This maid, to pain she gives, herself is remedy
kurals.drew: The remedy for a disease is always something different (from it); but for the disease caused by this jewelled maid, she is herself the cure

kurals.translit: Thaamveezhvaar Mendrol Thuyilin Inidhukol / Thaamaraik Kannaan Ulaku
kurals.pope: Than rest in her soft arms to whom the soul is giv'n, Is any sweeter joy in his, the Lotus-eyed-one's heaven
kurals.drew: Can the lotus-eyed Vishnu's heaven be indeed as sweet to those who delight to sleep in the delicate arms of their beloved ?

kurals.translit: Neengin Theruum Kurukungaal Thannennum / Theeyaantup Petraal Ival?
kurals.pope: Withdraw, it burns; approach, it soothes the pain; Whence did the maid this wondrous fire obtain
kurals.drew: From whence has she got this fire that burns when I withdraw and cools when I approach ?

kurals.translit: Vetta Pozhudhin Avaiyavai Polume / Thottaar Kadhuppinaal Thol
kurals.pope: In her embrace, whose locks with flowery wreaths are bound, Each varied form of joy the soul can wish is found
kurals.drew: Each varied form of joy the soul can wish is found

kurals.translit: Urudhoru Uyirdhalirppath Theentalaal Pedhaikku / Amizhdhin Iyandrana Thol
kurals.pope: Ambrosia are the simple maiden's arms; when I attainTheir touch, my withered life puts forth its buds again
kurals.drew: The shoulders of this fair one are made of ambrosia, for they revive me with pleasure every time I embrace them

kurals.translit: Thammil Irundhu Thamadhupaaththu Untatraal / Ammaa Arivai Muyakku
kurals.pope: As when one eats from household store, with kindly graceSharing his meal: such is this golden maid's embrace
kurals.drew: The embraces of a gold-complexioned beautiful female are as pleasant as to dwell in one's own house and live by one's own (earnings) after distributing (a portion of it in charity)

kurals.translit: Veezhum Iruvarkku Inidhe Valiyitai / Pozhap Pataaa Muyakku
kurals.pope: Sweet is the strict embrace of those whom fond affection binds, Where no dissevering breath of discord entrance finds
kurals.drew: To ardent lovers sweet is the embrace that cannot be penetrated even by a breath of breeze

kurals.translit: Ootal Unardhal Punardhal Ivaikaamam / Kootiyaar Petra Payan
kurals.pope: The jealous variance, the healing of the strife, reunion gained:These are the fruits from wedded love obtained
kurals.drew: Love quarrel, reconciliation and intercourse - these are the advantages reaped by those who marry for lust

kurals.translit: Aridhoru Ariyaamai Kantatraal Kaamam / Seridhorum Seyizhai Maattu
kurals.pope: The more men learn, the more their lack of learning they detect;'Tis so when I approach the maid with gleaming jewels decked
kurals.drew: As (one's) ignorance is discovered the more one learns, so does repeated intercourse with a welladorned female (only create a desire for more)

kurals.translit: Nanneerai Vaazhi Anichchame Ninninum / Menneeral Yaamveezh Paval
kurals.pope: O flower of the sensitive plant! than theeMore tender's the maiden beloved by me
kurals.drew: May you flourish, O Anicham! you have a delicate nature But my beloved is more delicate than you

kurals.translit: Malarkaanin Maiyaaththi Nenje Ivalkan / Palarkaanum Poovokkum Endru
kurals.pope: You deemed, as you saw the flowers, her eyes were as flowers, my soul, That many may see; it was surely some folly that over you stole
kurals.drew: O my soul, fancying that flowers which are seen by many can resemble her eyes, you become confused at the sight of them

kurals.translit: Murimeni Muththam Muruval Verinaatram / Velunkan Veyththo Lavatku
kurals.pope: As tender shoot her frame; teeth, pearls; around her odours blend; Darts are the eyes of her whose shoulders like the bambu bend
kurals.drew: The complexion of this bamboo-shouldered one is that of a shoot; her teeth, are pearls; her breath,

kurals.translit: Kaanin Kuvalai Kavizhndhu Nilannokkum / Maanizhai Kannovvem Endru
kurals.pope: The lotus, seeing her, with head demiss, the ground would eye, And say, 'With eyes of her, rich gems who wears, we cannot vie.'
kurals.drew: If the blue lotus could see, it would stoop and look at the ground saying, "I can never resemble the eyes of this excellent jewelled one."

kurals.translit: Anichchappook Kaalkalaiyaal Peydhaal Nukappirku / Nalla Pataaa Parai
kurals.pope: The flowers of the sensitive plant as a girdle around her she placed; The stems she forgot to nip off; they 'll weigh down the delicate waist
kurals.drew: No merry drums will be beaten for the (tender) waist of her who has adorned herself with the anicham without having removed its stem

kurals.translit: Madhiyum Matandhai Mukanum Ariyaa / Padhiyin Kalangiya Meen
kurals.pope: The stars perplexed are rushing wildly from their spheres; For like another moon this maiden's face appears
kurals.drew: The stars have become confused in their places not being able to distinguish between the moon and the maid's countenance

kurals.translit: Aruvaai Niraindha Avirmadhikkup Pola / Maruvunto Maadhar Mukaththu
kurals.pope: In moon, that waxing waning shines, as sports appear, Are any spots discerned in face of maiden here
kurals.drew: Could there be spots in the face of this maid like those in the bright full moon ?

kurals.translit: Maadhar Mukampol Olivita Vallaiyel / Kaadhalai Vaazhi Madhi
kurals.pope: Farewell, O moon! If that thine orb could shineBright as her face, thou shouldst be love of mine
kurals.drew: If you can indeed shine like the face of women, flourish, O moon, for then would you be worth loving ?

kurals.translit: Malaranna Kannaal Mukamoththi Yaayin / Palarkaanath Thondral Madhi
kurals.pope: If as her face, whose eyes are flowers, thou wouldst have charms for me, Shine for my eyes alone, O moon, shine not for all to see
kurals.drew: O moon, if you wish to resemble the face of her whose eyes are like (these) flowers, do not appear so as to be seen by all

kurals.translit: Anichchamum Annaththin Thooviyum Maadhar / Atikku Nerunjip Pazham
kurals.pope: The flower of the sensitive plant, and the down on the swan's white breast, As the thorn are harsh, by the delicate feet of this maiden pressed
kurals.drew: The anicham and the feathers of the swan are to the feet of females, like the fruit of the (thorny) Nerunji

kurals.translit: Paalotu Thenkalan Thatre Panimozhi / Vaaleyiru Ooriya Neer
kurals.pope: The dew on her white teeth, whose voice is soft and low, Is as when milk and honey mingled flow
kurals.drew: The water which oozes from the white teeth of this soft speeched damsel is like a mixture of milk and honey

kurals.translit: Utampotu Uyiritai Ennamar Ranna / Matandhaiyotu Emmitai Natpu
kurals.pope: Between this maid and me the friendship kindIs as the bonds that soul and body bind
kurals.drew: The love between me and this damsel is like the union of body and soul

kurals.translit: Karumaniyir Paavaainee Podhaayaam Veezhum / Thirunudharku Illai Itam
kurals.pope: For her with beauteous brow, the maid I love, there place is none; To give her image room, O pupil of mine eye, begone
kurals.drew: O you image in the pupil (of my eye)! depart; there is no room for (my) fair-browed beloved

kurals.translit: Vaazhdhal Uyirkkannal Aayizhai Saadhal / Adharkannal Neengum Itaththu
kurals.pope: Life is she to my very soul when she draws nigh; Dissevered from the maid with jewels rare, I die
kurals.drew: My fair-jewelled one resembles the living soul (when she is in union with me), the dying soul when she leaves me

kurals.translit: Ulluvan Manyaan Marappin Marappariyen / Ollamark Kannaal Kunam
kurals.pope: I might recall, if I could once forget; but from my heartHer charms fade not, whose eyes gleam like the warrior's dart
kurals.drew: If I had forgotten her who has bright battling eyes, I would have remembered (thee); but I never forget her (Thus says he to her maid)

kurals.translit: Kannullin Pokaar Imaippin Parukuvaraa / Nunniyarem Kaadha Lavar
kurals.pope: My loved one's subtle form departs not from my eyes; I wink them not, lest I should pain him where he lies
kurals.drew: My lover would not depart from mine eyes; even if I wink, he would not suffer (from pain); he is so ethereal

kurals.translit: Kannullaar Kaadha Lavaraakak Kannum / Ezhudhem Karappaakku Arindhu
kurals.pope: My love doth ever in my eyes reside; I stain them not, fearing his form to hide
kurals.drew: As my lover abides in my eyes, I will not even paint them, for he would (then) have to conceal himself

kurals.translit: Nenjaththaar Kaadha Lavaraaka Veydhuntal / Anjudhum Vepaak Karindhu
kurals.pope: Within my heart my lover dwells; from food I turnThat smacks of heat, lest he should feel it burn
kurals.drew: As my lover is in my heart, I am afraid of eating (anything) hot, for I know it would pain him

kurals.translit: Imaippin Karappaakku Arival Anaiththirke / Edhilar Ennum Iv Voor
kurals.pope: I fear his form to hide, nor close my eyes:'Her love estranged is gone!' the village cries
kurals.drew: I will not wink, knowing that if I did, my lover would hide himself; and for this reason, this town says, he is unloving

kurals.translit: Uvandhuraivar Ullaththul Endrum Ikandhuraivar / Edhilar Ennum Iv Voor
kurals.pope: Rejoicing in my very soul he ever lies;'Her love estranged is gone far off!' the village cries
kurals.drew: My lover dwells in my heart with perpetual delight; but the town says he is unloving and (therefore) dwells afar

kurals.translit: Kaamam Uzhandhu Varundhinaarkku Emam / Matalalladhu Illai Vali
kurals.pope: To those who 've proved love's joy, and now afflicted mourn, Except the helpful 'horse of palm', no other strength remains
kurals.drew: To those who after enjoyment of sexual pleasure suffer (for want of more), there is no help so efficient as the palmyra horse

kurals.translit: Nonaa Utampum Uyirum Matalerum / Naaninai Neekki Niruththu
kurals.pope: My body and my soul, that can no more endure, Will lay reserve aside, and mount the 'horse of palm'
kurals.drew: Having got rid of shame, the suffering body and soul save themselves on the palmyra horse

kurals.translit: Naanotu Nallaanmai Pantutaiyen Indrutaiyen / Kaamutraar Erum Matal
kurals.pope: I once retained reserve and seemly manliness; To-day I nought possess but lovers' 'horse of palm'
kurals.drew: Modesty and manliness were once my own; now, my own is the palmyra horse that is ridden by the lustful

kurals.translit: Kaamak Katumpunal Uykkum Naanotu / Nallaanmai Ennum Punai
kurals.pope: Love's rushing tide will sweep away the raftOf seemly manliness and shame combined
kurals.drew: The raft of modesty and manliness, is, alas, carried-off by the strong current of lust

kurals.translit: Thotalaik Kurundhoti Thandhaal Matalotu / Maalai Uzhakkum Thuyar
kurals.pope: The maid that slender armlets wears, like flowers entwined, Has brought me 'horse of palm,' and pangs of eventide
kurals.drew: She with the small garland-like bracelets has given me the palmyra horse and the sorrow that is endured at night

kurals.translit: Mataloordhal Yaamaththum Ulluven Mandra / Patalollaa Pedhaikken Kan
kurals.pope: Of climbing 'horse of palm' in midnight hour, I think; My eyes know no repose for that same simple maid
kurals.drew: Mine eyes will not close in sleep on your mistress's account; even at midnight will I think of mounting the palmyra horse

kurals.translit: Katalanna Kaamam Uzhandhum Mataleraap / Pennin Perundhakka Thil
kurals.pope: There's nought of greater worth than woman's long-enduring soul, Who, vexed by love like ocean waves, climbs not the 'horse of palm'
kurals.drew: There is nothing so noble as the womanly nature that would not ride the palmyra horse, though plunged a sea of lust

kurals.translit: Niraiyariyar Manaliyar Ennaadhu Kaamam / Maraiyirandhu Mandru Patum
kurals.pope: In virtue hard to move, yet very tender, too, are we; Love deems not so, would rend the veil, and court publicity
kurals.drew: Even the Lust (of women) transgresses its secrecy and appears in public, forgetting that they are too chaste and liberal (to be overcome by it)

kurals.translit: Arikilaar Ellaarum Endreen Kaamam / Marukin Marukum Maruntu
kurals.pope: 'There's no one knows my heart,' so says my love, And thus, in public ways, perturbed will rove
kurals.drew: And thus, in public ways, perturbed will rove

kurals.translit: Yaamkannin Kaana Nakupa Arivillaar / Yaampatta Thaampataa Aaru
kurals.pope: Before my eyes the foolish make a mock of me, Because they ne'er endured the pangs I now must drie
kurals.drew: Even strangers laugh (at us) so as to be seen by us, for they have not suffered

kurals.translit: Alarezha Aaruyir Na�rkum Adhanaip / Palarariyaar Paakkiyath Thaal
kurals.pope: By this same rumour's rise, my precious life stands fast; Good fortune grant the many know this not
kurals.drew: My precious life is saved by the raise of rumour, and this, to my good luck no others are aware of

kurals.translit: Malaranna Kannaal Arumai Ariyaadhu / Alaremakku Eendhadhiv Voor
kurals.pope: The village hath to us this rumour giv'n, that makes her mine; Unweeting all the rareness of the maid with flower-like eyne
kurals.drew: Not knowing the value of her whose eyes are like flowers this town has got up a rumour about me

kurals.translit: Uraaadho Oorarindha Kelavai Adhanaip / Peraaadhu Petranna Neerththu
kurals.pope: The rumour spread within the town, is it not gain to me?It is as though that were obtained that may not be
kurals.drew: Will I not get a rumour that is known to the (whole) town ? For what I have not got is as if I had got it (already)

kurals.translit: Kavvaiyaal Kavvidhu Kaamam Adhuvindrel / Thavvennum Thanmai Izhandhu
kurals.pope: The rumour rising makes my love to rise; My love would lose its power and languish otherwise
kurals.drew: Rumour increases the violence of my passion; without it it would grow weak and waste away

kurals.translit: Kaliththorum Kalluntal Vettatraal Kaamam / Velippatun Thorum Inidhu
kurals.pope: The more man drinks, the more he ever drunk would be; The more my love's revealed, the sweeter 'tis to me
kurals.drew: As drinking liquor is delightful (to one) whenever one is in mirth, so is lust delightful to me whenever it is the subject of rumour

kurals.translit: Kantadhu Mannum Orunaal Alarmannum / Thingalaip Paampukon Tatru
kurals.pope: I saw him but one single day: rumour spreads soonAs darkness, when the dragon seizes on the moon
kurals.drew: It was but a single day that I looked on (my lover); but the rumour thereof has spread like the seizure of the moon by the serpent

kurals.translit: Ooravar Kelavai Eruvaaka Annaisol / Neeraaka Neelumin Noi
kurals.pope: My anguish grows apace: the town's reportManures it; my mother's word doth water it
kurals.drew: This malady (of lust) is manured by the talk of women and watered by the (harsh) words of my mother

kurals.translit: Neyyaal Erinudhuppem Endratraal Kelavaiyaal / Kaamam Nudhuppem Enal
kurals.pope: With butter-oil extinguish fire! 'Twill proveHarder by scandal to extinguish love
kurals.drew: To say that one could extinguish passion by rumour is like extinguishing fire with ghee

kurals.translit: Alarnaana Olvadho Anjalompu Endraar / Palarnaana Neeththak Katai
kurals.pope: When he who said 'Fear not!' hath left me blamed, While many shrink, can I from rumour hide ashamed
kurals.drew: When the departure of him who said "fear not" has put me to shame before others, why need I be ashamed of scandal

kurals.translit: Thaamventin Nalkuvar Kaadhalar Yaamventum / Kelavai Etukkumiv Voor
kurals.pope: If we desire, who loves will grant what we require; This town sends forth the rumour we desire
kurals.drew: The rumour I desire is raised by the town (itself); and my lover would if desired consent (to my following him)

kurals.translit: Sellaamai Untel Enakkurai Matrunin / Valvaravu Vaazhvaark Kurai
kurals.pope: If you will say, 'I leave thee not,' then tell me so; Of quick return tell those that can survive this woe
kurals.drew: If it is not departure, tell me; but if it is your speedy return, tell it to those who would be alive then

kurals.translit: Inkan Utaiththavar Paarval Pirivanjum / Punkan Utaiththaal Punarvu
kurals.pope: It once was perfect joy to look upon his face; But now the fear of parting saddens each embrace
kurals.drew: His very look was once pleasing; but (now) even intercourse is painful through fear of separation

kurals.translit: Aridharo Thetram Arivutaiyaar Kannum / Pirivo Ritaththunmai Yaan
kurals.pope: To trust henceforth is hard, if ever he depart, E'en he, who knows his promise and my breaking heart
kurals.drew: As even the lover who understands (everything) may at times depart, confidence is hardly possible

kurals.translit: Aliththanjal Endravar Neeppin Theliththasol / Theriyaarkku Unto Thavaru
kurals.pope: If he depart, who fondly said, 'Fear not,' what blame's incurredBy those who trusted to his reassuring word
kurals.drew: If he who bestowed his love and said "fear not" should depart, will it be the fault of those who believed in (his) assuring words ?

kurals.translit: Ompin Amaindhaar Pirivompal Matravar / Neengin Aridhaal Punarvu
kurals.pope: If you would guard my life, from going him restrainWho fills my life! If he depart, hardly we meet again
kurals.drew: If you would save (my life), delay the departure of my destined (husband); for if he departs, intercourse will become impossible

kurals.translit: Pirivuraikkum Vankannar Aayin Aridhavar / Nalkuvar Ennum Nasai
kurals.pope: To cherish longing hope that he should ever gracious be, Is hard, when he could stand, and of departure speak to me
kurals.drew: Is hard, when he could stand, and of departure speak to me

kurals.translit: Thuraivan Thurandhamai Thootraakol Munkai / Iraiiravaa Nindra Valai
kurals.pope: The bracelet slipping from my wrist announced beforeDeparture of the Prince that rules the ocean shore
kurals.drew: Do not the rings that begin to slide down my fingers forebode the separation of my lord ?

kurals.translit: Innaadhu Inaniloor Vaazhdhal Adhaninum / Innaadhu Iniyaarp Pirivu
kurals.pope: 'Tis sad to sojourn in the town where no kind kinsmen dwell;'Tis sadder still to bid a friend beloved farewell
kurals.drew: Painful is it to live in a friendless town; but far more painful is it to part from one's lover

kurals.translit: Thotirsutin Alladhu Kaamanoi Pola / Vitirsutal Aatrumo Thee
kurals.pope: Fire burns the hands that touch; but smart of loveWill burn in hearts that far away remove
kurals.drew: Fire burns when touched; but, like the sickness of love, can it also burn when removed ?

kurals.translit: Aridhaatri Allalnoi Neekkip Pirivaatrip / Pinirundhu Vaazhvaar Palar
kurals.pope: Sorrow's sadness meek sustaining, Driving sore distress away, Separation uncomplaining Many bear the livelong day
kurals.drew: As if there were many indeed that can consent to the impossible, kill their pain, endure separation and yet continue to live afterwards

kurals.translit: Maraippenman Yaaniqdho Noyai Iraippavarkku / Ootruneer Pola Mikum
kurals.pope: I would my pain conceal, but see! it surging swells, As streams to those that draw from ever-springing wells
kurals.drew: I would hide this pain from others; but it (only) swells like a spring to those who drain it

kurals.translit: Karaththalum Aatrenin Noyainoi Seydhaarkku / Uraiththalum Naanuth Tharum
kurals.pope: I cannot hide this pain of mine, yet shame restrainsWhen I would tell it out to him who caused my pains
kurals.drew: I cannot conceal this pain, nor can I relate it without shame to him who has caused it

kurals.translit: Kaamamum Naanum Uyirkaavaath Thoongumen / Nonaa Utampin Akaththu
kurals.pope: My soul, like porter's pole, within my wearied frame, Sustains a two-fold burthen poised, of love and shame
kurals.drew: (Both) lust and shame, with my soul for their shoulder pole balance themselves on a body that cannot bear them

kurals.translit: Kaamak Katalmannum Unte Adhuneendhum / Emap Punaimannum Il
kurals.pope: A sea of love, 'tis true, I see stretched out before, But not the trusty bark that wafts to yonder shore
kurals.drew: There is indeed a flood of lust; but there is no raft of safety to cross it with

kurals.translit: Thuppin Evanaavar Mankol Thuyarvaravu / Natpinul Aatru Pavar
kurals.pope: Who work us woe in friendship's trustful hour, What will they prove when angry tempests lower
kurals.drew: What will they prove when angry tempests lower?

kurals.translit: Inpam Katalmatruk Kaamam Aqdhatungaal / Thunpam Adhanir Peridhu
kurals.pope: A happy love 's sea of joy; but mightier sorrows rollFrom unpropitious love athwart the troubled soul
kurals.drew: The pleasure of lust is (as great as) the sea; but the pain of lust is far greater

kurals.translit: Kaamak Katumpunal Neendhik Karaikaanen / Yaamaththum Yaane Ulen
kurals.pope: I swim the cruel tide of love, and can no shore descry, In watches of the night, too, 'mid the waters, only I
kurals.drew: I have swam across the terrible flood of lust, but have not seen its shore; even at midnight I am alone; still I live

kurals.translit: Mannuyir Ellaam Thuyitri Aliththiraa / Ennalladhu Illai Thunai
kurals.pope: All living souls in slumber soft she steeps; But me alone kind night for her companing keeps
kurals.drew: The night which graciously lulls to sleep all living creatures, has me alone for her companion

kurals.translit: Kotiyaar Kotumaiyin Thaamkotiya Innaal / Netiya Kazhiyum Iraa
kurals.pope: More cruel than the cruelty of him, the cruel one, In these sad times are lengthening hours of night I watch alone
kurals.drew: The long nights of these days are far more cruel than the heartless one who is torturing me

kurals.translit: Ullampondru Ulvazhich Chelkirpin Vellaneer / Neendhala Mannoen Kan
kurals.pope: When eye of mine would as my soul go forth to him, It knows not how through floods of its own tears to swim
kurals.drew: Could mine eyes travel like my thoughts to the abode (of my absent lord), they would not swim in this flood of tears

kurals.translit: Kandhaam Kaluzhva Thevankolo Thantaanoi / Thaamkaatta Yaamkan Tadhu
kurals.pope: They showed me him, and then my endless painI saw: why then should weeping eyes complain
kurals.drew: As this incurable malady has been caused by my eyes which showed (him) to me, why should they now weep for (him)

kurals.translit: Therindhunaraa Nokkiya Unkan Parindhunaraap / Paidhal Uzhappadhu Evan?
kurals.pope: How glancing eyes, that rash unweeting looked that day, With sorrow measureless are wasting now away
kurals.drew: The dyed eyes that (then) looked without foresight, why should they now endure sorrow, without feeling sharply (their own fault)

kurals.translit: Kadhumenath Thaanokkith Thaame Kaluzhum / Ithunakath Thakka Thutaiththu
kurals.pope: The eyes that threw such eager glances round erewhileAre weeping now. Such folly surely claims a smile
kurals.drew: They themselves looked eagerly (on him) and now they weep. Is not this to be laughed at ?

kurals.translit: Peyalaatraa Neerulandha Unkan Uyalaatraa / Uyvilnoi Enkan Niruththu
kurals.pope: Those eyes have wept till all the fount of tears is dry, That brought upon me pain that knows no remedy
kurals.drew: These painted eyes have caused me a lasting mortal disease; and now they can weep no more, the tears having dried up

kurals.translit: Patalaatraa Paidhal Uzhakkum Katalaatraak / Kaamanoi Seydhaen Kan
kurals.pope: The eye that wrought me more than sea could hold of woes, Is suffering pangs that banish all repose
kurals.drew: Mine eyes have caused me a lust that is greater than the sea and (they themselves) endure the torture of sleeplessness

kurals.translit: Oo Inidhe Emakkinnoi Seydhakan / Thaaam Itharpat Tadhu
kurals.pope: Oho! how sweet a thing to see! the eyeThat wrought this pain, in the same gulf doth lie
kurals.drew: The eyes that have given me this disease have themselves been seized with this (suffering) Oh! I am much delighted

kurals.translit: Uzhandhuzhan Thulneer Aruka Vizhaindhizhaindhu / Venti Avarkkanta Kan
kurals.pope: Aching, aching, let those exhaust their stream, That melting, melting, that day gazed on him
kurals.drew: The eyes that became tender and gazed intently on him, may they suffer so much as to dry up the fountain of their tears

kurals.translit: Penaadhu Pettaar Ularmanno Matravark / Kaanaadhu Amaivila Kan
kurals.pope: Who loved me once, onloving now doth here remain; Not seeing him, my eye no rest can gain
kurals.drew: He is indeed here who loved me with his lips but not with his heart but mine eyes suffer from not seeing him

kurals.translit: Vaaraakkaal Thunjaa Varindhunjaa Aayitai / Aaragnar Utrana Kan
kurals.pope: When he comes not, all slumber flies; no sleep when he is there; Thus every way my eyes have troubles hard to bear
kurals.drew: When he is away they do not sleep; when he is present they do not sleep; in either case, mine eyes endure unbearable agony

kurals.translit: Maraiperal Ooraarkku Aridhandraal Empol / Araiparai Kannaar Akaththu
kurals.pope: It is not hard for all the town the knowledge to obtain, When eyes, as mine, like beaten tambours, make the mystery plain
kurals.drew: It is not difficult for the people of this place to understand the secret of those whose eyes, like mine, are as it were beaten drums

kurals.translit: Nayandhavarkku Nalkaamai Nerndhen Pasandhaven / Panpiyaarkku Uraikko Pira
kurals.pope: I willed my lover absent should remain; Of pining's sickly hue to whom shall I complain
kurals.drew: I who (then) consented to the absence of my loving lord, to whom can I (now) relate the fact of my having turned sallow

kurals.translit: Avardhandhaar Ennum Thakaiyaal Ivardhandhen / Menimel Oorum Pasappu
kurals.pope: 'He gave': this sickly hue thus proudly speaks, Then climbs, and all my frame its chariot makes
kurals.drew: Sallowness, as if proud of having been caused by him, would now ride on my person

kurals.translit: Saayalum Naanum Avarkontaar Kaimmaaraa / Noyum Pasalaiyum Thandhu
kurals.pope: Of comeliness and shame he me bereft, While pain and sickly hue, in recompense, he left
kurals.drew: He has taken (away) my beauty and modesty, and given me instead disease and sallowness

kurals.translit: Ulluvan Manyaan Uraippadhu Avardhiramaal / Kallam Piravo Pasappu
kurals.pope: I meditate his words, his worth is theme of all I say, This sickly hue is false that would my trust betray
kurals.drew: I think (of him); and what I speak about is but his excellence; still is there sallowness; and this is deceitful

kurals.translit: Uvakkaanem Kaadhalar Selvaar Ivakkaanen / Meni Pasappoor Vadhu
kurals.pope: My lover there went forth to roam; This pallor of my frame usurps his place at home
kurals.drew: Just as my lover departed then, did not sallowness spread here on my person ?

kurals.translit: Vilakkatram Paarkkum Irulepol Konkan / Muyakkatram Paarkkum Pasappu
kurals.pope: As darkness waits till lamp expires, to fill the place, This pallor waits till I enjoy no more my lord's embrace
kurals.drew: Just as darkness waits for the failing light; so does sallowness wait for the laxity of my husband's intercourse

kurals.translit: Pullik Kitandhen Putaipeyarndhen Avvalavil / Allikkol Vatre Pasappu
kurals.pope: I lay in his embrace, I turned unwittingly; Forthwith this hue, as you might grasp it, came on me
kurals.drew: I who was in close embrace just turned aside and the moment I did so, sallowness came on me like something to be seized on

kurals.translit: Pasandhaal Ivalenpadhu Allaal Ivalaith / Thurandhaar Avarenpaar Il
kurals.pope: On me, because I pine, they cast a slur; But no one says, 'He first deserted her.'
kurals.drew: Besides those who say "she has turned sallow" there are none who say "he has forsaken her"

kurals.translit: Pasakkaman Pattaangen Meni Nayappiththaar / Nannilaiyar Aavar Enin
kurals.pope: Well let my frame, as now, be sicklied o'er with pain, If he who won my heart's consent, in good estate remain
kurals.drew: If he is clear of guilt who has conciliated me (to his departure) let my body suffer its due and turn sallow

kurals.translit: Pasappenap Perperudhal Nandre Nayappiththaar / Nalkaamai Thootraar Enin
kurals.pope: 'Tis well, though men deride me for my sickly hue of pain; If they from calling him unkind, who won my love, refrain
kurals.drew: It would be good to be said of me that I have turned sallow, if friends do not reproach with unkindness him who pleased me (then)

kurals.translit: Thaamveezhvaar Thamveezhap Petravar Petraare / Kaamaththuk Kaazhil Kani
kurals.pope: The bliss to be beloved by those they love who gains, Of love the stoneless, luscious fruit obtains
kurals.drew: The women who are beloved by those whom they love, have they have not got the stone-less fruit of sexual delight ?

kurals.translit: Vaazhvaarkku Vaanam Payandhatraal Veezhvaarkku / Veezhvaar Ala� Kkum Ali
kurals.pope: As heaven on living men showers blessings from above, Is tender grace by lovers shown to those they love
kurals.drew: The bestowal of love by the beloved on those who love them is like the rain raining (at the proper season) on those who live by it

kurals.translit: Veezhunar Veezhap Patuvaarkku Amaiyume / Vaazhunam Ennum Serukku
kurals.pope: Who love and are beloved to them aloneBelongs the boast, 'We've made life's very joys our own.'
kurals.drew: The pride that says "we shall live" suits only those who are loved by their beloved (husbands)

kurals.translit: Veezhap Patuvaar Kezheeiyilar Thaamveezhvaar / Veezhap Pataaar Enin
kurals.pope: Those well-beloved will luckless prove, Unless beloved by those they love
kurals.drew: Even those who are esteemed (by other women) are devoid of excellence, if they are not loved by their beloved

kurals.translit: Naamkaadhal Kontaar Namakkevan Seypavo / Thaamkaadhal Kollaak Katai
kurals.pope: From him I love to me what gain can be, Unless, as I love him, he loveth me
kurals.drew: He who is beloved by me, what will he do to me, if I am not beloved by him ?

kurals.translit: Orudhalaiyaan Innaadhu Kaamamkaap Pola / Irudhalai Yaanum Inidhu
kurals.pope: Love on one side is bad; like balanced loadBy porter borne, love on both sides is good
kurals.drew: Lust, like the weight of the KAVADI, pains if it lies in one end only but pleases if it is in both

kurals.translit: Paruvaralum Paidhalum Kaanaankol Kaaman / Oruvarkan Nindrozhuku Vaan
kurals.pope: While Kaman rushes straight at me alone, Is all my pain and wasting grief unknown
kurals.drew: Would not cupid who abides and contends in one party (only) witness the pain and sorrow (in that party)?

kurals.translit: Veezhvaarin Insol Peraaadhu Ulakaththu / Vaazhvaarin Vankanaar Il
kurals.pope: Who hear from lover's lips no pleasant word from day to day, Yet in the world live out their life,- no braver souls than they
